55/// Whether record/replay verification hashes syscall output buffers, and
56/// therefore whether its log comparison can see buffer CONTENT at all.
57///
58/// ONE CONSTANT BECAUSE TWO INDEPENDENT SWITCHES HAD TO AGREE AND SILENTLY DID
59/// NOT MATTER. Record/replay carried this decision twice: `metadata.rs`'s
60/// `record_or_replay_config` decided whether the recorder EMITS the hash, and
61/// `record_start.rs`'s `ComparisonOptions` decided whether the comparator READS
62/// it. Both were hard-coded `false`, neither was reachable from the command
63/// line, and nothing related them. Setting either alone achieves nothing: hash
64/// without compare is dead weight, compare without hash finds nothing. Naming
65/// the decision once makes the pair impossible to desynchronize, and makes
66/// changing it a one-line edit in a place a reader can find.
67pub const RECORD_REPLAY_HASHES_IO_BUFFERS: bool = true;
68
69/// Whether record/replay virtualizes time. FALSE, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS WHY
70/// A GREEN RECORD/REPLAY VERDICT IS NOT A DETERMINISM RESULT.
71///
72/// Named for the same reason as [`RECORD_REPLAY_HASHES_IO_BUFFERS`] directly
73/// above: the decision was about to be carried twice. `metadata.rs`'s
74/// `record_or_replay_config` sets the config the recorder and replayer run
75/// under, and `record_start.rs`'s `ComparisonOptions` now discloses that setting
76/// in the verdict. If those two disagreed, the report would describe a time
77/// policy the run did not use — which is precisely the class of defect the
78/// disclosure exists to close, reintroduced one layer up.
79///
80/// `hermit run --verify` reads its value from the live `det_config` instead,
81/// because `--no-virtualize-time` makes it a genuine runtime choice there. Only
82/// the record/replay path is a fixed decision, so only it gets a constant.
83pub const RECORD_REPLAY_VIRTUALIZES_TIME: bool = false;

85/// Exit status for a completed comparison that found a divergence.
86///
87/// This is the conventional `diff` result: zero means equal and one means
88/// different. The verification JSON distinguishes it from a guest that exits
89/// one of its own accord.
90pub const HERMIT_VERIFICATION_DIVERGENCE_EXIT: i32 = 1;
91
92/// Exit status for a failure of HERMIT ITSELF, as distinct from the guest's.
93///
94/// ⚠️ EVERY CLI ERROR USED TO BE `Exited(1)`, WHICH IS THE SINGLE MOST COMMON
95/// GUEST FAILURE CODE. A tracer panic and a guest that exited 1 of its own
96/// accord were therefore INDISTINGUISHABLE from `$?` alone — and every harness,
97/// gate and script on this project decides pass/fail from exactly that value.
98/// The information was not missing, only discarded: reverie's container reports
99/// the child's real status as a typed `ExitStatus`, and hermit collapsed it to
100/// prose and then to `1`.
101///
102/// WHY THIS DOES NOT BREAK THE "hermit's exit IS the guest's exit" CONTRACT.
103/// That contract describes the case where the guest RAN AND EXITED, and it is
104/// untouched: a guest status still flows through `raise_or_exit` unchanged, and
105/// only the `Err` arm — where there is NO guest exit code, because hermit failed
106/// before or instead of producing one — uses this value. The contract did not
107/// cover that case; it does now.
108///
109/// WHY 125. It is the established convention for "the wrapper tool itself
110/// failed" — GNU `env`, `chroot` and `timeout` all reserve 125 for exactly this,
111/// leaving 126/127 for exec-level problems. It is not a value hermit emits
112/// anywhere else.
113///
114/// ⚠️ THIS REDUCES A COLLISION, IT DOES NOT REMOVE ONE. A guest is free to exit
115/// 125 deliberately, and every value in 0..=255 is a legal guest status, so no
116/// code can be reserved outright. What it removes is the GUARANTEED collision
117/// with the most common failure code. For an unambiguous signal, read the
118/// `HERMIT_TASK_PANIC` marker on stderr or the verification JSON; this makes the
119/// cheap check — `$?` — stop actively lying.
120///
121/// ⚠️ IT LIVES IN THE LIBRARY, NOT IN `main.rs`, AND THAT PLACEMENT IS THE FIX
122/// FOR HOW IT WENT STALE. It was a private `const` inside the binary, so
123/// `tests/cli.rs` — the only thing that asserts on it — could not name it and
124/// wrote the number out by hand instead. When hermit#2558 moved the value from
125/// `1` to `125`, the definition moved and the sixteen copies did not: eight cli
126/// tests went red on main and stayed red, each failing an assertion about the
127/// exit code rather than about the behaviour it exists to check. Same shape as
128/// [`RECORD_REPLAY_HASHES_IO_BUFFERS`] above — a decision carried in two places
129/// that had to agree and had no way to. Exported here, the tests move with it.
130///
131/// ⚠️ DO NOT FLIP EVERY `Some(1)` YOU FIND. `tests/stress_suite.rs`
132/// asserts `Some(1)` as THE GUEST'S OWN SIGNAL, not as a stale copy of this
133/// constant: there `Some(1) => GuestOutcome::Exposed`, and
134/// `status.code() == Some(1)` IS the `exposes_bug` predicate. It is
135/// pattern-identical to the tests that DID go stale, and it is the OPPOSITE
136/// case -- the assertion is CORRECT and must not move with this constant.
137///
138/// ⚠️ ITS FAILURE MODE IS SILENT SUCCESS. Changing it to 125 would not
139/// turn the stress suite red; it would make `exposes_bug` NEVER FIRE, so the
140/// suite would report no bug exposed forever and pass while blind. A red is
141/// recoverable; a green that cannot fail is not.
142///
143/// REVIEWER RULE: a change to `tests/stress_suite.rs` inside an exit-code head
144/// SHOULD BE REFUSED ON SIGHT AND QUESTIONED.
145pub const HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE_EXIT: i32 = 125;
146
147/// A deadline hermit itself was asked to enforce expired: **124**.
148///
149/// The status the container init exits with when a hermit-owned bound ends the
150/// run -- `run --timeout`'s SIGALRM fallback here, and `record --record-timeout`'s
151/// handler in `record_start.rs`, which has always used this value. 124 is the
152/// established code for "a deadline fired" across GNU `timeout`, `safehermit`'s
153/// wall bound and both hermit spellings, so this names an existing convention
154/// rather than claiming a new number.
155///
156/// ⚠️ IT MUST BE READ AT THE CONTAINER BOUNDARY OR IT IS SILENTLY REWRITTEN TO
157/// 125. Found only by forcing the fallback to fire, 2026-08-26: the init exited
158/// 124, `classify_container_result` had no arm for it, and it fell through to
159/// `ContainerChildExit` -- so the run reported `exit 125` and
160/// `class=container-child-exit`, "the child died with a status it did not
161/// pick", for a deadline hermit chose to enforce. Identical in shape to the
162/// refusal that arrives as 122 and needs its own arm for the same reason.
163pub const HERMIT_DEADLINE_EXIT: i32 = 124;
164
165/// Hermit's own log output exceeded `--max-log-bytes`: **123**.
166///
167/// The status hermit exits with when the byte budget on its tracing output
168/// (stderr, or `--log-file`) is exhausted and it deliberately tears the run
169/// down. 123 was already reserved below for "a LOG BYTE CAP fired" on behalf of
170/// dev-hermit's `bin/safehermit`; this is the same event enforced one layer
171/// lower, exactly as 124 is shared by hermit's `--timeout` and safehermit's wall
172/// deadline. It is not 125 because the cap working is not hermit breaking, and
173/// not 122 because no fail-closed determinism policy was involved: the remedy
174/// is "lower the log level or raise the cap", not "change the program".
175///
176/// Like 124, it must be read at the container boundary
177/// (`classify_container_result`) or it is rewritten to 125.
178pub const HERMIT_LOG_CAP_EXIT: i32 = 123;
179
180/// The guest program could not be found at all: **127**.
181///
182/// Exported for the same reason as [`HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE_EXIT`] and with the
183/// same history one step behind it. `GuestProgramFault::exit_code` wrote `127`
184/// and `126` as bare literals, and `tests/cli.rs` had no way to name either, so
185/// a test meaning "not found" and a test meaning "hermit refused" were asserted
186/// with the same helper and the same number until the values diverged.
187///
188/// ⚠️ THIS IS NOT A SUBDIVISION OF HERMIT'S OWN FAILURE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
189/// DISTINCTION. 125 says *hermit* broke; 127 and 126 say *the guest program* was
190/// unusable and hermit correctly declined to start it. A caller that cannot tell
191/// those apart cannot tell "fix my tooling" from "fix my command line".
192pub const GUEST_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND_EXIT: i32 = 127;
193
194/// The guest program exists but cannot be executed as given: **126**.
195///
196/// See [`GUEST_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND_EXIT`]. 127/126 are the GNU `env`/`chroot`/
197/// `timeout` convention that 125 itself came from, so the three sit in one
198/// scheme rather than being three unrelated numbers.
199pub const GUEST_PROGRAM_NOT_EXECUTABLE_EXIT: i32 = 126;
200
201// ⚠️ THE VALUES THEMSELVES ARE PINNED, NOT ONLY THEIR NAMES.
202//
203// Naming a constant makes every consumer agree with the definition; it does not
204// make the definition right. Once `tests/cli.rs` asserts `Some(THE_CONSTANT)`
205// everywhere, the whole suite is self-consistent and completely unanchored -- a
206// one-character edit here would move all sixteen assertions with it and nothing
207// would fail. That is the exact shape of the defect this scheme exists to close,
208// displaced one level up, and it is why these are compile-time assertions rather
209// than a comment: a deliberate edit "would be noticed" is the argument that
210// already failed once, when hermit#2558 moved 1 -> 125 and sixteen copies went
211// stale.
212//
213// WHY EACH VALUE AND NOT ANOTHER. GNU `env`, `chroot` and `timeout` reserve 125
214// for "the wrapper itself failed", 127 for "command not found" and 126 for
215// "found but not executable". Borrowing the whole scheme rather than one number
216// is what keeps the three answers distinguishable from each other.
217//
218// ⚠️ THE EXIT-CODE ALLOCATION FOR THE `hermit` BINARY. ONE TABLE, HERE.
219//
220// Five separate exit-code defects were found in one evening and every one of
221// them came from a value being chosen, copied or rewritten somewhere that could
222// not see the others. This is the single place the space is allocated; anything
223// that emits or rewrites a hermit exit status is a consumer OF this table and
224// must not invent its own reading of it.
225//
226//   0          success.
227//   1          HERMIT_VERIFICATION_DIVERGENCE_EXIT, matching `diff`; also a
228//              legal guest status. Read the verification JSON to distinguish.
229//   2 ..= 121  THE GUEST'S OWN STATUS, passed through untouched. (The range
230//              stops at 121 because 122 is reserved below; a guest may still
231//              CHOOSE any value, see the caveat at the end.)
232//   122        HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT -- hermit REFUSED the run under a
233//              fail-closed policy. Hermit WORKED; the run was stopped on
234//              purpose and the reason was printed. Distinct from 125 because
235//              "hermit refused" and "hermit broke" demand opposite responses:
236//              read the refusal and change your program or flags, versus file a
237//              bug. Defined in `detcore-model` because `detcore` emits it and
238//              this crate recognises it, and that is the only crate both
239//              depend on.
240//   123        HERMIT_LOG_CAP_EXIT -- a LOG BYTE CAP fired. Hermit's own
241//              `--max-log-bytes` budget on its tracing output, and the value
242//              reserved for dev-hermit's `bin/safehermit` log-cap kill (which,
243//              as of 2026-09-26, still exits 125 -- see the 125 note below).
244//              Hermit's spelling prints `HERMIT_LOG_CAP class=log-cap`.
245//   124        DO NOT USE. GNU `timeout`'s deadline, and dev-hermit's
246//              `bin/safehermit` WALL DEADLINE kill. `tests/cli.rs` asserts
247//              `assert_ne!(code, Some(124))` on the awk-mincore probe.
248//   125        HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE_EXIT -- hermit itself failed, no guest
249//              ran. NOT YET THE SOLE MEANING through dev-hermit's
250//              `bin/safehermit`: that wrapper has exited 125 for its
251//              log-byte-cap kill since it was created on 2026-08-20 and still
252//              did on 2026-10-05, so a run through it produces one number for
253//              two faults with opposite remedies (see "125 ⚠️ NOT FREE" below).
254//              An earlier version of this table said safehermit had already
255//              moved off 125; it never did. The intended fix is that SAFEHERMIT
256//              MOVES -- to the 123 reserved for it above -- NOT HERMIT, because
257//              that wrapper is the only layer that knows which happened (it
258//              relays hermit's status otherwise) and because 125/126/127 is one
259//              GNU scheme that cannot be broken up. Tracked as
260//              `hermit_s_125_collides`.
261//   126        GUEST_PROGRAM_NOT_EXECUTABLE_EXIT.
262//   127        GUEST_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND_EXIT -- the ABSOLUTE-PATH form. The
263//              bare-name-on-guest-PATH form currently exits 125 instead, which
264//              is an inconsistency tracked as `hermit_reports_a_missing`, not a
265//              second meaning for 127.
266//   128 + N    killed by signal N (shell convention). Hermit does not emit these
267//              deliberately; a wrapper reporting a signal death must use them
268//              rather than borrow a code that already means something.
269//
270// ⚠️ NO CODE IS EXCLUSIVELY HERMIT'S. Every value in 0..=255 is a legal guest
271// status, so a guest may return 125 or 127 of its own accord and this table
272// cannot stop it. The table removes GUARANTEED collisions, not possible ones.
273// The only unambiguous discriminator is the `HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE` marker on
274// stderr, present exactly when hermit itself failed. Any consumer deciding on
275// `$?` alone is guessing, and should say so.
276//
277// ⚠️ THE SAME ARGUMENT APPLIES TO 124, AND MORE SHARPLY, BECAUSE FIVE
278// MECHANISMS PRODUCE IT. `hermit run --timeout`, its unwind fallback, `hermit
279// record --record-timeout`, the `timeout(1)` wrapped around a manifest cell, and
280// `safehermit`'s wall deadline all exit 124, and GNU `timeout` uses it for the
281// same event. They demand different responses -- a slow guest, a wedged
282// teardown inside hermit, a cell bound set too low, a run that escaped every
283// inner bound -- so `$?` cannot route the reader to any of them.
284//
285// The discriminator is again the marker on stderr, and it is a CONTRACT rather
286// than a diagnostic nicety: `class=run-timeout` for hermit's own bound (which
287// also states the bound in seconds), `HERMIT_RUN_TIMEOUT_FALLBACK` for the
288// unwind failing to complete, `safehermit: bound.wall=` for the cgroup reap.
289// EXIT 124 WITH NO MARKER AT ALL MEANS NO INNER BOUND FIRED -- something outside
290// hermit killed the run -- which is a configuration error and not a slow guest.
291// The full picture, including which rung bounds which quantity and the
292// strict-inequality invariant between them, is docs/TIMEOUT_LADDER.md.
293//
294// ⚠️ DO NOT CLAMP INTO THIS RANGE. `scripts/hermit-code-coverage.rs` used
295// `clamp(1, 125)` and so rewrote 127 and 126 into 125 -- turning "your program is
296// missing" into "hermit broke" and pointing the reader at the wrong project.
297// Truncating a status does not lose information here, it MANUFACTURES a false
298// attribution, because the ceiling is itself a meaning.
299//
300// ⚠️ WHAT EACH VALUE MUST NOT COLLIDE WITH -- AND 125 ALREADY DOES.
301//
302//   0    success. Never a failure code; see the nonzero pin below.
303//   1    the commonest guest exit status. Sharing it is the collision
304//        hermit#2558 introduced 125 to escape, so 125 must never drift back.
305//   124  GNU `timeout`'s "deadline fired", and dev-hermit's `bin/safehermit`
306//        uses it for its WALL DEADLINE kill. `tests/cli.rs` asserts
307//        `assert_ne!(code, Some(124))` on the awk-mincore probe for that reason.
308//   126  hermit's own GUEST_PROGRAM_NOT_EXECUTABLE_EXIT.
309//   127  hermit's own GUEST_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND_EXIT -- already in use for the
310//        ABSOLUTE-PATH form of a missing guest program. Note the bare-name form
311//        resolved against the guest PATH exits 125 instead, which is an
312//        inconsistency filed separately, not a licence to reuse 127.
313//
314//   125  ⚠️ NOT FREE. dev-hermit's `bin/safehermit` exits 125 to mean "the LOG
315//        BYTE CAP fired: safehermit killed the run through its cgroup"
316//        (`demos/lib/demo_common.py`'s SAFEHERMIT_EXIT_REASON). Any hermit run
317//        launched through that wrapper -- which is how the demos and the repeat
318//        harness run it -- can therefore produce 125 for two unrelated reasons:
319//        hermit refused, or the wrapper killed it for log volume. They demand
320//        opposite responses (fix the invocation vs raise the cap), and `$?`
321//        cannot tell them apart. This is a LIVE ambiguity, not a hypothetical:
322//        demo 5 has been observed reporting `exited with status 125` when the
323//        cap fired. It is recorded here rather than resolved because changing
324//        either value is a cross-repository decision.
325//
326//        The discriminator meanwhile is the same one that separates hermit's 125
327//        from a guest's own 125: the `HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE` marker on stderr,
328//        present only when hermit itself failed. safehermit writes its verdict
329//        to its `--sh-report` file instead. Read one of those, never the number
330//        alone.
331//
332// ⚠️ 0 IS THE DANGEROUS DRIFT, NOT 126 OR 127. Every one of these is asserted as
333// `assert_eq!(code, Some(CONST))`. At 0 those assertions would stop demanding a
334// FAILURE and start demanding a SUCCESS, and would still pass -- sixteen tests
335// silently inverted. `tests/cli.rs` also asserts `!status.success()` beside the
336// code for that reason; this pin is the second of the two locks.
337const _: () = assert!(
338    HERMIT_VERIFICATION_DIVERGENCE_EXIT == 1,
339    "1 is the established diff-style result for a completed comparison that diverged"
340);
341const _: () = assert!(
342    HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE_EXIT == 125,
343    "125 is the GNU wrapper-failed convention; 1 is the commonest guest status and 0 is success"
344);
345const _: () = assert!(
346    GUEST_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND_EXIT == 127,
347    "127 is the GNU command-not-found convention and must stay distinct from 125 and 126"
348);
349const _: () = assert!(
350    GUEST_PROGRAM_NOT_EXECUTABLE_EXIT == 126,
351    "126 is the GNU found-but-not-executable convention and must stay distinct from 125 and 127"
352);
353const _: () = assert!(
354    HERMIT_LOG_CAP_EXIT == 123,
355    "123 is Hermit's log-cap code, reserved for bin/safehermit's log-cap kill as well; see the allocation table"
356);
357const _: () = assert!(
358    HERMIT_LOG_CAP_EXIT != 0
359        && HERMIT_VERIFICATION_DIVERGENCE_EXIT != 0
360        && HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE_EXIT != 0
361        && GUEST_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND_EXIT != 0
362        && GUEST_PROGRAM_NOT_EXECUTABLE_EXIT != 0,
363    "a failure code of 0 would invert every assert_eq!(code, Some(CONST)) into demanding success"
364);

466enum KvmStdinReservation {
467    Open(fs::File),
468    Closed,
469}
470
471static KVM_STDIN_RESERVATION: Mutex<Option<KvmStdinReservation>> = Mutex::new(None);
472
473/// Saves stdin captured before Rust's process startup can reuse a closed fd 0.
474pub fn reserve_kvm_stdin(stdin: Option<fs::File>) -> io::Result<()> {
475    let mut reservation = KVM_STDIN_RESERVATION
476        .lock()
477        .map_err(|_| io::Error::other("KVM stdin reservation lock is poisoned"))?;
478    if reservation.is_some() {
479        return Err(io::Error::new(
480            io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists,
481            "KVM stdin is already reserved",
482        ));
483    }
484    *reservation = Some(match stdin {
485        Some(file) => KvmStdinReservation::Open(file),
486        None => KvmStdinReservation::Closed,
487    });
488    Ok(())
489}

491fn duplicate_current_stdin() -> io::Result<Option<fs::File>> {
492    // SAFETY: F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC duplicates fd 0 without taking ownership of it.
493    let duplicate = unsafe { libc::fcntl(libc::STDIN_FILENO, libc::F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC, 3) };
494    if duplicate >= 0 {
495        // SAFETY: F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC returned a new owned descriptor.
496        return Ok(Some(unsafe { fs::File::from_raw_fd(duplicate) }));
497    }
498    let error = io::Error::last_os_error();
499    if error.raw_os_error() == Some(libc::EBADF) {
500        Ok(None)
501    } else {
502        Err(error)
503    }
504}

506fn ensure_kvm_stdin_reserved() -> io::Result<()> {
507    let mut reservation = KVM_STDIN_RESERVATION
508        .lock()
509        .map_err(|_| io::Error::other("KVM stdin reservation lock is poisoned"))?;
510    if reservation.is_none() {
511        *reservation = Some(match duplicate_current_stdin()? {
512            Some(file) => KvmStdinReservation::Open(file),
513            None => KvmStdinReservation::Closed,
514        });
515    }
516    Ok(())
517}
518
519fn reserved_kvm_stdin() -> Result<Option<fs::File>, Error> {
520    ensure_kvm_stdin_reserved()?;
521    let reservation = KVM_STDIN_RESERVATION
522        .lock()
523        .map_err(|_| io::Error::other("KVM stdin reservation lock is poisoned"))?;
524    match reservation.as_ref() {
525        Some(KvmStdinReservation::Open(file)) => Ok(Some(file.try_clone()?)),
526        Some(KvmStdinReservation::Closed) => Ok(None),
527        None => unreachable!("stdin reservation was initialized above"),
528    }
529}

531/// A replayable snapshot of the guest's stdin for the output-capturing backends.
532///
533/// `hermit run --verify` executes the guest twice and compares the two runs. The
534/// output-capturing backends historically fed the guest `Stdio::null()`, so any
535/// data piped into hermit (`echo prog | hermit run --strict --verify -- ...`)
536/// was silently dropped. Both runs then saw identical *empty* input and hermit
537/// reported a false "deterministic" success even though the guest never received
538/// its input. `Seekable` holds a read-only, rewindable file so both runs receive
539/// the exact same bytes without being able to modify the caller's input; `None`
540/// means stdin should be `/dev/null` (nothing to replay, or a terminal that
541/// cannot be replayed identically to two runs).
542enum StdinSnapshot {
543    Seekable(fs::File),
544    None,
545}
546
547static OUTPUT_STDIN_SNAPSHOT: Mutex<Option<StdinSnapshot>> = Mutex::new(None);
548
549/// Records a rewindable snapshot of the process stdin so the output-capturing
550/// backends can replay identical input to each run of `hermit run --verify`.
551///
552/// `stdin` is the descriptor captured before Rust startup could reuse a closed
553/// fd 0 (see the binary's `startup_stdin`). A regular-file redirect is reopened
554/// read-only; a pipe/fifo/socket is drained once into a seekable temporary file
555/// and that file is reopened read-only. A terminal (or absent stdin) is treated
556/// as `/dev/null` because a live terminal cannot be replayed identically to two
557/// runs.
558pub fn reserve_output_stdin_snapshot(stdin: Option<fs::File>) -> io::Result<()> {
559    let snapshot = match stdin {
560        None => StdinSnapshot::None,
561        Some(mut file) => {
562            // SAFETY: as_raw_fd borrows the descriptor without taking ownership.
563            let is_tty = unsafe { libc::isatty(file.as_raw_fd()) } == 1;
564            if is_tty {
565                StdinSnapshot::None
566            } else {
567                let replay = if file.stream_position().is_ok() {
568                    // Already seekable (e.g. `< file`): retain it below through
569                    // a read-only descriptor with an independent file offset.
570                    file
571                } else {
572                    // Non-seekable (pipe/fifo/socket): buffer once into a
573                    // seekable temporary file so both --verify runs receive
574                    // identical input.
575                    //
576                    // NAME THE WAIT BEFORE ENTERING IT. This `io::copy` reads to
577                    // EOF, so a stdin that never reaches EOF -- an inherited socket,
578                    // a fifo whose writer stays open -- blocks here FOREVER, before
579                    // the guest has started. Measured: the process wedges with ZERO
580                    // bytes on stdout and stderr and is only cleared by killing it,
581                    // which is indistinguishable from a slow run. That
582                    // indistinguishability is the whole harm; an unbounded wait that
583                    // says what it is waiting for is merely slow, and a reader can
584                    // act on it.
585                    //
586                    // Deliberately UNCONDITIONAL rather than emitted after a delay:
587                    // a message that appears only once N seconds have passed makes
588                    // hermit's own stderr depend on timing, and this project does
589                    // not accept timing-dependent output. Deliberately NOT a
590                    // deadline either -- a 12s slow producer is legitimate and
591                    // delivers, and nothing can separate "slow" from "never" except
592                    // by waiting. This changes no control flow: every input that
593                    // worked before still works, byte for byte, on stdout.
594                    const BUFFERING_NOTE: &str = "hermit: --verify is buffering stdin from a non-seekable stream so both \
595                         runs receive identical input. If this appears to hang, stdin has not \
596                         reached end-of-file; pass `< /dev/null` when the guest needs no input.";
597                    if nonwaiting_write::diagnostics_must_not_wait() {
598                        // Under --max-log-bytes, termination must not depend
599                        // on this write; see `nonwaiting_write`.
600                        nonwaiting_write::write_without_waiting(
601                            libc::STDERR_FILENO,
602                            format!("{BUFFERING_NOTE}\n").as_bytes(),
603                        );
604                    } else {
605                        eprintln!("{BUFFERING_NOTE}");
606                    }
607                    let mut buffered = tempfile::tempfile()?;
608                    io::copy(&mut file, &mut buffered)?;
609                    buffered.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0))?;
610                    buffered
611                };
612
613                // A duplicate would keep the original access mode. Reopen the
614                // reserved descriptor read-only so neither verification run
615                // can modify the caller's stdin or the next run's input.
616                let replay_path = format!("/proc/self/fd/{}", replay.as_raw_fd());
617                StdinSnapshot::Seekable(fs::File::open(replay_path)?)
618            }
619        }
620    };
621    let mut reservation = OUTPUT_STDIN_SNAPSHOT
622        .lock()
623        .map_err(|_| io::Error::other("output stdin snapshot lock is poisoned"))?;
624    if reservation.is_some() {
625        return Err(io::Error::new(
626            io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists,
627            "output stdin snapshot is already reserved",
628        ));
629    }
630    *reservation = Some(snapshot);
631    Ok(())
632}
633
634/// Returns a rewound descriptor for the reserved stdin snapshot, if any.
635///
636/// Each call rewinds the snapshot and hands back a fresh descriptor, so
637/// repeated `--verify` runs read identical input from the start. Returns `None`
638/// when no snapshot was reserved or the reserved stdin is a terminal/absent
639/// (nothing to replay). Runs are sequential (each executes in its own forked
640/// container child), so resetting the shared open file description's offset here
641/// is safe.
642fn output_backend_stdin_reservation() -> Result<(bool, Option<fs::File>), Error> {
643    let mut reservation = OUTPUT_STDIN_SNAPSHOT
644        .lock()
645        .map_err(|_| io::Error::other("output stdin snapshot lock is poisoned"))?;
646    match reservation.as_mut() {
647        Some(StdinSnapshot::Seekable(file)) => {
648            file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0))?;
649            Ok((true, Some(file.try_clone()?)))
650        }
651        Some(StdinSnapshot::None) => Ok((true, None)),
652        None => Ok((false, None)),
653    }
654}
655
656fn output_backend_stdin_file() -> Result<Option<fs::File>, Error> {
657    Ok(output_backend_stdin_reservation()?.1)
658}
659
660/// Returns the stdin to hand a guest run in an output-capturing backend.
661///
662/// When [`reserve_output_stdin_snapshot`] has stored a replayable snapshot the
663/// file is rewound and a fresh descriptor handed to the guest, so each
664/// `--verify` run reads identical input. Otherwise (no snapshot reserved, or a
665/// terminal/absent stdin) the guest gets `/dev/null`, matching the previous
666/// behavior for callers that do not reserve a snapshot.
667pub fn output_backend_stdin() -> Result<Stdio, Error> {
668    match output_backend_stdin_file()? {
669        Some(file) => Ok(Stdio::from(file)),
670        None => Ok(Stdio::null()),
671    }
672}

684#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
685enum CapabilityProbe {
686    Namespaces,
687    Ptrace,
688    Seccomp,
689}
690
691fn run_capability_probe(probe: CapabilityProbe) -> Result<bool, Error> {
692    // SAFETY: The child calls only async-signal-safe syscalls and exits immediately.
693    let pid = unsafe { libc::fork() };
694    if pid == -1 {
695        return Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error()).context("Failed to fork capability probe");
696    }
697    if pid == 0 {
698        let supported = match probe {
699            CapabilityProbe::Namespaces => unsafe {
700                libc::unshare(libc::CLONE_NEWUSER | libc::CLONE_NEWPID) == 0
701            },
702            CapabilityProbe::Ptrace => {
703                // SAFETY: PTRACE_TRACEME ignores the pid and address arguments.
704                unsafe {
705                    libc::ptrace(
706                        libc::PTRACE_TRACEME,
707                        0,
708                        std::ptr::null_mut::<libc::c_void>(),
709                        std::ptr::null_mut::<libc::c_void>(),
710                    ) != -1
711                }
712            }
713            CapabilityProbe::Seccomp => {
714                let mut filter = libc::sock_filter {
715                    code: 0x06, // BPF_RET | BPF_K
716                    jt: 0,
717                    jf: 0,
718                    k: 0x7fff0000, // SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW
719                };
720                let program = libc::sock_fprog {
721                    len: 1,
722                    filter: &mut filter,
723                };
724                // SAFETY: The filter is an allow-all program with a valid one-element lifetime.
725                unsafe {
726                    libc::prctl(libc::PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, 1, 0, 0, 0) == 0
727                        && libc::syscall(
728                            libc::SYS_seccomp,
729                            1, // SECCOMP_SET_MODE_FILTER
730                            0,
731                            &program,
732                        ) == 0
733                }
734            }
735        };
736        // SAFETY: Avoid running Rust destructors after fork.
737        unsafe { libc::_exit(i32::from(!supported)) }
738    }
739
740    let mut status = 0;
741    loop {
742        // SAFETY: pid is the child created above and status points to valid storage.
743        let result = unsafe { libc::waitpid(pid, &mut status, 0) };
744        if result == pid {
745            return Ok(libc::WIFEXITED(status) && libc::WEXITSTATUS(status) == 0);
746        }
747        if result == -1 {
748            let error = std::io::Error::last_os_error();
749            if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::Interrupted {
750                continue;
751            }
752            return Err(error).context("Failed to wait for capability probe");
753        }
754    }
755}
756
757/// Whether a run creates Hermit's user and PID namespaces. A `--no-namespace`
758/// run starts the guest as a plain child and never calls `unshare`, so the
759/// namespace probe says nothing about whether it can run
760/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4515>).
761#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
762pub enum NamespaceUse {
763    /// The run unshares its user and PID namespaces (the default).
764    Creates,
765    /// The run creates no namespace (`--no-namespace`).
766    None,
767}
768
769/// Check the host mechanisms needed by a retained exec-stop launcher or a
770/// ptrace run, without assuming which runtime artifact the launcher uses.
771pub fn validate_tracing_environment(namespaces: NamespaceUse) -> Result<(), Error> {
772    check_tracing_environment(namespaces, run_capability_probe)
773}
774
775/// Refuses a ptrace run that `probe` says this environment cannot host: the
776/// namespace probe for a run that creates namespaces, then the ptrace and
777/// seccomp probes for every run, which a `--no-namespace` run needs too.
778fn check_tracing_environment(
779    namespaces: NamespaceUse,
780    mut probe: impl FnMut(CapabilityProbe) -> Result<bool, Error>,
781) -> Result<(), Error> {
782    if namespaces == NamespaceUse::Creates && !probe(CapabilityProbe::Namespaces)? {
783        anyhow::bail!(
784            "Hermit cannot create its required user and PID namespaces: \
785             unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWPID) was denied. Allow unprivileged user namespaces \
786             and the unshare syscall in the host/container policy."
787        );
788    }
789    if !probe(CapabilityProbe::Ptrace)? {
790        anyhow::bail!(
791            "Hermit cannot use ptrace in this environment: a child PTRACE_TRACEME probe was \
792             denied. Allow same-UID parent-child ptrace in the container seccomp and host \
793             Yama/LSM policy; CAP_SYS_PTRACE is normally not required. Use --namespace-only for \
794             a sandbox smoke test without ptrace (it intercepts only kill, through a seccomp \
795             filter)."
796        );
797    }
798    if !probe(CapabilityProbe::Seccomp)? {
799        anyhow::bail!(
800            "Hermit cannot install its tracee seccomp filter: \
801             seccomp(SECCOMP_SET_MODE_FILTER) was denied. Allow seccomp and \
802             prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS) in the container policy. --namespace-only also \
803             installs a seccomp filter (on kill), so it cannot run here either."
804        );
805    }
806    Ok(())
807}

855// AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
856// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#688): Review LiteInst runtime discovery.
857/// Checks that `path` is an x86-64 shared object that exports every name in
858/// `required` and registers `initializer_name` in its constructor array, so
859/// that preloading it runs that initializer. `label` names the library in every
860/// error message. Returns the canonical path.
861/// Detcore requires its protected root and sole local RELATIVE registration;
862/// this is minimal discovery, separate from complete artifact qualification.
863fn validate_preload_constructor_library(
864    path: &Path,
865    label: &str,
866    required: &[&str],
867    initializer_name: &str,
868) -> io::Result<PathBuf> {
869    let bytes = fs::read(path).map_err(|error| {
870        io::Error::new(
871            error.kind(),
872            format!("failed to read {label} {}: {error}", path.display()),
873        )
874    })?;
875    let elf = Elf::parse(&bytes).map_err(|error| {
876        io::Error::new(
877            io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
878            format!("{label} {} is not an ELF DSO: {error}", path.display()),
879        )
880    })?;
881    if elf.header.e_type != header::ET_DYN || elf.header.e_machine != header::EM_X86_64 {
882        return Err(io::Error::new(
883            io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
884            format!("{label} {} is not an x86-64 shared object", path.display()),
885        ));
886    }
887
888    for &name in required {
889        if !elf
890            .dynsyms
891            .iter()
892            .any(|symbol| elf.dynstrtab.get_at(symbol.st_name) == Some(name))
893        {
894            return Err(io::Error::new(
895                io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
896                format!(
897                    "{label} {} is missing required export {name}",
898                    path.display()
899                ),
900            ));
901        }
902    }
903    if initializer_name == liteinst_constructor::ROOT {
904        liteinst_constructor::validate(&bytes, &elf).map_err(|error| {
905            io::Error::new(
906                error.kind(),
907                format!(
908                    "{label} {} has invalid Detcore constructor binding: {error}",
909                    path.display()
910                ),
911            )
912        })?;
913        return path.canonicalize();
914    }
915    let (initializer_index, initializer) = elf
916        .dynsyms
917        .iter()
918        .enumerate()
919        .find(|(_, symbol)| elf.dynstrtab.get_at(symbol.st_name) == Some(initializer_name))
920        .ok_or_else(|| {
921            io::Error::other(format!(
922                "checked {label} initializer {initializer_name} disappeared"
923            ))
924        })?;
925    let init_array = elf
926        .section_headers
927        .iter()
928        .find(|section| section.sh_type == section_header::SHT_INIT_ARRAY)
929        .ok_or_else(|| {
930            io::Error::new(
931                io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
932                format!("{label} {} has no constructor array", path.display()),
933            )
934        })?;
935    let init_start = init_array.sh_addr;
936    let init_end = init_start.saturating_add(init_array.sh_size);
937    let relocated_initializer = elf
938        .dynrelas
939        .iter()
940        .chain(elf.dynrels.iter())
941        .any(|relocation| {
942            (init_start..init_end).contains(&relocation.r_offset)
943                && relocation.r_sym == initializer_index
944        });
945    let init_bytes = usize::try_from(init_array.sh_offset)
946        .ok()
947        .and_then(|start| {
948            usize::try_from(init_array.sh_size)
949                .ok()
950                .and_then(|size| bytes.get(start..start.checked_add(size)?))
951        })
952        .unwrap_or_default();
953    let direct_initializer = init_bytes
954        .as_chunks::<8>()
955        .0
956        .iter()
957        .any(|entry| u64::from_le_bytes(*entry) == initializer.st_value);
958    if !relocated_initializer && !direct_initializer {
959        return Err(io::Error::new(
960            io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
961            format!(
962                "{label} {} does not register {initializer_name} as a preload constructor",
963                path.display()
964            ),
965        ));
966    }
967    path.canonicalize()
968}

970/// Environment variable naming the in-guest Detcore preload
971/// (`libdetcore_liteinst.so`) explicitly.
972pub const LITEINST_TOOL_RUNTIME_ENV: &str = "HERMIT_LITEINST_TOOL_RUNTIME";
973
974// AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
975// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3635): Review in-guest Detcore runtime discovery.
976/// Returns the in-guest Detcore preload: the one [`LITEINST_TOOL_RUNTIME_ENV`]
977/// names; otherwise the packaged `rsrcs/libdetcore_liteinst.so` of the selected
978/// Hermit installation (`hermit-install` stages it, as it stages the DBT and
979/// SaBRe Detcore runtimes, and a standalone installation or published bundle
980/// carries it). A selected installation missing that resource is incomplete
981/// and is refused. When no installation is selected, the development fallback
982/// is the one `cargo build -p detcore-liteinst` built beside the Hermit binary
983/// or in its `deps/` directory.
984///
985/// A runtime built from another tree is refused when it starts: Hermit passes
986/// it [`detcore::config_wire_fingerprint`], which it compares with its own
987/// before decoding anything (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3986>).
988#[doc(hidden)]
989pub fn liteinst_tool_runtime_library_path() -> io::Result<PathBuf> {
990    if let Some(path) = std::env::var_os(LITEINST_TOOL_RUNTIME_ENV) {
991        let path = PathBuf::from(path);
992        if !path.is_file() {
993            return Err(io::Error::new(
994                io::ErrorKind::NotFound,
995                format!("{LITEINST_TOOL_RUNTIME_ENV} does not name a regular file"),
996            ));
997        }
998        return validate_liteinst_tool_runtime_library(&path).map_err(|error| {
999            io::Error::new(
1000                error.kind(),
1001                format!("{LITEINST_TOOL_RUNTIME_ENV} is invalid: {error}"),
1002            )
1003        });
1004    }
1005
1006    if let Some(path) = hermit_resources::resource("libdetcore_liteinst.so")? {
1007        if !path.is_file() {
1008            return Err(io::Error::new(
1009                io::ErrorKind::NotFound,
1010                "selected Hermit installation has no finalized in-guest Detcore runtime; \
1011                 run `make install-deps` to build and stage the qualified LiteInst runtime",
1012            ));
1013        }
1014        return validate_liteinst_tool_runtime_library(&path);
1015    }
1016
1017    let executable = std::env::current_exe()?;
1018    let directory = executable.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
1019        io::Error::new(
1020            io::ErrorKind::NotFound,
1021            "Hermit executable has no parent directory",
1022        )
1023    })?;
1024    if let Some(path) = [
1025        directory.join("libdetcore_liteinst.so"),
1026        directory.join("deps/libdetcore_liteinst.so"),
1027    ]
1028    .into_iter()
1029    .find(|path| path.is_file())
1030    {
1031        return validate_liteinst_tool_runtime_library(&path);
1032    }
1033    Err(io::Error::new(
1034        io::ErrorKind::NotFound,
1035        format!(
1036            "libdetcore_liteinst.so was not built beside {} or staged as an installed resource",
1037            executable.display()
1038        ),
1039    ))
1040}

1043    validate_preload_constructor_library(

1045        "in-guest Detcore runtime",
1046        &["detcore_liteinst_initialize"],
1047        "detcore_liteinst_initialize",
1048    )

1051// AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
1052// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3635): Review the in-guest LiteInst library refusals.
1053/// In-guest LiteInst refused a run before starting its guest, because the

1056/// A type rather than a message, because it crosses the container error
1057/// boundary as [`error::FailureKind::PolicyRefusal`] (exit 122).
1058#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
1059pub struct LiteinstInGuestRefusal {
1060    backend: Backend,
1061    reason: String,

1063
1064impl LiteinstInGuestRefusal {
1065    /// A refusal of a `--backend=liteinst` run.
1066    pub fn new(reason: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
1067        Self::for_backend(Backend::Liteinst, reason)
