1069
1070    /// A refusal of a run of `backend`, one of the in-guest LiteInst backends
1071    /// ([`Backend::is_in_guest_liteinst`]), so the message names the backend
1072    /// the caller selected.
1073    pub fn for_backend(backend: Backend, reason: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
1074        debug_assert!(backend.is_in_guest_liteinst(), "{backend:?}");
1075        Self {
1076            backend,
1077            reason: reason.into(),
1078        }
1079    }
1080}
1081
1082impl std::fmt::Display for LiteinstInGuestRefusal {
1083    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
1084        let runtime = match self.backend {
1085            Backend::InGuestTrap => "in-guest LiteInst, site patching off",
1086            _ => "in-guest LiteInst",
1087        };
1088        write!(
1089            f,
1090            "--backend={} ({runtime}) refuses this run: {}",
1091            self.backend.as_str(),
1092            self.reason
1093        )
1094    }
1095}
1096
1097impl std::error::Error for LiteinstInGuestRefusal {}
1098
1099/// Refuses, before the guest starts, an in-guest LiteInst run that the runtime
1100/// cannot honour or could not monitor.
1101///
1102/// - A maximum timeslice. Reverie's in-guest Tool host has no preemption timer:
1103///   its `set_timer` refuses with `ENOSYS`, and Detcore treats a failed
1104///   `set_timer` as fatal (`.expect("Failed to set timer")`), so the guest
1105///   would panic at its first scheduling point. The CLI refuses
1106///   `--max-timeslice` earlier; this covers library callers.
1107/// - A kernel older than Linux 6.5 ([`in_guest_liteinst_kernel_gap`]).
1108/// - A guest program that would run code before, or without, the runtime's
1109///   constructor ([`in_guest_liteinst_program_gap`]).
1110/// - For `in-guest-trap`, a guest environment that sets
1111///   `REVERIE_LITEINST_SITE_PATCHING` to anything but `0`
1112///   ([`in_guest_trap_site_patching_conflict`]).
1113///
1114/// This runs where the guest is spawned (inside the container for the CLI),
1115/// so it resolves the program in the filesystem the guest sees. It pins the
1116/// resolved program on `command` ([`pin_spawn_program`]), so the launch
1117/// executes the same path this check inspected. For `in-guest-trap` it then
1118/// sets `REVERIE_LITEINST_SITE_PATCHING=0` on `command`
1119/// ([`force_in_guest_site_patching`]).
1120#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1121fn refuse_in_guest_liteinst_run(
1122    command: &mut Command,
1123    config: &DetConfig,
1124    backend: Backend,
1125) -> Result<(), Error> {
1126    let reason = if let Some(conflict) = in_guest_trap_site_patching_conflict(command, backend) {
1127        Some(conflict)
1128    } else if config.max_timeslice.is_some() {
1129        Some(
1130            "it cannot deliver Detcore's preemption timer yet (the in-guest Tool host refuses \
1131             set_timer with ENOSYS), so the run would fail at its first timeslice; pass \
1132             --max-timeslice=disabled"
1133                .to_owned(),
1134        )
1135    } else if let Some(gap) = in_guest_liteinst_kernel_gap(&running_kernel_release()) {
1136        Some(gap)
1137    } else {
1138        in_guest_liteinst_program_gap(command)?
1139    };
1140    match reason {
1141        Some(reason) => Err(Error::new(LiteinstInGuestRefusal::for_backend(
1142            backend, reason,
1143        ))),
1144        None => {
1145            force_in_guest_site_patching(command, backend);
1146            Ok(())
1147        }
1148    }
1149}
1150
1151/// The value of `REVERIE_LITEINST_SITE_PATCHING` (`reverie_liteinst::SITE_PATCHING_ENV`)
1152/// that the guest sees under `backend`, when Hermit decides it: `0` for
1153/// `in-guest-trap`, which exists to run with no syscall site patched, and
1154/// `None` for `liteinst`, which leaves the variable to the guest environment
1155/// (unset means patching on).
1156pub fn forced_site_patching_value(backend: Backend) -> Option<&'static str> {
1157    match backend {
1158        Backend::InGuestTrap => Some("0"),
1159        _ => None,
1160    }
1161}
1162
1163/// Whether LiteInst's SIGTRAP guard router can be installed in the in-guest
1164/// Tool images of a default-route run of `backend` configured by `config`:
1165/// on an in-guest backend, unless every image runs with syscall site
1166/// patching off (`config.in_guest_site_patching_off`, set for
1167/// `--backend=in-guest-trap`).
1168///
1169/// At the pinned Reverie, the shared Tool host's preparation
1170/// (`LiteinstPatchHost::prepare_patcher`, reverie-liteinst `src/runtime.rs`)
1171/// installs the router only when the site-patching setting its runtime
1172/// captured is on: the router takes the breakpoints LiteInst plants while it
1173/// publishes a patched site, and with patching off it publishes none
1174/// (A5 step 3c slice 0c). Every in-guest-trap image checks that its runtime
1175/// captured patching off and refuses to run otherwise
1176/// (`detcore::in_guest_site_patching`), so no image of such a run executes
1177/// guest code with the router. On `--backend=liteinst` Hermit leaves the setting to the guest's
1178/// environment, so an image can run with patching off and no router; the
1179/// answer is then `true` all the same, which reserves SIGTRAP where it is
1180/// not needed: a refusal Linux would not make, never a missed one. The
1181/// loader route (Reverie's private-image installer) keeps the router
1182/// whatever its setting, and never calls this (D26).
1183pub const fn in_guest_guard_router_installed(config: &DetConfig, backend: Backend) -> bool {
1184    backend.is_in_guest_liteinst() && !config.in_guest_site_patching_off
1185}
1186
1187/// The signals the in-guest runtime keeps for itself in a run of `backend`
1188/// configured by `config` (`detcore::Config::in_guest_reserved_signals`), bit
1189/// `n - 1` for signal `n`, for Hermit's default in-guest route: SIGSYS, its
1190/// syscall trap, always; SIGSEGV while it subscribes instructions, when it
1191/// installs its instruction-fault handler for SIGSEGV; and SIGTRAP while
1192/// LiteInst's guard router can be installed, which is site patching on
1193/// ([`in_guest_guard_router_installed`]): never on `in-guest-trap`, whose
1194/// `config.in_guest_site_patching_off` the caller has set first.
1195/// The subscription is Detcore's own decision from the same configuration
1196/// (`Tool::subscriptions`), which each in-guest Tool image reads to choose
1197/// its instruction subscriptions (reverie-inguest `tool_install.rs:191-195`).
1198/// Empty (0) for every other backend. The in-guest loader route never calls
1199/// this, so its set stays empty: today's behaviour there (D13(a)).
1200pub fn in_guest_reserved_signals(config: &DetConfig, backend: Backend) -> u64 {
1201    if !backend.is_in_guest_liteinst() {
1202        return 0;
1203    }
1204    let bit = |signal: libc::c_int| 1_u64 << (signal - 1);
1205    let subscription = <Detcore as reverie::Tool>::subscriptions(config);
1206    let mut reserved = bit(libc::SIGSYS);
1207    if subscription.has_rdtsc() || subscription.has_cpuid() {
1208        reserved |= bit(libc::SIGSEGV);
1209    }
1210    if in_guest_guard_router_installed(config, backend) {
1211        reserved |= bit(libc::SIGTRAP);
1212    }
1213    reserved
1214}
1215
1216/// Whether Detcore refuses host-timed signal producers in a run of `backend`
1217/// (`detcore::Config::in_guest_refuses_host_timed_producers`, A5 step 3c
1218/// slice 0b): on Hermit's default in-guest route, for both in-guest backends,
1219/// and never on another backend. The in-guest loader route never calls this,
1220/// so the setting stays off there: today's behaviour (D13(a), D26).
1221pub const fn in_guest_refuses_host_timed_producers(backend: Backend) -> bool {
1222    backend.is_in_guest_liteinst()
1223}
1224
1225/// Whether this process, which runs the scheduler of the in-guest run it
1226/// launches, owns the guests' PID namespace (A5 step 3c.1, D51 and D52): it
1227/// is PID 1 of its PID namespace, and every guest it launches descends from
1228/// it, so is a member of that namespace. When a PID namespace's init exits,
1229/// the kernel sends SIGKILL to every task with a PID in the namespace and
1230/// waits for them (`zap_pid_ns_processes`, kernel/pid_namespace.c v6.12
1231/// lines 170-222). That covers a guest in a nested PID namespace too: a task
1232/// has a PID in its own namespace and in every ancestor (`alloc_pid`,
1233/// kernel/pid.c v6.12 lines 194-253), and `setns` enters only the caller's
1234/// namespace or a descendant of it (`pidns_install`, kernel/pid_namespace.c
1235/// lines 390-397), so no guest leaves the namespace. So a refusal that exits
1236/// the scheduler (`GlobalRequest::StoppingRefusal`) then leaves no guest
1237/// process running; the in-guest delivery gate requires that
1238/// ([`in_guest_signal_delivery_gate`]).
1239///
1240/// A fact read from the process, never a setting a caller supplies, so the
1241/// run-wide-exit claim cannot be forged: `hermit run`'s container launch,
1242/// which runs the scheduler as the init of the namespace it creates, owns it,
1243/// and `hermit run --no-namespace` does not (its scheduler is a plain
1244/// child). A library caller owns it exactly when it really is that init.
1245pub fn scheduler_owns_guest_pid_namespace() -> bool {
1246    // SAFETY: getpid has no preconditions.
1247    unsafe { libc::getpid() == 1 }
1248}
1249
1250/// Whether the pinned in-guest runtime delivers the guest's signals itself
1251/// under the gate (its runtime mask, final-read loop and predicted deaths,
1252/// A5 step 3c.1e). Not yet: until the flip (3c.1f), the gate stays off on
1253/// every route, whatever [`in_guest_signal_delivery_gate`] answers.
1254#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1255const IN_GUEST_RUNTIME_DELIVERS_SIGNALS: bool = false;
1256
1257/// The in-guest delivery gate (`detcore::Config::in_guest_signal_delivery`,
1258/// D35 of the A5 step 3c design) for a run of `backend` on Hermit's default
1259/// in-guest route, from its final prepared configuration and the launcher's
1260/// PID-namespace ownership: an in-guest backend, site patching off,
1261/// sequentialized threads, no configuration in which the two-phase delivery
1262/// protocol cannot be kept (`detcore::two_phase_refusal`: a timeslice, a
1263/// recorded or replayed schedule, an in-effect pipe hand-off, and the rows no
1264/// in-guest backend reaches), and a scheduler that owns the guest's PID
1265/// namespace (`owns_guest_pid_namespace`, which the launch sites compute
1266/// with [`scheduler_owns_guest_pid_namespace`]). The in-guest loader route
1267/// never asks (D26, D43): its configuration keeps the gate off.
1268pub fn in_guest_signal_delivery_gate(
1269    config: &DetConfig,
1270    backend: Backend,
1271    owns_guest_pid_namespace: bool,
1272) -> bool {
1273    backend.is_in_guest_liteinst()
1274        && config.in_guest_site_patching_off
1275        && config.sequentialize_threads
1276        && detcore::two_phase_refusal(config).is_none()
1277        && owns_guest_pid_namespace
1278}
1279
1280/// `RLIMIT_CPU`'s value as Hermit's log and refusal print it: `unlimited`, or
1281/// a number of seconds.
1282#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1283fn rlimit_seconds(value: libc::rlim_t) -> String {
1284    if value == libc::RLIM_INFINITY {
1285        "unlimited".to_owned()
1286    } else {
1287        format!("{value}s")
1288    }
1289}
1290
1291/// The INFO line for the physical `RLIMIT_CPU` the guest's own check found,
1292/// `old`, just before its program started, and set to unlimited, the value
1293/// Detcore reports (`syscalls/sysinfo.rs`): D25 of A5 step 3c.
1294#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1295fn rlimit_cpu_report_line(old: libc::rlimit) -> String {
1296    if old.rlim_cur == libc::RLIM_INFINITY && old.rlim_max == libc::RLIM_INFINITY {
1297        format!(
1298            "HERMIT_IN_GUEST_RLIMIT_CPU: the guest's physical RLIMIT_CPU was soft {} hard {}, the \
1299             value Detcore reports; the guest starts with it unchanged (A5 step 3c, D25)",
1300            rlimit_seconds(old.rlim_cur),
1301            rlimit_seconds(old.rlim_max),
1302        )
1303    } else {
1304        format!(
1305            "HERMIT_IN_GUEST_RLIMIT_CPU: the guest's physical RLIMIT_CPU was soft {} hard {}; \
1306             Hermit sets it to soft unlimited hard unlimited as the guest starts, the value \
1307             Detcore reports, so the kernel never sends SIGXCPU at a moment host CPU time decides \
1308             (A5 step 3c, D25)",
1309            rlimit_seconds(old.rlim_cur),
1310            rlimit_seconds(old.rlim_max),
1311        )
1312    }
1313}
1314
1315/// Why the guest cannot start with the finite physical `RLIMIT_CPU` its own
1316/// check found, `old`, which it could not raise to unlimited (`errno`; raising
1317/// a hard limit needs `CAP_SYS_RESOURCE` in the initial user namespace,
1318/// `do_prlimit`, which Hermit's container never has). A finite limit would
1319/// make the kernel send SIGXCPU at the soft limit and SIGKILL at the hard
1320/// one, at moments host CPU time decides.
1321#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1322fn rlimit_cpu_refusal(old: libc::rlimit, errno: nix::errno::Errno) -> String {
1323    format!(
1324        "the guest would inherit a finite physical RLIMIT_CPU (soft {}, hard {}), and Hermit \
1325         cannot raise it ({errno}), so the kernel would send SIGXCPU or SIGKILL at a moment host \
1326         CPU time decides; run Hermit with an unlimited hard CPU-time limit \
1327         (A5 step 3c, D25, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4485)",
1328        rlimit_seconds(old.rlim_cur),
1329        rlimit_seconds(old.rlim_max),
1330    )
1331}
1332
1333/// Why descriptor `fd`, which the guest would inherit, cannot be inherited by
1334/// an in-guest guest: it is already a complete host-timed signal producer
1335/// (`state`, D25 of A5 step 3c), holds a lease (`lease`), or has an owner
1336/// without `O_ASYNC` on a file that is not a socket. A directory
1337/// notification (`F_NOTIFY`) sets such an owner and signals it for its
1338/// events, and cannot be read back (there is no `F_GETNOTIFY`, and fdinfo
1339/// does not show dnotify), so any owner fails closed. `None` when it has
1340/// none of these.
1341#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1342fn inherited_producer_refusal(
1343    fd: std::os::fd::RawFd,
1344    state: detcore::host_timed_producers::ProducerState,
1345    lease: bool,
1346) -> Option<String> {
1347    let what = if lease {
1348        "it holds a lease, whose owner Linux sends SIGIO when another process opens the file"
1349    } else if state.is_complete() && state.o_async {
1350        "it has O_ASYNC and an owner, which Linux sends SIGIO when it becomes ready"
1351    } else if state.is_complete() {
1352        "it is a socket with an owner, which Linux sends SIGURG when out-of-band data arrives"
1353    } else if state.owner {
1354        "it has an owner, which a directory notification (F_NOTIFY) on it would make Linux send \
1355         SIGIO for the directory's changes, and Hermit cannot tell whether one is set"
1356    } else {
1357        return None;
1358    };
1359    Some(format!(
1360        "the guest would inherit descriptor {fd}, which is already a signal producer: {what}, at \
1361         a moment host timing decides; close it, or clear its owner and O_ASYNC, before running \
1362         Hermit (A5 step 3c, D25, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4485)"
1363    ))
1364}
1365
1366/// Why descriptor `fd`, which the guest would inherit and whose state cannot
1367/// be read (`errno`), is not inherited unchecked.
1368#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1369fn unreadable_descriptor_refusal(fd: std::os::fd::RawFd, errno: nix::errno::Errno) -> String {
1370    format!(
1371        "the guest would inherit descriptor {fd}, whose signal owner and flags cannot be read \
1372         ({errno}), so Hermit cannot tell whether it is a signal producer \
1373         (A5 step 3c, D25, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4485)"
1374    )
1375}
1376
1377/// Why the guest's descriptor table could not be listed (`errno`), so is not
1378/// inherited unchecked.
1379#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1380fn unlisted_descriptors_refusal(errno: nix::errno::Errno) -> String {
1381    format!(
1382        "the guest's descriptor table could not be listed from /proc/self/fd ({errno}), so \
1383         Hermit cannot tell whether a descriptor it would inherit is a signal producer \
1384         (A5 step 3c, D25, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4485)"
1385    )
1386}
1387
1388/// The guest's own check, in its process just before its program starts
1389/// (D25 of A5 step 3c): a `pre_exec` callback Hermit installs after every
1390/// other one that can change what it checks, so after
1391/// the spawner has put the command's configured standard streams in place
1392/// (whatever descriptor each came from, close-on-exec or not) and after every
1393/// callback the caller installed (one of which could clear close-on-exec on a
1394/// descriptor of its own, or change a limit). Hermit's own process cannot see
1395/// that state. The callback
1396/// - lists the whole descriptor table from `/proc/self/fd`, and fails the
1397///   launch, by name, when it cannot ([`audit_inherited_descriptors`]);
1398/// - reads each descriptor without close-on-exec, and fails the launch for a
1399///   complete producer, a lease or any owner, or one it cannot read
1400///   ([`check_inherited_descriptor`]);
1401/// - reads `RLIMIT_CPU` and sets it to unlimited, and fails the launch when it
1402///   cannot.
1403///
1404/// Every outcome is written to a pipe this process reads ([`LaunchReport`]):
1405/// a failure's reason, from which the caller makes the named refusal, or the
1406/// limit the check found, which is logged at INFO at the end of the run, on
1407/// every exit path (`detcore::host_timed_producers::defer_run_end_log`).
1408#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1409struct LaunchAudit {
1410    pipe: std::sync::Arc<LaunchPipe>,
1411}
1412
1413/// The pipe the guest's check reports through, and its report once read.
1414#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1415struct LaunchPipe {
1416    read: std::os::fd::OwnedFd,
1417    _write: std::os::fd::OwnedFd,
1418    report: std::sync::OnceLock<Option<LaunchReport>>,
1419}
1420
1421#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1422impl LaunchPipe {
1423    /// The next report in the pipe, if the check wrote one.
1424    fn read_report(&self) -> Option<LaunchReport> {
1425        let mut bytes = [0u8; LaunchReport::SIZE];
1426        let read = nix::unistd::read(&self.read, &mut bytes).ok()?;
1427        (read == bytes.len()).then(|| LaunchReport::decode(bytes))
1428    }
1429
1430    /// The launch's report, read once.
1431    fn report(&self) -> Option<LaunchReport> {
1432        *self.report.get_or_init(|| self.read_report())
1433    }
1434
1435    /// Logs at INFO the `RLIMIT_CPU` a check that passed found and set to
1436    /// unlimited (D25); nothing for a check that failed or never ran.
1437    fn log_rlimit(&self) {
1438        match self.report() {
1439            Some(report) if report.kind == audit_bits::PASSED => {
1440                tracing::info!("{}", rlimit_cpu_report_line(report.limit()));
1441            }
1442            // A refusal is reported where the launch fails, not here.
1443            Some(_) => {}
1444            None => tracing::warn!(
1445                "HERMIT_IN_GUEST_RLIMIT_CPU: the guest's launch check reported nothing \
1446                 (A5 step 3c, D25)"
1447            ),
1448        }
1449    }
1450}
1451
1452/// The report's kinds and state bits.
1453#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1454mod audit_bits {
1455    /// The check passed; the report carries the limit it found.
1456    pub const PASSED: u8 = 0;
1457    /// A descriptor is a complete producer; the bits say what it holds.
1458    pub const PRODUCER: u8 = 1;
1459    /// A descriptor's state cannot be read; the errno says why.
1460    pub const UNREADABLE: u8 = 2;
1461    /// The descriptor table cannot be listed; the errno says why.
1462    pub const UNLISTED: u8 = 3;
1463    /// `RLIMIT_CPU` cannot be raised; the report carries the limit and errno.
1464    pub const RLIMIT_CPU: u8 = 4;
1465
1466    pub const O_ASYNC: u8 = 1;
1467    pub const OWNER: u8 = 2;
1468    pub const SOCKET: u8 = 4;
1469    pub const LEASE: u8 = 8;
1470}
1471
1472/// What the guest's check reports ([`LaunchAudit`]): its kind
1473/// ([`audit_bits`]), state bits, errno, descriptor, and the `RLIMIT_CPU` it
1474/// found, in 24 native-endian bytes.
1475#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1476#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
1477struct LaunchReport {
1478    kind: u8,
1479    bits: u8,
1480    errno: u8,
1481    fd: libc::c_int,
1482    rlimit: (libc::rlim_t, libc::rlim_t),
1483}
1484
1485#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1486impl LaunchReport {
1487    const SIZE: usize = 24;
1488
1489    fn encode(self) -> [u8; Self::SIZE] {
1490        let mut bytes = [0u8; Self::SIZE];
1491        bytes[0] = self.kind;
1492        bytes[1] = self.bits;
1493        bytes[2] = self.errno;
1494        bytes[4..8].copy_from_slice(&self.fd.to_ne_bytes());
1495        bytes[8..16].copy_from_slice(&self.rlimit.0.to_ne_bytes());
1496        bytes[16..24].copy_from_slice(&self.rlimit.1.to_ne_bytes());
1497        bytes
1498    }
1499
1500    fn decode(bytes: [u8; Self::SIZE]) -> Self {
1501        let word = |range: std::ops::Range<usize>| {
1502            libc::rlim_t::from_ne_bytes(bytes[range].try_into().expect("eight bytes"))
1503        };
1504        Self {
1505            kind: bytes[0],
1506            bits: bytes[1],
1507            errno: bytes[2],
1508            fd: libc::c_int::from_ne_bytes(bytes[4..8].try_into().expect("four bytes")),
1509            rlimit: (word(8..16), word(16..24)),
1510        }
1511    }
1512
1513    fn errno(self) -> nix::errno::Errno {
1514        nix::errno::Errno::from_raw(self.errno.into())
1515    }
1516
1517    fn limit(self) -> libc::rlimit {
1518        libc::rlimit {
1519            rlim_cur: self.rlimit.0,
1520            rlim_max: self.rlimit.1,
1521        }
1522    }
1523
1524    /// The refusal this report names, `None` for a check that passed.
1525    fn refusal(self) -> Option<String> {
1526        match self.kind {
1527            audit_bits::PRODUCER => {
1528                let state = detcore::host_timed_producers::ProducerState {
1529                    o_async: self.bits & audit_bits::O_ASYNC != 0,
1530                    owner: self.bits & audit_bits::OWNER != 0,
1531                    socket: self.bits & audit_bits::SOCKET != 0,
1532                };
1533                inherited_producer_refusal(self.fd, state, self.bits & audit_bits::LEASE != 0)
1534            }
1535            audit_bits::UNREADABLE => Some(unreadable_descriptor_refusal(self.fd, self.errno())),
1536            audit_bits::UNLISTED => Some(unlisted_descriptors_refusal(self.errno())),
1537            audit_bits::RLIMIT_CPU => Some(rlimit_cpu_refusal(self.limit(), self.errno())),
1538            _ => None,
1539        }
1540    }
1541}
1542
1543/// The report for descriptor `fd` of the calling process if the guest must
1544/// not inherit it, `None` if it may: one with close-on-exec, which it does
1545/// not inherit, or `report`, the audit's own pipe, are skipped.
1546/// Async-signal-safe: fcntl and fstat only, no allocation.
1547#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1548fn check_inherited_descriptor(fd: libc::c_int, report: libc::c_int) -> Option<LaunchReport> {
1549    // SAFETY: F_GETFD reads a descriptor flag and writes no memory.
1550    let fd_flags = unsafe { libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_GETFD) };
1551    if fd == report || fd_flags < 0 || fd_flags & libc::FD_CLOEXEC != 0 {
1552        return None;
1553    }
1554    let (kind, bits, errno) = match detcore::host_timed_producers::host_descriptor_state(fd) {
1555        Ok((state, lease)) if lease || state.owner || state.is_complete() => (
1556            audit_bits::PRODUCER,
1557            (if state.o_async {
1558                audit_bits::O_ASYNC
1559            } else {
1560                0
1561            }) | (if state.owner { audit_bits::OWNER } else { 0 })
1562                | (if state.socket { audit_bits::SOCKET } else { 0 })
1563                | (if lease { audit_bits::LEASE } else { 0 }),
1564            0,
1565        ),
1566        Ok(_) | Err(nix::errno::Errno::EBADF) => return None,
1567        Err(errno) => (audit_bits::UNREADABLE, 0, errno as i32 as u8),
1568    };
1569    Some(LaunchReport {
1570        kind,
1571        bits,
1572        errno,
1573        fd,
1574        rlimit: (0, 0),
1575    })
1576}
1577
1578/// The first report [`check_inherited_descriptor`] makes for the calling
1579/// process's descriptors, every one `/proc/self/fd` lists, read with
1580/// `getdents64` into a stack buffer. Where that directory cannot be listed
1581/// (its open or a read fails, for example with EMFILE after a caller lowered
1582/// `RLIMIT_NOFILE` below its open descriptors), the report says so
1583/// (`UNLISTED`, with the errno): no number-range scan stands in for it, since
1584/// no bound below the largest open descriptor is sure. Async-signal-safe:
1585/// open, getdents64, close, fcntl and fstat only, no allocation.
1586#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1587fn audit_inherited_descriptors(report: libc::c_int) -> Option<LaunchReport> {
1588    let unlisted = || LaunchReport {
1589        kind: audit_bits::UNLISTED,
1590        bits: 0,
1591        errno: nix::errno::Errno::last_raw() as u8,
1592        fd: -1,
1593        rlimit: (0, 0),
1594    };
1595    // SAFETY: plain system calls on this process's descriptor table, writing
1596    // only into the local buffer.
1597    unsafe {
1598        let directory = libc::open(
1599            c"/proc/self/fd".as_ptr(),
1600            libc::O_RDONLY | libc::O_DIRECTORY | libc::O_CLOEXEC,
1601        );
1602        if directory < 0 {
1603            return Some(unlisted());
1604        }
1605        let mut buffer = [0u8; 4096];
1606        loop {
1607            let read = libc::syscall(
1608                libc::SYS_getdents64,
1609                directory,
1610                buffer.as_mut_ptr(),
1611                buffer.len(),
1612            );
1613            if read < 0 {
1614                let failed = unlisted();
1615                libc::close(directory);
1616                return Some(failed);
1617            }
1618            if read == 0 {
1619                break;
1620            }
1621            let mut offset = 0;
1622            while offset + 19 < read as usize {
1623                // struct linux_dirent64: d_ino (8), d_off (8), d_reclen (2),
1624                // d_type (1), d_name.
1625                let length =
1626                    u16::from_ne_bytes([buffer[offset + 16], buffer[offset + 17]]) as usize;
1627                if length == 0 {
1628                    break;
1629                }
1630                let mut fd: libc::c_int = 0;
1631                let mut digits = 0;
1632                for &byte in &buffer[offset + 19..offset + length] {
1633                    if !byte.is_ascii_digit() {
1634                        break;
1635                    }
1636                    fd = fd
1637                        .saturating_mul(10)
1638                        .saturating_add((byte - b'0') as libc::c_int);
1639                    digits += 1;
1640                }
1641                if digits > 0
1642                    && fd != directory
1643                    && let Some(found) = check_inherited_descriptor(fd, report)
1644                {
1645                    libc::close(directory);
1646                    return Some(found);
1647                }
1648                offset += length;
1649            }
1650        }
1651        libc::close(directory);
1652        None
1653    }
1654}
1655
1656/// The guest's whole check ([`LaunchAudit`]), in its process: the descriptor
1657/// table, then `RLIMIT_CPU`, which it sets to unlimited. Every outcome is a
1658/// report; a failing one fails the launch. Async-signal-safe.
1659#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1660fn launch_check(report: libc::c_int) -> LaunchReport {
1661    if let Some(failed) = audit_inherited_descriptors(report) {
1662        return failed;
1663    }
1664    // SAFETY: getrlimit and setrlimit read and write only the local limits.
1665    unsafe {
1666        let mut old: libc::rlimit = std::mem::zeroed();
1667        if libc::getrlimit(libc::RLIMIT_CPU, &mut old) != 0 {
1668            return LaunchReport {
1669                kind: audit_bits::RLIMIT_CPU,
1670                bits: 0,
1671                errno: nix::errno::Errno::last_raw() as u8,
1672                fd: -1,
1673                rlimit: (0, 0),
1674            };
1675        }
1676        let mut found = LaunchReport {
1677            kind: audit_bits::PASSED,
1678            bits: 0,
1679            errno: 0,
1680            fd: -1,
1681            rlimit: (old.rlim_cur, old.rlim_max),
1682        };
1683        if old.rlim_cur != libc::RLIM_INFINITY || old.rlim_max != libc::RLIM_INFINITY {
1684            let unlimited = libc::rlimit {
1685                rlim_cur: libc::RLIM_INFINITY,
1686                rlim_max: libc::RLIM_INFINITY,
1687            };
1688            if libc::setrlimit(libc::RLIMIT_CPU, &unlimited) != 0 {
1689                found.kind = audit_bits::RLIMIT_CPU;
1690                found.errno = nix::errno::Errno::last_raw() as u8;
1691            }
1692        }
1693        found
1694    }
1695}
1696
1697#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1698impl LaunchAudit {
1699    /// Installs the check on `command`, after every `pre_exec` callback
1700    /// already installed on it, so a library caller's own run first. It is
1701    /// the last callback that can change what it checks: Reverie's in-guest
1702    /// launcher then adds two of its own (reverie-inguest
1703    /// `src/launcher/mod.rs` at a214eb85): `personality(ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE)`
1704    /// (`:619`, called at `:1048` and `:1092`), and clearing close-on-exec on
1705    /// its own sealed bootstrap memfd (`:1061-1068`, `bootstrap.rs`). Neither
1706    /// touches `RLIMIT_CPU` or creates a signal producer.
1707    /// Also keeps the INFO line of the limit it finds to log at the end of
1708    /// the run, on every exit path (`detcore::host_timed_producers`).
1709    fn install(command: &mut Command) -> Result<Self, Error> {
1710        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
1711        let (read, write) =
1712            nix::unistd::pipe2(nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_CLOEXEC | nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_NONBLOCK)?;
1713        let report = write.as_raw_fd();
1714        // SAFETY: the callback is async-signal-safe (see `launch_check`) and
1715        // allocates nothing.
1716        unsafe {
1717            command.pre_exec(move || {
1718                let found = launch_check(report);
1719                let bytes = found.encode();
1720                libc::write(report, bytes.as_ptr().cast(), bytes.len());
1721                if found.kind == audit_bits::PASSED {
1722                    Ok(())
1723                } else {
1724                    Err(reverie::Errno::EPERM)
1725                }
1726            });
1727        }
1728        let pipe = std::sync::Arc::new(LaunchPipe {
1729            read,
1730            _write: write,
1731            report: std::sync::OnceLock::new(),
1732        });
1733        let logged = pipe.clone();
1734        detcore::host_timed_producers::defer_run_end_log(move || logged.log_rlimit());
1735        Ok(Self { pipe })
1736    }
1737
1738    /// `error`, the launch's, or the named refusal the guest's check reported
1739    /// for `backend`, which is why the launch failed. A check that passed
1740    /// before the backend failed has its limit logged first, as on every
1741    /// other exit path.
1742    fn launch_error(&self, backend: Backend, error: reverie::Error) -> Error {
1743        match self.pipe.report().and_then(LaunchReport::refusal) {
1744            Some(reason) => Error::new(LiteinstInGuestRefusal::for_backend(backend, reason)),
1745            None => {
1746                detcore::host_timed_producers::emit_run_end_log();
1747                Error::from(error)
1748            }
1749        }
1750    }
1751}
1752
1753/// Before an in-guest launch on the default route, installs the guest's own
1754/// check of what it inherits (D25 of A5 step 3c, design section 16.32,
1755/// [`LaunchAudit`]): it refuses the launch by name for an inherited
1756/// descriptor that is already a host-timed signal producer, a descriptor
1757/// table it cannot list, or a finite `RLIMIT_CPU` it cannot raise, and
1758/// otherwise sets the guest's physical `RLIMIT_CPU` to unlimited as the guest
1759/// starts. The caller turns a failed launch's report into the refusal; a
1760/// passed one's limit is logged at INFO at the end of the run, on every exit
1761/// path. `None` for a backend
1762/// that does not refuse host-timed producers.
1763#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1764fn neutralize_inherited_signal_producers(
1765    command: &mut Command,
1766    backend: Backend,
1767) -> Result<Option<LaunchAudit>, Error> {
1768    if !in_guest_refuses_host_timed_producers(backend) {
1769        return Ok(None);
1770    }
1771    Ok(Some(LaunchAudit::install(command)?))
1772}
1773
1774/// Why an `in-guest-trap` run cannot start with the guest environment of
1775/// `command`: the environment (explicit or inherited) sets
1776/// `REVERIE_LITEINST_SITE_PATCHING` to a value other than the one Hermit
1777/// forces. Hermit refuses such a run rather than overriding the value
1778/// silently, because the caller asked for two contradictory things: site
1779/// patching (or a value the runtime would reject) and the backend that exists
1780/// to run without it. A value equal to the forced one is accepted. `None`
1781/// for every other backend.
1782#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1783fn in_guest_trap_site_patching_conflict(command: &Command, backend: Backend) -> Option<String> {
1784    let forced = forced_site_patching_value(backend)?;
1785    let name = reverie_liteinst::SITE_PATCHING_ENV;
1786    let value = command.get_env(name)?;
1787    (*value != *std::ffi::OsStr::new(forced)).then(|| {
1788        format!(
1789            "the guest environment sets {name}={}, but --backend={} runs with syscall site \
1790             patching off and sets {name}={forced} itself; drop the variable, or select \
1791             --backend=liteinst to patch syscall sites",
1792            value.to_string_lossy(),
1793            backend.as_str()
1794        )
1795    })
1796}
1797
1798/// Sets the guest's `REVERIE_LITEINST_SITE_PATCHING` to the value Hermit
1799/// forces for `backend` ([`forced_site_patching_value`]), leaving the
1800/// environment unchanged for a backend that forces none. The guest's
1801/// descendants inherit it unless the guest changes its own environment; a
1802/// descendant that turns patching back on shows in the run's dispatch record
1803/// as patched sites.
1804#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1805fn force_in_guest_site_patching(command: &mut Command, backend: Backend) {
1806    if let Some(value) = forced_site_patching_value(backend) {
1807        command.env(reverie_liteinst::SITE_PATCHING_ENV, value);
1808    }
1809}
1810
1811/// Whether every in-guest Tool image of a `backend` run checks that its runtime
1812/// captured site patching off and statistics on
1813/// (`detcore::Config::in_guest_site_patching_off`): true for `in-guest-trap`.
1814#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1815fn in_guest_site_patching_off(backend: Backend) -> bool {
1816    forced_site_patching_value(backend) == Some("0")
1817}
1818
1819/// Whether an in-guest run of `backend` collects LiteInst's statistics: when
1820/// something reads them ([`backend_stats::request`]), and on every
1821/// `in-guest-trap` run, whose result is checked against them
1822/// ([`in_guest_trap_patching_evidence`]).
1823#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1824fn in_guest_stats_request(
1825    backend: Backend,
1826    summary_json: &Option<PathBuf>,
1827) -> reverie::BackendStatsRequest {
1828    if backend == Backend::InGuestTrap {
1829        reverie::BackendStatsRequest::ENABLED
1830    } else {
1831        backend_stats::request(summary_json)
1832    }
1833}
1834
1835/// Reports a refusal the fail-closed policy decided inside the guest as
1836/// Hermit's own refusal. The in-guest Detcore that refuses tells the
1837/// coordinator why (`GlobalState::policy_refusal`) and exits with
1838/// `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT`, which ends only the guest process. Without
1839/// this the run ended with that as the guest's exit status and no reason, or
1840/// with whatever postcondition the early exit then tripped (an unregistered
1841/// exit, or in-guest-trap's missing statistics). Checked before those.
1842#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1843fn refuse_in_guest_policy(backend: Backend, refusal: Option<String>) -> Result<(), Error> {
1844    match refusal {
1845        Some(reason) => Err(Error::new(LiteinstInGuestRefusal::for_backend(
1846            backend,
1847            format!("{reason}; --backend=ptrace runs this program"),
1848        ))),
1849        None => Ok(()),
1850    }
1851}
1852
1853/// Why a finished `in-guest-trap` run did not show that it ran with syscall
1854/// site patching off, from its dispatch record and the number of guest
1855/// processes that reported LiteInst statistics: a site the runtime patched or
1856/// considered patching (with patching off it considers none), no record, or no
1857/// process report at all, in which case the record's zeros are not
1858/// measurements (a run whose guests collected no statistics still yields an
1859/// empty record). `None` for every other backend.
1860///
1861/// This is the coordinator's postcondition. Each Tool image also refuses to
1862/// run its program when the runtime started it with patching on
1863/// (`detcore::in_guest_site_patching`), which holds for every image whatever
1864/// it reports; this one sees only the images that report, because an image
1865/// reports its statistics when it exits (`exit` or `exit_group`), so an image
1866/// that `execve`s, or is killed by a signal, sends none, and the coordinator
1867/// cannot tell that from a report that was suppressed. It refuses a run in
1868/// which no process reported; it does not detect a run in which some did and
1869/// others did not. Each image's own check covers that: an image whose runtime
1870/// is not collecting statistics refuses to run its program.
1871#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1872fn in_guest_trap_patching_evidence(
1873    backend: Backend,
1874    dispatch: Option<&reverie::DispatchStats>,
1875    process_reports: u64,
1876) -> Option<String> {
1877    if backend != Backend::InGuestTrap {
1878        return None;
1879    }
1880    let Some(record) = dispatch else {
1881        return Some(
1882            "the run produced no LiteInst dispatch record, so it cannot show that no syscall \
1883             site was patched"
1884                .to_owned(),
1885        );
1886    };
1887    if process_reports == 0 {
1888        return Some(
1889            "no guest process reported LiteInst statistics, so the run's zero patched sites \
1890             are not a measurement and it cannot show that no syscall site was patched"
1891                .to_owned(),
1892        );
1893    }
1894    let shown =
1895        |count: Option<u64>| count.map_or_else(|| "unmeasured".to_owned(), |n| n.to_string());
1896    (record.sites.patched != Some(0) || record.sites.candidates != Some(0)).then(|| {
1897        format!(
1898            "its guests' LiteInst statistics report {} patched and {} candidate syscall sites, \
1899             so it did not run with syscall site patching off and its result is not an \
1900             in-guest-trap result",
1901            shown(record.sites.patched),
1902            shown(record.sites.candidates)
1903        )
1904    })
1905}
1906
1907/// Refuses a finished `in-guest-trap` run whose dispatch record shows site
1908/// patching ([`in_guest_trap_patching_evidence`]): records a determinism loss,
1909/// so verification refuses to compare it, and returns the typed in-guest
1910/// refusal (exit 122).
1911#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1912fn refuse_in_guest_trap_patching(backend: Backend, evidence: Option<String>) -> Result<(), Error> {
1913    match evidence {
1914        Some(reason) => {
1915            detcore::detlog::record_determinism_loss(&reason);
1916            Err(Error::new(LiteinstInGuestRefusal::for_backend(
1917                backend, reason,
1918            )))
1919        }
1920        None => Ok(()),
1921    }
1922}
1923
1924/// Use the existing actual subscriber-derived forwarding policy for the
1925/// shared native path. Call inside the same verification tracing scope.
1926#[cfg(any(
1927    feature = "native-exec",
1928    all(feature = "exec-stop-launcher", feature = "liteinst")
1929))]
1930#[doc(hidden)]
1931pub fn in_guest_detlog_forward_policy_for_native() -> detcore::detlog::ForwardPolicy {
1932    in_guest_detlog_forward_policy()
1933}
1934
1935/// Report the shared native trap runtime through the existing statistics
1936/// comparator and require a real guest report with site patching disabled.
1937/// This never converts a patching-off execution into LiteInst evidence.
1938#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1939#[doc(hidden)]
1940pub fn native_trap_dispatch_stats(
1941    source: &reverie_liteinst::LiteinstBackendStatsSource,
1942) -> Result<Option<reverie::DispatchStats>, Error> {
1943    let backend = Backend::InGuestTrap;
1944    let record = backend_stats::report(backend, reverie::BackendStatsRequest::ENABLED, source);
1945    let evidence = in_guest_trap_patching_evidence(
1946        backend,
1947        record.as_ref(),
1948        source.snapshot().process_reports(),
1949    );
1950    refuse_in_guest_trap_patching(backend, evidence)?;
1951    Ok(record)
1952}
1953
1954/// The oldest kernel in-guest LiteInst runs on, as (major, minor). Linux 6.5
1955/// added `SO_PEERPIDFD`: the coordinator admits each guest process through the
1956/// pidfd of the socket's peer and watches that pidfd for the process's exit
1957/// (`in_guest_exits`). On an older kernel every admission would fail.
1958#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1959const IN_GUEST_LITEINST_KERNEL_FLOOR: (u32, u32) = (6, 5);
1960
1961/// The running kernel's release string (`uname -r`), or empty if unreadable.
1962#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1963fn running_kernel_release() -> String {
1964    let mut name: libc::utsname = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
1965    // SAFETY: uname fills the struct it is given.
1966    if unsafe { libc::uname(&mut name) } != 0 {
1967        return String::new();
1968    }
1969    // SAFETY: uname NUL-terminates each field.
1970    unsafe { std::ffi::CStr::from_ptr(name.release.as_ptr()) }
1971        .to_string_lossy()
1972        .into_owned()
1973}
1974
1975/// Why kernel `release` cannot run in-guest LiteInst, or `None` when it is at
1976/// least [`IN_GUEST_LITEINST_KERNEL_FLOOR`]. A release whose version cannot be
1977/// read is refused.
1978#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
1979fn in_guest_liteinst_kernel_gap(release: &str) -> Option<String> {
1980    let mut numbers = release
1981        .split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit())
1982        .map(|part| part.parse::<u32>().ok());
1983    let (floor_major, floor_minor) = IN_GUEST_LITEINST_KERNEL_FLOOR;
1984    match (numbers.next().flatten(), numbers.next().flatten()) {
1985        (Some(major), Some(minor)) if (major, minor) >= IN_GUEST_LITEINST_KERNEL_FLOOR => None,
1986        (Some(_), Some(_)) => Some(format!(
1987            "it needs Linux {floor_major}.{floor_minor} or later (SO_PEERPIDFD, which it uses to \
1988             admit each guest process and observe its exit); this kernel is {release}"
1989        )),
1990        _ => Some(format!(
1991            "it needs Linux {floor_major}.{floor_minor} or later (SO_PEERPIDFD), and the kernel \
1992             release {release:?} does not say which version this is"
1993        )),
1994    }
1995}
1996
1997/// How many `#!` interpreters [`in_guest_liteinst_program_gap`] follows before
1998/// it refuses the program. The kernel has its own small limit (`exec_binprm` in
1999/// `fs/exec.c`); a chain this check stops following is refused, not run, so the
2000/// check fails closed whichever limit is lower.
2001#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
2002const MAX_INTERPRETER_DEPTH: usize = 4;
2003
2004/// Why the guest program would run code before, or without, the in-guest
2005/// runtime, or `None` when it would not.
2006///
2007/// The runtime is an `LD_PRELOAD` library whose constructor installs Detcore.
2008/// The dynamic loader never loads it into a statically linked image or an image
2009/// of another architecture, and ignores `LD_PRELOAD` in secure-execution mode
2010/// (set-user-ID, set-group-ID, or file capabilities). An executable's
2011/// `DT_PREINIT_ARRAY` runs before every library constructor. Each of those
2012/// would run guest code unmonitored, so each is refused. `#!` scripts are
2013/// checked through their interpreter, read as the kernel's script handler
2014/// reads it ([`script::KernelScript`]). A program or interpreter that is not a
2015/// regular file is refused before it is opened: the kernel executes only
2016/// regular files, opening a device can act on it, opening a socket fails, and
2017/// reading a FIFO that has no writer would block the check.
2018///
2019/// Every fact about one file (its type, header, ELF headers, mode bits and
2020/// capabilities) is read through one open descriptor, so they all describe
2021/// the same file. The check is still advisory, not containment: the `execve`
2022/// opens the path again, and a file replaced at that path in between is not
2023/// checked again.
2024///
2025/// Not covered, and recorded on
2026/// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3520>:
2027/// - The loader itself, the C library's initialization, the executable's
2028///   `IFUNC` resolvers and the constructors of the executable's own shared
2029///   libraries all run before the runtime's constructor in every guest.
2030/// - Secure-execution mode that a security module or a parent with differing
2031///   real and effective IDs imposes; only the file's own mode bits and
2032///   capabilities are checked.
2033/// - Whether the `PT_INTERP` loader honours `LD_PRELOAD` at all.
2034/// - A `binfmt_misc` rule, which the kernel consults before its ELF and script
2035///   handlers, and which can hand a file this check accepted to another
2036///   interpreter (for example an emulator).
2037/// - A runtime library the loader fails to load: the loader continues without
2038///   it, and only the launch's check that the guest connected before it exited
2039///   reports the failure, after the guest ran.
2040/// - A `pre_exec` callback on `command` that changes the working directory or
2041///   the root directory: the check resolves paths against the working
2042///   directory `command` is configured with, in Hermit's root, before any
2043///   such callback runs.
2044#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
2045fn in_guest_liteinst_program_gap(command: &mut Command) -> Result<Option<String>, Error> {
2046    use std::io::Read;
2047    use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt;
2048
2049    use script::KernelScript;
2050
2051    let mut path = pin_spawn_program(command)?;
2052    for _ in 0..=MAX_INTERPRETER_DEPTH {
2053        let shown = path.display().to_string();
2054        let not_regular = || {
2055            Ok(Some(format!(
2056                "{shown} is not a regular file, and the kernel executes only regular files"
2057            )))
2058        };
2059        if !fs::metadata(&path)
2060            .with_context(|| format!("cannot read guest program {shown}"))?
2061            .is_file()
2062        {
2063            return not_regular();
2064        }
2065        // The path can change type after the check above. O_NONBLOCK then keeps
2066        // the open of a FIFO that has no writer from blocking, and O_NOCTTY
2067        // keeps a terminal from becoming Hermit's controlling terminal; neither
2068        // changes how a regular file is read. The descriptor's own type is
2069        // checked again below.
2070        let mut file = fs::OpenOptions::new()
2071            .read(true)
2072            .custom_flags(libc::O_NONBLOCK | libc::O_NOCTTY)
2073            .open(&path)
2074            .with_context(|| format!("cannot read guest program {shown}"))?;
2075        if !file
2076            .metadata()
2077            .with_context(|| format!("cannot read guest program {shown}"))?
2078            .is_file()
2079        {
2080            return not_regular();
2081        }
2082        let mut header = Vec::new();
2083        (&file)
2084            .take(256)
2085            .read_to_end(&mut header)
2086            .with_context(|| format!("cannot read guest program {shown}"))?;
2087        match KernelScript::from_buf(&header) {
2088            KernelScript::Interpreter(interpreter) => {
2089                // The kernel opens a relative interpreter against the working
2090                // directory of the process calling execve.
2091                path = match command.get_current_dir() {
2092                    Some(directory) => directory.join(interpreter),
2093                    None => interpreter,
2094                };
2095                continue;
2096            }
2097            KernelScript::Declined => {
2098                return Ok(Some(format!(
2099                    "{shown} starts with #! but the kernel's script handler declines it (it \
2100                     names no interpreter, or the interpreter path fills the first 256 bytes), \
2101                     so the kernel would fail the execve or hand the file to another handler \
2102                     that need not load the runtime"
2103                )));
2104            }
2105            KernelScript::NotScript => {}
2106        }
2107        let Some(startup) = interp::elf_startup(&mut file)
2108            .with_context(|| format!("cannot read the ELF headers of guest program {shown}"))?
2109        else {
2110            return Ok(Some(format!(
2111                "{shown} is neither an ELF executable nor a #! script, so the kernel would hand \
2112                 it to a handler that need not load the runtime"
2113            )));
2114        };
2115        let reason = if !startup.x86_64 {
2116            "is not a 64-bit x86-64 ELF image, so the dynamic loader cannot load the 64-bit \
2117             runtime into it"
2118        } else if !startup.has_interp {
2119            "is statically linked (it has no PT_INTERP), so no dynamic loader runs to load the \
2120             runtime"
2121        } else if is_secure_execution_image(&file, &shown)? {
2122            "is set-user-ID, set-group-ID or has file capabilities, so the kernel runs it in \
2123             secure-execution mode, where the dynamic loader ignores LD_PRELOAD"
2124        } else if startup.has_preinit_array {
2125            "has a DT_PREINIT_ARRAY, whose functions run before the runtime's constructor"
2126        } else {
2127            return Ok(None);
2128        };
2129        return Ok(Some(format!(
2130            "guest program {shown} {reason}, so it would run unmonitored if Hermit launched it"
2131        )));
2132    }
2133    Ok(Some(format!(
2134        "the #! interpreters of guest program {} nest more than {MAX_INTERPRETER_DEPTH} deep",
2135        Path::new(command.get_program()).display()
2136    )))
2137}
2138
2139/// Resolves the program `command` executes with Reverie's
2140/// [`Command::find_program`], the call the in-guest launch makes, and pins the
2141/// result on `command`, keeping `argv[0]`.
2142///
2143/// The result is absolute, so the launch's own `find_program` returns it
2144/// unchanged and the launch executes the same path the check inspected,
2145/// whatever `PATH` or working directory either side would otherwise use. The
2146/// path, not its contents: a file replaced at that path in between is not
2147/// checked again (see [`in_guest_liteinst_program_gap`]). A program the launch
2148/// could not find is an error here, as it would be at launch.
2149#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
2150fn pin_spawn_program(command: &mut Command) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
2151    let arg0 = command.get_arg0().to_owned();
2152    let program = command.find_program().with_context(|| {
2153        format!(
2154            "cannot find guest program {}",
2155            Path::new(command.get_program()).display()
2156        )
2157    })?;
2158    command.program(&program).arg0(arg0);
2159    Ok(program)
2160}
2161
2162/// Whether executing `file` (shown as `shown`) puts the kernel in
2163/// secure-execution mode (`AT_SECURE`): set-user-ID, set-group-ID (with group
2164/// execute, as the kernel requires), or a `security.capability` attribute.
2165#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
2166fn is_secure_execution_image(file: &fs::File, shown: &str) -> Result<bool, Error> {
2167    let mode = file
2168        .metadata()
2169        .with_context(|| format!("cannot stat guest program {shown}"))?
2170        .permissions()
2171        .mode();
2172    if mode & 0o4000 != 0 || mode & 0o2010 == 0o2010 {
2173        return Ok(true);
2174    }
2175    // SAFETY: the descriptor is open for the call, the name is NUL-terminated,
2176    // and a zero-sized query writes no value.
2177    let size = unsafe {
2178        libc::fgetxattr(
2179            file.as_raw_fd(),
2180            c"security.capability".as_ptr(),
2181            std::ptr::null_mut(),
2182            0,
2183        )
2184    };
2185    if size >= 0 {
2186        return Ok(true);
2187    }
2188    match io::Error::last_os_error().raw_os_error() {
2189        Some(libc::ENODATA) | Some(libc::ENOTSUP) => Ok(false),
2190        _ => Err(Error::new(io::Error::last_os_error()).context(format!(
2191            "cannot read the file capabilities of guest program {shown}"
2192        ))),
2193    }
2194}
2195
2196/// Refuses a wall-clock bound on an in-guest LiteInst run. The bound drops the
2197/// run's future, and dropping it neither kills the guest nor stops the
2198/// blocking task that waits for it.
2199#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
2200fn refuse_in_guest_liteinst_timeout(
2201    backend: Backend,
2202    timeout: Option<Duration>,
2203) -> Result<(), Error> {
2204    if backend.is_in_guest_liteinst() && timeout.is_some() {
2205        return Err(Error::new(LiteinstInGuestRefusal::for_backend(
2206            backend,
2207            "a wall-clock timeout has not been qualified for the in-guest runtime, whose run \
2208             future does not kill the guest when it is dropped",
2209        )));
2210    }
2211    Ok(())
2212}
2213
2214#[cfg(not(feature = "liteinst"))]
2215fn refuse_in_guest_liteinst_timeout(
2216    _backend: Backend,
2217    _timeout: Option<Duration>,
2218) -> Result<(), Error> {
2219    Ok(())
2220}

2260/// Process instrumentation backend used to run a Hermit guest.
2261#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, Eq, PartialEq, ValueEnum)]
2262pub enum Backend {
2263    /// Use Reverie's ptrace backend.
2264    #[default]
2265    Ptrace,
2266    /// Use the DynamoRIO backend.
2267    Dbt,
2268    /// Use LiteInst, with Detcore's Tool running inside the guest.
2269    Liteinst,
2270    /// Use in-guest LiteInst with syscall site patching off: the same
2271    /// in-guest Detcore host as `liteinst`, but every trapped syscall reaches
2272    /// the Tool through the seccomp `SIGSYS` fallback and no syscall site is
2273    /// rewritten. Hermit sets `REVERIE_LITEINST_SITE_PATCHING=0` in the
2274    /// guest's environment and refuses a run whose environment asks for any
2275    /// other value.
2276    InGuestTrap,
2277    /// Use the SaBRe static binary rewriting backend.
2278    Sabre,
2279    /// Use the KVM backend.
2280    Kvm,
2281    /// Preprocess the main ELF with e9patch, then use the ptrace runtime.
2282    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-594): Review the CLI-only hybrid backend selection.
2283    E9patch,
2284}
2285
2286/// A requested backend could not start because its required runtime support is absent.
2287///
2288/// Keep this as a typed error until the top-level command records its failure class.
2289/// The human-readable message is for the operator; consumers must use the class line
2290/// emitted by the command rather than matching this prose.
2291#[derive(Debug, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
2292pub struct BackendUnavailable {
2293    backend: Backend,
2294    reason: String,
2295}
2296
2297impl BackendUnavailable {
2298    pub fn new(backend: Backend, reason: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
2299        Self {
2300            backend,
2301            reason: reason.into(),
2302        }
2303    }
2304
2305    pub fn backend(&self) -> Backend {
2306        self.backend
2307    }
2308
2309    pub fn reason(&self) -> &str {
2310        &self.reason
2311    }
2312}
2313
2314impl std::fmt::Display for BackendUnavailable {
2315    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
2316        write!(
2317            formatter,
2318            "backend `{}` is unavailable: {}",
2319            self.backend.as_str(),
2320            self.reason
2321        )
2322    }
2323}
2324
2325impl std::error::Error for BackendUnavailable {}
2326
2327impl Backend {
2328    const ALL: [Self; 7] = [
2329        Self::Ptrace,
2330        Self::Dbt,
2331        Self::Liteinst,
2332        Self::InGuestTrap,
2333        Self::Sabre,
2334        Self::Kvm,
2335        Self::E9patch,
2336    ];
2337
2338    /// Returns the command-line spelling for this backend.
2339    pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
2340        match self {
2341            Self::Ptrace => "ptrace",
2342            Self::Dbt => "dbt",
2343            Self::Liteinst => "liteinst",
2344            Self::InGuestTrap => "in-guest-trap",
2345            Self::Sabre => "sabre",
2346            Self::Kvm => "kvm",
2347            Self::E9patch => "e9patch",
2348        }
2349    }
2350
2351    /// Whether this backend hosts Detcore's Tool inside each guest process
2352    /// through the in-guest LiteInst preload runtime: `liteinst` and
2353    /// `in-guest-trap`, which differ only in whether syscall sites are patched.
2354    /// Every refusal, capability and launch step of in-guest LiteInst applies to
2355    /// both.
2356    pub const fn is_in_guest_liteinst(self) -> bool {
2357        matches!(self, Self::Liteinst | Self::InGuestTrap)
2358    }
2359
2360    /// The name of the backend runtime that executes this backend's guest, as
2361    /// its statistics source names itself (`BackendStatsSnapshot::BACKEND_NAME`).
2362    /// `in-guest-trap` runs the in-guest LiteInst runtime, so its statistics come
2363    /// from that runtime's source, which is named `liteinst`.
2364    pub const fn runtime_name(self) -> &'static str {
2365        match self {
2366            Self::InGuestTrap => Self::Liteinst.as_str(),
2367            other => other.as_str(),
2368        }
2369    }
2370
2371    fn uses_ptrace_pmu_timers(self) -> bool {
2372        match self {
2373            Self::Ptrace | Self::E9patch => true,
2374            // In-guest Detcore has no ptrace tracer to arm the PMU timer from.
2375            Self::Liteinst | Self::InGuestTrap | Self::Dbt | Self::Sabre | Self::Kvm => false,
2376        }
2377    }
2378
2379    /// Returns backends whose Hermit integration prerequisites are met.
2380    ///
2381    /// Some integrations use CLI launch adapters rather than direct
2382    /// [`run_with_backend`] dispatch.
2383    pub fn available() -> impl Iterator<Item = Self> {
2384        Self::ALL
2385            .into_iter()
2386            .filter(|backend| backend.is_available())
2387    }
2388
2389    /// Returns whether this backend's integration prerequisites are met.
2390    pub fn is_available(self) -> bool {
2391        self.unavailable_reason().is_none()
2392    }
2393
2394    /// Returns an actionable error when this backend's prerequisites are not met.
2395    pub fn ensure_available(self) -> Result<(), Error> {
2396        self.ensure_available_for(NamespaceUse::Creates)
2397    }
2398
2399    /// [`Backend::ensure_available`] for a run that creates `namespaces`: a
2400    /// `--no-namespace` ptrace run is not refused where only `unshare` of a
2401    /// user namespace is denied, since it never makes that call; the ptrace
2402    /// and seccomp probes still apply.
2403    pub fn ensure_available_for(self, namespaces: NamespaceUse) -> Result<(), Error> {
2404        if let Some(reason) = self.unavailable_reason_for(namespaces) {
2405            Err(Error::new(BackendUnavailable::new(self, reason)))
2406        } else {
2407            Ok(())
2408        }
2409    }
2410
2411    fn unavailable_reason(self) -> Option<String> {
2412        self.unavailable_reason_for(NamespaceUse::Creates)
2413    }
2414
2415    fn unavailable_reason_for(self, namespaces: NamespaceUse) -> Option<String> {
2416        match self {
2417            Self::Ptrace => validate_tracing_environment(namespaces)
2418                .err()
2419                .map(|error| error.to_string()),
2420            Self::Dbt => dbt_unavailable_reason(),
2421            // The same runtime, so the same prerequisites and the same reason.
2422            Self::Liteinst | Self::InGuestTrap => liteinst_unavailable_reason(),
2423            // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#589): Review SaBRe backend availability reporting.
2424            Self::Sabre => sabre_unavailable_reason(),
2425            Self::Kvm => kvm_device_unavailable_reason(Path::new("/dev/kvm")),
2426            Self::E9patch => e9patch_unavailable_reason(),
2427        }
2428    }
2429}

2431struct SkidOvershootReport {
2432    enabled: bool,
2433}
2434
2435/// The backend failed while running the guest, after Hermit launched it: the
2436/// DBT evidence check, a KVM execution failure, a SaBRe guest that never
2437/// reached Detcore. `run --verify` records it as `run_failed` with
2438/// `backend_failure` instead of leaving the `not_run` stamp.
2439///
2440/// It sits in the chain below the message that names the failure, so the
2441/// first `Error:` line is unchanged; it crosses the container error boundary
2442/// as [`error::FailureKind::BackendRunFailure`].
2443#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
2444pub struct BackendRunFailure;
2445
2446impl std::fmt::Display for BackendRunFailure {
2447    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
2448        f.write_str("the backend failed while running the guest")
2449    }
2450}
2451
2452impl std::error::Error for BackendRunFailure {}
2453
2454/// A ptrace-backed run observed late precise-timer delivery, so Hermit refuses
2455/// to treat the completed execution as deterministic evidence.
2456///
2457/// This is a type rather than a message match because it crosses the container
2458/// error boundary as [`error::FailureKind::PolicyRefusal`].
2459#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
2460pub struct SkidOvershootError {
2461    count: u64,
2462}
2463
2464impl SkidOvershootError {
2465    pub fn new(count: u64) -> Self {
2466        assert!(
2467            count > 0,
2468            "a skid-overshoot refusal requires a positive count"
2469        );
2470        Self { count }
2471    }
2472
2473    pub fn count(&self) -> u64 {
2474        self.count
2475    }
2476}
2477
2478impl std::fmt::Display for SkidOvershootError {
2479    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
2480        write!(
2481            f,
2482            "observed {} {} report(s); refusing the result because precise PMU timer \
2483             delivery passed its target and deterministic execution was not established",
2484            self.count,
2485            reverie::SKID_OVERSHOOT_MARKER
2486        )
2487    }
2488}
2489
2490impl std::error::Error for SkidOvershootError {}
2491
2492fn take_skid_overshoot_error() -> Option<SkidOvershootError> {
2493    let count = reverie::take_skid_overshoot_count();
2494    (count > 0).then(|| SkidOvershootError::new(count))
2495}
2496
2497impl SkidOvershootReport {
2498    fn begin(enabled: bool) -> Self {
2499        if enabled {
2500            // A previous invocation in this process must not qualify this one.
2501            let _ = reverie::take_skid_overshoot_count();
2502        }
2503        Self { enabled }
2504    }
2505
2506    fn finish<T>(self, result: Result<T, Error>) -> Result<T, Error> {
2507        if !self.enabled {
2508            return result;
2509        }
2510
2511        let Some(overshoot) = take_skid_overshoot_error() else {
2512            return result;
2513        };
2514        match result {
2515            Ok(_) => Err(Error::new(overshoot)),
2516            Err(error) => Err(error.context(overshoot)),
2517        }
2518    }
2519
2520    fn finish_with_count<T>(self, result: Result<T, Error>) -> Result<(T, u64), Error> {
2521        if !self.enabled {
2522            return result.map(|value| (value, 0));
2523        }
2524
2525        let count = reverie::take_skid_overshoot_count();
2526        match result {
2527            Ok(value) => Ok((value, count)),
2528            Err(error) if count > 0 => Err(error.context(SkidOvershootError::new(count))),
2529            Err(error) => Err(error),
2530        }
2531    }
2532}

2593#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2594const SABRE_BINARY_ENV: &str = "HERMIT_SABRE_BINARY";
2595
2596#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2597fn is_executable_file(path: &Path) -> bool {
2598    fs::metadata(path)
2599        .is_ok_and(|metadata| metadata.is_file() && metadata.permissions().mode() & 0o111 != 0)
2600}
2601
2602// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-739): Review SaBRe loader discovery and executable validation.
2603#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2604fn resolve_sabre_binary_from(
2605    override_path: Option<&OsStr>,
2606    packaged_path: Option<&Path>,
2607    executable: &Path,
2608    path_env: &OsStr,
2609) -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
2610    if let Some(requested) = override_path {
2611        if requested.is_empty() {
2612            return Err(anyhow!("{SABRE_BINARY_ENV} is empty"));
2613        }
2614        let path = PathBuf::from(requested);
2615        return is_executable_file(&path)
2616            .then_some(path.clone())
2617            .ok_or_else(|| {
2618                anyhow!(
2619                    "{SABRE_BINARY_ENV}={} is not an executable file",
2620                    path.display()
2621                )
2622            });
2623    }
2624
2625    if let Some(path) = packaged_path
2626        && is_executable_file(path)
2627    {
2628        return Ok(path.to_path_buf());
2629    }
2630
2631    let directory = executable
2632        .parent()
2633        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("Hermit executable has no parent directory"))?;
2634    let sibling = directory.join("sabre");
2635    let target_build = directory.parent().map(|target| target.join("sabre/sabre"));
2636
2637    if is_executable_file(&sibling) {
2638        return Ok(sibling);
2639    }
2640    if let Some(candidate) = &target_build
2641        && is_executable_file(candidate)
2642    {
2643        return Ok(candidate.clone());
2644    }
2645    if !path_env.is_empty()
2646        && let Some(candidate) = std::env::split_paths(path_env)
2647            .map(|directory| directory.join("sabre"))
2648            .find(|candidate| is_executable_file(candidate))
2649    {
2650        return Ok(candidate);
2651    }
2652
2653    Err(anyhow!(
2654        "SaBRe executable was not found in the Hermit installation, beside {}, or in PATH; set {} or {SABRE_BINARY_ENV}",
2655        executable.display(),
2656        hermit_resources::INSTALL_DIR_ENV
2657    ))
2658}
2659
2660#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2661fn resolve_sabre_binary() -> Result<PathBuf, Error> {
2662    let executable =
2663        std::env::current_exe().context("failed to locate running Hermit executable")?;
2664    let override_path = std::env::var_os(SABRE_BINARY_ENV);
2665    let packaged_path = hermit_resources::resource("sabre")?;
2666    let path_env = std::env::var_os("PATH").unwrap_or_default();
2667    resolve_sabre_binary_from(
2668        override_path.as_deref(),
2669        packaged_path.as_deref(),
2670        &executable,
2671        &path_env,
2672    )
2673}
2674
2675#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2676const SABRE_RPC_SOCKET_ENV: &str = "REVERIE_SABRE_HERMIT_RPC_SOCKET";
2677#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2678const SABRE_DETLOG_FORWARD_ENV: &str = "REVERIE_SABRE_HERMIT_FORWARD_DETLOG";
2679/// `reverie_sabre::TOOL_OUTPUT_ENV`: the descriptor reverie-sabre protects
2680/// for the in-guest tool's own output. Hermit does not link reverie-sabre.
2681#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2682const SABRE_TOOL_OUTPUT_ENV: &str = "REVERIE_SABRE_TOOL_OUTPUT_FD";
2683/// `detcore_liteinst::DETLOG_FORWARD_ENV`; that crate is a preload `cdylib`, so
2684/// Hermit cannot import the constant.
2685#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
2686const LITEINST_DETLOG_FORWARD_ENV: &str = "HERMIT_LITEINST_FORWARD_DETLOG";
2687/// `detcore_liteinst::DETLOG_FORWARD_POLICY_ENV`, for the same reason.
2688#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
2689const LITEINST_DETLOG_FORWARD_POLICY_ENV: &str = "HERMIT_LITEINST_FORWARD_DETLOG_POLICY";
2690
2691/// Where in-guest LiteInst and SaBRe runs in this process forward Detcore's
2692/// DETLOG records; see [`forward_in_guest_detlogs_to`].
2693static IN_GUEST_DETLOG_SINK: Mutex<Option<std::os::fd::OwnedFd>> = Mutex::new(None);
2694
2695/// Makes the in-guest LiteInst and SaBRe runs this process starts forward the
2696/// DETLOG records Detcore logs inside the guest to `socket`, the sending end of a Unix
2697/// `SOCK_SEQPACKET` pair. `hermit run --verify` gives each run its own pair and
2698/// reads the records from the other end into that run's log. Each record is one
2699/// message, one line (`detcore::detlog::forwarded_line`).
2700/// A record is forwarded when the CLI's filter logs INFO for its module (see
2701/// [`in_guest_detlog_forward_policy`]); without a socket none are forwarded.
2702#[doc(hidden)]
2703pub fn forward_in_guest_detlogs_to(socket: std::os::fd::OwnedFd) {
2704    *IN_GUEST_DETLOG_SINK.lock().unwrap() = Some(socket);
2705}
2706
2707/// What Hermit tells the in-guest LiteInst runtime, which travels in the
2708/// sealed preload bootstrap rather than the guest's environment
2709/// ([`detcore::in_guest_launch`]), so none of it lands on the guest's initial
2710/// stack or in `/proc/self/environ`:
2711/// - this build's [`detcore::config_wire_fingerprint`], which the runtime
2712///   compares with its own before it decodes the configuration the
2713///   coordinator sends. A runtime built from another tree then fails naming
2714///   both fingerprints and its own path, not with a bare decoding error
2715///   (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3986>);
2716/// - when `policy` forwards any record, the socket chosen with
2717///   [`forward_in_guest_detlogs_to`] (an inheritable duplicate, which the
2718///   runtime moves to a descriptor Reverie reserves and protects from the
2719///   guest) and the encoded policy, which the guest's Detcore applies to each
2720///   record by its module as each in-process `detlog!` callsite asks tracing.
2721///
2722/// The caller keeps the returned duplicate open until the guest has started.
2723/// Hermit's own variable names are removed from `command`, so a stale value
2724/// cannot reach a runtime that falls back to the environment.
2725#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
2726fn in_guest_liteinst_launch(
2727    command: &mut Command,
2728    policy: &detcore::detlog::ForwardPolicy,
2729) -> Result<
2730    (
2731        detcore::in_guest_launch::InGuestLaunch,
2732        Option<std::os::fd::OwnedFd>,
2733    ),
2734    Error,
2735> {
2736    command.env_remove(LITEINST_DETLOG_FORWARD_ENV);
2737    command.env_remove(LITEINST_DETLOG_FORWARD_POLICY_ENV);
2738    command.env_remove(detcore::LITEINST_CONFIG_FINGERPRINT_ENV);
2739    let mut launch = detcore::in_guest_launch::InGuestLaunch {
2740        coordinator_fingerprint: Some(detcore::config_wire_fingerprint()),
2741        ..Default::default()
2742    };
2743    // Asking only whether INFO is on for `detcore`, and then forwarding
2744    // everything, kept records a target-scoped filter drops under ptrace
2745    // (info,detcore::random=warn) and could forward nothing where it keeps
2746    // some (warn,detcore::random=info).
2747    if !policy.forwards_any() {
2748        return Ok((launch, None));
2749    }
2750    let Some(duplicate) = inheritable_in_guest_detlog_socket()? else {
2751        return Ok((launch, None));
2752    };
2753    launch.forward_request = Some(detcore::detlog::tool_output_env_value(
2754        duplicate.as_raw_fd(),
2755    )?);
2756    launch.forward_policy = Some(policy.encode());
2757    Ok((launch, Some(duplicate)))
2758}
2759
2760/// An inheritable duplicate of the socket chosen with
2761/// [`forward_in_guest_detlogs_to`], or `None` when none was chosen. The
2762/// caller passes its number to the guest and keeps it open until the guest
2763/// has started.
2764#[cfg(any(feature = "sabre", feature = "liteinst"))]
2765fn inheritable_in_guest_detlog_socket() -> Result<Option<std::os::fd::OwnedFd>, Error> {
2766    let sink = IN_GUEST_DETLOG_SINK.lock().unwrap();
2767    let Some(socket) = sink.as_ref() else {
2768        return Ok(None);
2769    };
2770    // SAFETY: F_DUPFD on an open descriptor returns a new descriptor or -1.
2771    let duplicate = unsafe { libc::fcntl(socket.as_raw_fd(), libc::F_DUPFD, 3) };
2772    if duplicate < 0 {
2773        return Err(Error::new(std::io::Error::last_os_error())
2774            .context("duplicating the in-guest DETLOG forwarding socket"));
2775    }
2776    // SAFETY: fcntl returned a new descriptor this function now owns.
2777    Ok(Some(unsafe {
2778        std::os::fd::OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(duplicate)
2779    }))
2780}
2781#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2782const SABRE_PATH_EVIDENCE_ENV: &str = "HERMIT_SABRE_PATH_EVIDENCE";
2783
2784/// The INFO policy for DETLOG records an in-guest Detcore (SaBRe's plugin,
2785/// in-guest LiteInst) forwards: the current subscriber's answer for every
2786/// target the CLI's `RUST_LOG` names (the text
2787/// `EffectiveFilter::from_default_env` builds every CLI subscriber from) and
2788/// for any other target.
2789#[cfg(any(feature = "sabre", feature = "liteinst"))]
2790fn in_guest_detlog_forward_policy() -> detcore::detlog::ForwardPolicy {
2791    let directives = std::env::var(tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::DEFAULT_ENV).unwrap_or_default();
2792    detcore::detlog::ForwardPolicy::from_current_subscriber(&directives)
2793}
2794#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2795const SABRE_STAGING_DIRECTORY: &str = "/dev/shm";
2796
2797#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2798struct StagedSabreProgram {
2799    path: PathBuf,
2800}
2801
2802#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2803impl Drop for StagedSabreProgram {
2804    fn drop(&mut self) {
2805        let _ = fs::remove_file(&self.path);
2806    }
2807}
2808
2809#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2810fn sabre_program_needs_neutral_name(program: &Path) -> bool {
2811    program
2812        .file_name()
2813        .is_some_and(|name| name.as_bytes().starts_with(b"ld"))
2814}
2815
2816// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-845): Review the neutral-name workaround for SaBRe's
2817// dynamic-loader prefix collision.
2818#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2819fn stage_sabre_program_in(
2820    program: &Path,
2821    staging_directory: &Path,
2822) -> Result<Option<StagedSabreProgram>, Error> {
2823    if !sabre_program_needs_neutral_name(program) {
2824        return Ok(None);
2825    }
2826
2827    let path = staging_directory.join(format!("hermit-sabre-program-{}", std::process::id()));
2828    let mut source = fs::File::open(program).map_err(|error| {
2829        anyhow!(
2830            "failed to open SaBRe guest executable {} for neutral-name staging: {error}",
2831            program.display()
2832        )
2833    })?;
2834    let mut staged = fs::OpenOptions::new()
2835        .write(true)
2836        .create_new(true)
2837        .mode(0o700)
2838        .open(&path)
2839        .map_err(|error| {
2840            anyhow!(
2841                "failed to stage SaBRe guest executable {} as {}: {error}",
2842                program.display(),
2843                path.display()
2844            )
2845        })?;
2846    if let Err(error) = io::copy(&mut source, &mut staged) {
2847        let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);
2848        return Err(anyhow!(
2849            "failed to stage SaBRe guest executable {} as {}: {error}",
2850            program.display(),
2851            path.display()
2852        ));
2853    }
2854    drop(staged);
2855
2856    Ok(Some(StagedSabreProgram { path }))
2857}

2859// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-738): Review controller/plugin artifact separation.
2860#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2861fn sabre_runtime_library_path() -> io::Result<PathBuf> {
2862    if let Some(path) = hermit_resources::resource("libdetcore_sabre.so")?
2863        && path.is_file()
2864    {
2865        return Ok(path);
2866    }
2867
2868    let executable = std::env::current_exe()?;
2869    let directory = executable.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
2870        io::Error::new(
2871            io::ErrorKind::NotFound,
2872            "Hermit executable has no parent directory",
2873        )
2874    })?;
2875    [
2876        directory.join("libdetcore_sabre.so"),
2877        directory.join("deps/libdetcore_sabre.so"),
2878    ]
2879    .into_iter()
2880    .find(|path| path.is_file())
2881    .ok_or_else(|| {
2882        io::Error::new(
2883            io::ErrorKind::NotFound,
2884            format!(
2885                "libdetcore_sabre.so was not built beside {}",
2886                executable.display()
2887            ),
2888        )
2889    })
2890}
