2904// AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
2905// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-774): Review the bounded SaBRe RPC disconnect drain.
2906#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2907const SABRE_RPC_DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);
2908
2909#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2910async fn wait_for_sabre_rpc_disconnects<T>(
2911    global: &Arc<T>,
2912    timeout: Duration,
2913) -> Result<(), usize> {
2914    let disconnected = tokio::time::timeout(timeout, async {
2915        while Arc::strong_count(global) > 1 {
2916            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1)).await;
2917        }
2918    })
2919    .await;
2920
2921    if disconnected.is_ok() {
2922        return Ok(());
2923    }
2924
2925    let live_references = Arc::strong_count(global).saturating_sub(1);
2926    if live_references == 0 {
2927        Ok(())
2928    } else {
2929        Err(live_references)
2930    }
2931}
2932
2933// AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
2934// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-782): Review SaBRe RPC server shutdown errors.
2935#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2936async fn stop_sabre_rpc_server<E>(
2937    server_task: tokio::task::JoinHandle<Result<(), E>>,
2938) -> Result<(), Error>
2939where
2940    E: std::fmt::Display,
2941{
2942    server_task.abort();
2943    match server_task.await {
2944        Err(error) if error.is_cancelled() => Ok(()),
2945        Err(error) => Err(anyhow!("SaBRe coordinator task failed: {error}")),
2946        Ok(Err(error)) => Err(anyhow!("SaBRe coordinator server failed: {error}")),
2947        Ok(Ok(())) => Err(anyhow!("SaBRe coordinator server stopped unexpectedly")),
2948    }
2949}
2950
2951// AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
2952// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-789): Review complete SaBRe RPC shutdown ordering.
2953#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2954async fn shutdown_sabre_rpc<T, E>(
2955    server_task: tokio::task::JoinHandle<Result<(), E>>,
2956    global: &Arc<T>,
2957    timeout: Duration,
2958) -> Result<(), Error>
2959where
2960    E: std::fmt::Display,
2961{
2962    let server_result = stop_sabre_rpc_server(server_task).await;
2963    let disconnect_result = wait_for_sabre_rpc_disconnects(global, timeout).await;
2964
2965    server_result?;
2966    disconnect_result.map_err(|live_references| {
2967        anyhow!("SaBRe coordinator stopped with {live_references} live RPC reference(s)")
2968    })
2969}
2970
2971fn ensure_backend_dispatch(backend: Backend) -> Result<(), Error> {
2972    // The CLI probes ptrace readiness before entering its container; repeating
2973    // the namespace probe here would test nested namespaces instead of the host.
2974    if backend == Backend::Ptrace {
2975        return Ok(());
2976    }
2977    if backend == Backend::E9patch {
2978        return Err(anyhow!(
2979            "backend `e9patch` requires CLI preprocessing; library callers must use \
2980             e9patch::prepare and then select `ptrace`"
2981        ));
2982    }
2983    // KVM and DBT have dedicated dispatches (`run_kvm` and `run_dbt`); neither
2984    // must reach this generic rejection path.
2985    backend.ensure_available()?;
2986    Err(anyhow!(
2987        "backend `{}` has no Hermit dispatch implementation",
2988        backend.as_str()
2989    ))
2990}
2991
2992/// Run one command with the Detcore tool executing inside a SaBRe plugin and
2993/// the single GlobalState held by this Hermit coordinator process.
2994// AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
2995// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-738): Review SaBRe coordinator lifetime and artifact loading.
2996#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
2997async fn run_sabre(
2998    mut command: Command,
2999    config: DetConfig,
3000    print_summary: bool,
3001    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
3002    capture_output: bool,
3003) -> Result<Output, Error> {
3004    let path_evidence_file = std::env::var_os(SABRE_PATH_EVIDENCE_ENV).map(PathBuf::from);
3005    // Whether this run passes the plugin a DETLOG socket (below), in which case
3006    // every Tool image must forward on it; see
3007    // detcore::Config::in_guest_detlog_forward_policy.
3008    let mut config = config;
3009    let policy = in_guest_detlog_forward_policy();
3010    config.in_guest_detlog_forward_policy = (policy.forwards_any()
3011        && IN_GUEST_DETLOG_SINK.lock().unwrap().is_some())
3012    .then(|| policy.encode());
3013    let sabre = resolve_sabre_binary()?;
3014    // The kernel execs SaBRe's loader, which loads the guest itself, so the
3015    // kernel's `exe` link names the loader (`detcore::LaunchImage::launcher`).
3016    // Declared even where the first image could not be resolved, so that a
3017    // link Detcore cannot answer is refused rather than named the loader.
3018    config
3019        .launch_image
3020        .get_or_insert(detcore::LaunchImage {
3021            exe: None,
3022            launcher: None,
3023        })
3024        .launcher = Some(PathBuf::from(&sabre));
3025    let plugin = sabre_runtime_library_path()
3026        .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to locate the Detcore SaBRe plugin: {error}"))?;
3027    let program = command.find_program().map_err(|error| {
3028        anyhow!(
3029            "failed to resolve SaBRe guest executable {:?}: {error}",
3030            command.get_program()
3031        )
3032    })?;
3033    let staged_program = stage_sabre_program_in(&program, Path::new(SABRE_STAGING_DIRECTORY))?;
3034    let launch_program = staged_program
3035        .as_ref()
3036        .map_or(program.as_path(), |staged| staged.path.as_path());
3037
3038    let bootstrap_launch =
3039        sabre_bootstrap::Launch::new(Path::new(&sabre), launch_program, &config)?;
3040
3041    // This runs after Hermit enters the guest mount namespace, where `/tmp`
3042    // names the container-visible temporary filesystem. Do not inherit a
3043    // host-side nested TMPDIR: validation commonly sets TMPDIR=/tmp/<run>/tmp,
3044    // but that parent path is hidden once the private `/tmp` mount is active.
3045    // The SaBRe plugin and coordinator must name the socket through the same
3046    // namespace-visible path.
3047    let socket_dir = tempfile::Builder::new()
3048        .prefix("hermit-sabre-rpc-")
3049        .tempdir_in(Path::new("/tmp"))?;
3050    let socket_path = socket_dir.path().join("coordinator.sock");
3051    let fallback_ready = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
3052    let global = Arc::new(detcore::GlobalState::init_global_state(&config).await);
3053    let server = reverie_rpc_transport::RpcServer::bind_with_readiness(
3054        &socket_path,
3055        global.clone(),
3056        config.clone(),
3057        fallback_ready.clone(),
3058    )
3059    .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to start SaBRe coordinator RPC: {error}"))?;
3060    let server_task = tokio::spawn(async move { server.serve().await });
3061
3062    // SaBRe runs with the guest's own argv and environment, so the kernel
3063    // builds the guest's initial stack, /proc/self/cmdline and
3064    // /proc/self/environ from them, as for an exec of the guest itself. The
3065    // plugin and image paths and the plugin's settings go in a sealed launch
3066    // specification instead (reverie_sabre_stats::launch), which SaBRe's loader
3067    // reads and closes before the guest starts. A script runs as its
3068    // interpreter, with the argv the kernel would give it.
3069    let mut first_bytes = vec![0u8; 256];
3070    let read = std::fs::File::open(launch_program)
3071        .and_then(|mut file| std::io::Read::read(&mut file, &mut first_bytes))
3072        .map_err(|error| {
3073            anyhow!(
3074                "failed to read SaBRe guest executable {}: {error}",
3075                launch_program.display()
3076            )
3077        })?;
3078    first_bytes.truncate(read);
3079    let arg0 = command.get_arg0().to_owned();
3080    let client = match reverie_sabre_stats::launch::shebang(&first_bytes) {
3081        Some((interpreter, argument)) => {
3082            command.program(&sabre);
3083            command.arg0(OsStr::from_bytes(&interpreter));
3084            let mut words: Vec<&OsStr> = argument
3085                .iter()
3086                .map(|word| OsStr::from_bytes(word))
3087                .collect();
3088            words.push(launch_program.as_os_str());
3089            command.prepend_args(words);
3090            PathBuf::from(OsStr::from_bytes(&interpreter))
3091        }
3092        None => {
3093            command.program(&sabre);
3094            command.arg0(&arg0);
3095            launch_program.to_path_buf()
3096        }
3097    };
3098    let mut launch_settings: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::new();
3099    let mut setting = |name: &str, value: &OsStr| {
3100        let mut entry = name.as_bytes().to_vec();
3101        entry.push(b'=');
3102        entry.extend_from_slice(value.as_bytes());
3103        launch_settings.push(entry);
3104    };
3105    setting(SABRE_RPC_SOCKET_ENV, socket_path.as_os_str());
3106    command.env_remove(SABRE_RPC_SOCKET_ENV);
3107    command.env_remove(sabre_bootstrap::ENVIRONMENT);
3108    if bootstrap_launch.initializes_random() {
3109        setting(sabre_bootstrap::ENVIRONMENT, OsStr::new("1"));
3110    }
3111    // Publish the configuration and clock RPC fingerprint for this coordinator.
3112    // The plugin is a separate artifact in the same target directory, so it can
3113    // be stale without looking it. Its check before connecting names the mismatch
3114    // instead of failing to decode Config or a later DetTime request field.
3115    // See detcore_model::config_wire_fingerprint.
3116    setting(
3117        detcore::CONFIG_FINGERPRINT_ENV,
3118        OsStr::new(&detcore::config_wire_fingerprint()),
3119    );
3120    command.env_remove(detcore::CONFIG_FINGERPRINT_ENV);
3121    command.env_remove(SABRE_PATH_EVIDENCE_ENV);
3122    command.env_remove(SABRE_DETLOG_FORWARD_ENV);
3123    // Per emitting module, as each in-process `detlog!` callsite asks tracing:
3124    // asking only about `detcore` dropped every record a target-scoped
3125    // RUST_LOG (warn,detcore::random=info) keeps under ptrace.
3126    command.env_remove(SABRE_TOOL_OUTPUT_ENV);
3127    let detlog_policy = in_guest_detlog_forward_policy();
3128    // Kept open until the guest has started (it inherits its own copy).
3129    let mut _detlog_descriptor = None;
3130    if detlog_policy.forwards_any() {
3131        setting(
3132            SABRE_DETLOG_FORWARD_ENV,
3133            OsStr::new(&detlog_policy.encode()),
3134        );
3135        // With a socket (`hermit run --verify`), the plugin sends each record
3136        // on it from a descriptor reverie-sabre protects from the guest, and
3137        // the coordinator writes each thread's records into the log at that
3138        // thread's scheduler turns, as for in-guest LiteInst. Without one it
3139        // writes them to the guest's standard error.
3140        if let Some(socket) = inheritable_in_guest_detlog_socket()? {
3141            setting(
3142                SABRE_TOOL_OUTPUT_ENV,
3143                OsStr::new(&detcore::detlog::tool_output_env_value(socket.as_raw_fd())?),
3144            );
3145            _detlog_descriptor = Some(socket);
3146        }
3147    }
3148    command.env_remove("SABRE_BINARY");
3149    command.env_remove("SABRE_PLUGIN");
3150    // Always collect: the statistics page is a descriptor the guest can see,
3151    // so creating it only when a summary or DEBUG log is requested would make
3152    // those flags change the guest's view. Its number travels in the launch
3153    // specification, and the descriptor sits above the plugin's fixed RPC
3154    // socket.
3155    let stats = reverie_sabre_stats::SabreStats::create(reverie::BackendStatsRequest::ENABLED)
3156        .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to create the SaBRe statistics page: {error}"))?
3157        .expect("an enabled request creates the statistics page");
3158    setting(
3159        reverie_sabre_stats::BACKEND_STATS_ENV,
3160        OsStr::new(&stats.raw_fd().to_string()),
3161    );
3162    command.env_remove(reverie_sabre_stats::BACKEND_STATS_ENV);
3163    let launch_settings: Vec<&[u8]> = launch_settings.iter().map(Vec::as_slice).collect();
3164    let launch_spec = reverie_sabre_stats::launch::spec_bytes(
3165        plugin.as_os_str().as_bytes(),
3166        client.as_os_str().as_bytes(),
3167        &launch_settings,
3168    )
3169    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("the SaBRe launch specification is malformed or too large"))?;
3170    // Kept open until the guest has started (it inherits its own copy, which
3171    // SaBRe's loader closes).
3172    let _launch_spec = reverie_sabre_stats::launch::spec_fd(&launch_spec)
3173        .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to create the SaBRe launch specification: {error}"))?;
3174
3175    // THE SOCKET PATH IS DELIBERATELY RANDOM AND MUST NOT BE COMPARED.
3176    //
3177    // `tempfile` appends a random 6-character suffix to the directory above, so
3178    // the absolute path differs on every launch by design -- that is what keeps
3179    // concurrent hermit invocations on a shared host from binding the same
3180    // coordinator socket. Emitting it at INFO put per-launch randomness into the
3181    // INFO stream, which `--verify-strict` compares:
3182    //
3183    //   Mismatch at log messages 2 (run 1) and 2 (run 2):
3184    //   < socket=/tmp/hermit-sabre-rpc-Gw6tUi/coordinator.sock
3185    //   > socket=/tmp/hermit-sabre-rpc-7SZ94p/coordinator.sock
3186    //
3187    // That fails EVERY SaBRe verify cell before the guest executes an
3188    // instruction, for a host-side value with no guest-visible content. The
3189    // defect was in the oracle, not the backend.
3190    //
3191    // WHY THE VALUE IS DROPPED FROM INFO RATHER THAN MADE DETERMINISTIC: the two
3192    // `--verify` runs execute in SEPARATE CHILD PROCESSES, so any path stable
3193    // across both would have to be derived from state shared between them. That
3194    // trades `tempfile`'s guaranteed-fresh directory for a reused one, and a
3195    // run1 that dies holding the socket would then make run2 fail to bind -- a
3196    // real new failure mode in exchange for a cosmetic field. The path keeps its
3197    // randomness; only the compared stream stops carrying it.
3198    //
3199    // This is NOT a comparator relaxation. No normalization envelope is widened,
3200    // so any future randomness leaking into this banner still fails the
3201    // comparison. The full path remains available one level down.
3202    tracing::debug!(
3203        target: "hermit::sabre",
3204        socket = %socket_path.display(),
3205        "SaBRe coordinator RPC socket (per-launch temp path, deliberately not at INFO)",
3206    );
3207    tracing::info!(
3208        target: "hermit::sabre",
3209        guest = %program.display(),
3210        plugin = %plugin.display(),
3211        "launching Detcore guest through SaBRe with coordinator RPC",
3212    );
3213
3214    let supervised = match sabre_ptrace::run(
3215        command.into_std_lossy(),
3216        PathBuf::from(&sabre),
3217        plugin.clone(),
3218        fallback_ready,
3219        global.clone(),
3220        bootstrap_launch,
3221        stats.clone(),
3222        capture_output,
3223    )
3224    .await
3225    {
3226        Ok(supervised) => supervised,
3227        Err(error) => {
3228            global.release_all_physical_process_exits();
3229            global.force_shutdown_with_error();
3230            let _ = shutdown_sabre_rpc(server_task, &global, SABRE_RPC_DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT).await;
3231            return Err(error);
3232        }
3233    };
3234    // The supervisor returns only after every tracee reached a final kernel wait status. Release
3235    // the root process's barrier (and any intentionally unreaped child barriers) before scheduler
3236    // shutdown; no guest thread remains that could race timer fast-forward here.
3237    global.release_all_physical_process_exits();
3238    // A SaBRe execution in which no guest thread ever reached the coordinator
3239    // is an execution in which Detcore was never loaded as a Reverie tool: the
3240    // guest ran on bare Linux. Treat it exactly like a failed run so the
3241    // scheduler is torn down here instead of blocking forever in `clean_up`
3242    // below, waiting for a guest thread that will never register.
3243    let detcore_never_engaged = !supervised.path_evidence.guest_rpc_observed;
3244    let requires_forced_shutdown = !supervised.status.success() || detcore_never_engaged;
3245    if requires_forced_shutdown {
3246        global.force_shutdown_with_error();
3247    }
3248    // Emit one unconditional, machine-readable per-run fact instead of a
3249    // free-form warning. SaBRe loads the guest interpreter before the Detcore
3250    // plugin, so pre-plugin loader syscalls are structurally absent from its
3251    // observation envelope. Versioning that fact lets scorecard consumers
3252    // reject old or incomplete records rather than infer coverage from silence.
3253    //
3254    // Keep this in the controller-diagnostic stream rather than writing
3255    // directly to the process stderr that also carries captured guest stderr.
3256    // WARN is Hermit's default tracing level, and `--log-file` can therefore
3257    // separate the unconditional controller fact from guest output without a
3258    // comparator exception. A missing record remains distinct from a record
3259    // whose counters are zero.
3260    let backend_evidence = sabre_backend_evidence_line(&supervised.path_evidence);
3261    tracing::warn!(target: "hermit::sabre", "{backend_evidence}");
3262    if let Some(path) = path_evidence_file {
3263        let mut file = fs::OpenOptions::new()
3264            .create(true)
3265            .append(true)
3266            .mode(0o600)
3267            .open(&path)
3268            .map_err(|error| {
3269                anyhow!(
3270                    "failed to open SaBRe path evidence {}: {error}",
3271                    path.display()
3272                )
3273            })?;
3274        serde_json::to_writer(&mut file, &supervised.path_evidence)?;
3275        writeln!(file)?;
3276    }
3277    let output = Output {
3278        status: supervised.status.into(),
3279        stdout: supervised.stdout,
3280        stderr: supervised.stderr,
3281    };
3282
3283    shutdown_sabre_rpc(server_task, &global, SABRE_RPC_DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT).await?;
3284    let mut global = Arc::try_unwrap(global).map_err(|global| {
3285        anyhow!(
3286            "SaBRe coordinator stopped with {} live RPC reference(s)",
3287            Arc::strong_count(&global) - 1
3288        )
3289    })?;
3290    if requires_forced_shutdown {
3291        global.cancel_internal_scheduler().await;
3292    }
3293    let dispatch_stats = backend_stats::report(
3294        Backend::Sabre,
3295        backend_stats::request(print_summary_to_json_file),
3296        &stats,
3297    );
3298    let finalized = global
3299        .clean_up_with_dispatch_stats(print_summary, print_summary_to_json_file, dispatch_stats)
3300        .await;
3301    tracing::info!(
3302        target: "hermit::sabre::fallback",
3303        ptrace_fallback_sites = supervised.path_evidence.ptrace_fallback_sites,
3304        trusted_shared_object_sites = supervised.path_evidence.trusted_shared_object_sites,
3305        guest_rpc_observed = supervised.path_evidence.guest_rpc_observed,
3306        "SaBRe ptrace fallback completed",
3307    );
3308    if detcore_never_engaged {
3309        return detcore::combine_finalization(
3310            Err(Error::new(BackendRunFailure)
3311                .context(sabre_uninstrumented_guest_message(&output.status))),
3312            finalized,
3313        );
3314    }
3315    detcore::combine_finalization(Ok(output), finalized)
3316}
3317
3318#[cfg(not(feature = "sabre"))]
3319async fn run_sabre(
3320    _command: Command,
3321    _config: DetConfig,
3322    _print_summary: bool,
3323    _print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
3324    _capture_output: bool,
3325) -> Result<Output, Error> {
3326    Backend::Sabre.ensure_available()?;
3327    unreachable!("SaBRe availability must fail when the feature is disabled");
3328}
3329
3330/// Classify the existing SaBRe reach evidence without collapsing "never
3331/// engaged" into the same zero-valued state as a fully exercised run.
3332#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
3333fn sabre_reach_state(guest_rpc_observed: bool, ptrace_fallback_sites: usize) -> &'static str {
3334    match (guest_rpc_observed, ptrace_fallback_sites) {
3335        (false, _) => "no-detcore-reached",
3336        (true, 1..) => "degraded-ptrace-fallback",
3337        (true, 0) => "sabre-exercised",
3338    }
3339}
3340
3341/// Produce the versioned SaBRe backend fact consumed by compatibility reports.
3342///
3343/// `preplugin_coverage=absent` is a property of SaBRe's launch order: the guest
3344/// interpreter runs before the Detcore plugin is loaded. It is recorded rather
3345/// than inferred from counters because the ptrace fallback cannot observe that
3346/// interval either.
3347///
3348/// Preserve the originating #1725 measurement as provenance for that field:
3349/// on its measurement host, `/bin/true` produced 3 COMMITs under SaBRe versus
3350/// 14 under ptrace; the 11 absent records were the loader's libc.so.6 path
3351/// resolution. The launch-order fact, not that host-specific count, is the
3352/// runtime contract.
3353#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
3354fn sabre_backend_evidence_line(evidence: &sabre_ptrace::PathEvidence) -> String {
3355    format!(
3356        ":: Backend: sabre static rewriting + ptrace runtime; run_mode=run; \
3357         evidence_schema={}; preplugin_coverage=absent; ptrace_fallback_sites={}; \
3358         trusted_shared_object_sites={}; guest_rpc_observed={}; reach_state={}",
3359        evidence.schema,
3360        evidence.ptrace_fallback_sites,
3361        evidence.trusted_shared_object_sites,
3362        evidence.guest_rpc_observed,
3363        sabre_reach_state(evidence.guest_rpc_observed, evidence.ptrace_fallback_sites),
3364    )
3365}
3366
3367/// Explain a SaBRe run whose guest never reached the Detcore coordinator.
3368///
3369/// `guest_rpc_observed` is set by the coordinator RPC listener the first time a
3370/// SaBRe-loaded guest connects. When it stays false the guest completed without
3371/// Detcore intercepting anything, so the run carries no determinism guarantee
3372/// whatsoever -- its timing, scheduling, PIDs, and clock reads all came from the
3373/// host. Reporting that as a successful `hermit run` would be a fail-open
3374/// determinism hole, so the caller turns it into a hard error and this function
3375/// supplies the diagnosis.
3376///
3377/// The dominant cause is a guest whose syscall sites SaBRe never rewrote. A
3378/// statically linked ELF is the sharp edge: it has no dynamic loader and no
3379/// shared library through which SaBRe could regain control, so an unrewritten
3380/// static client runs entirely on bare Linux with no second chance.
3381#[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
3382fn sabre_uninstrumented_guest_message(status: &ExitStatus) -> String {
3383    format!(
3384        "the SaBRe backend finished ({status:?}) without the guest ever reaching the Detcore \
3385         coordinator: no syscall was intercepted, so this run applied no determinization at all \
3386         and its result is not a Hermit guarantee. This means SaBRe rewrote no syscall site in \
3387         the guest -- most often a statically linked ELF, whose syscall sites SaBRe must patch \
3388         in the client image itself because there is no dynamic loader to intercept."
3389    )
3390}
3391
3392/// Guest-physical memory available to the single-process KVM personality.
3393// The KVM personality is a sparse MAP_NORESERVE address space. QEMU needs room
3394// for its own ELF mappings in addition to the nested machine's RAM mapping.
3395// reverie-kvm places every guest mapping in this window, even a PROT_NONE
3396// reservation, so a runtime that reserves address space up front needs room
3397// here: node's V8 reserves 256, 128 and then 512 MiB twice, which 1 GiB could
3398// not hold (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4366). 3 GiB is the
3399// largest window reverie-kvm's bootstrap identity-maps. The window costs the
3400// host only the pages a guest touches, and mmap and munmap discard ranges of
3401// 2 MiB or more rather than writing zeros over them
3402// (https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/1059). madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)
3403// still writes zeros over every page, and node calls it over its 512 MiB
3404// reservation, so a node run peaks near 880 MB of host memory until that is
3405// made lazy too (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4366).
3406const KVM_GUEST_MEMORY_BYTES: usize = 3 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024;
3407
3408/// Maximum `#!` interpreter indirection levels, matching the Linux kernel's
3409/// `BINPRM_MAX_RECURSION` limit for chained script interpreters.
3410const MAX_SHEBANG_DEPTH: usize = 4;
3411
3412/// Resolve `#!` interpreter scripts before the reverie-kvm ELF loader runs.
3413///
3414/// The KVM ELF loader can only map ELF images, so a guest program that is
3415/// actually a `#!`-script (for example `/usr/local/bin/file` -> `#!/bin/bash`,
3416/// or `/usr/bin/pkg-config` -> `#!/usr/bin/sh`) must be rewritten to launch its
3417/// interpreter, exactly as the kernel's `execve(2)` `binfmt_script` handler
3418/// does. On success the returned image is an ELF and `argv` has the interpreter,
3419/// its shebang arguments, and the script path prepended in kernel order:
3420/// `[interp, shebang_args.., script_path, <original argv[1..]>]`.
3421///
3422/// The interpreter line is parsed with hermit's shared [`Shebang`] so the KVM
3423/// backend matches how the ptrace backend and recorder treat `#!`-scripts.
3424fn resolve_kvm_shebang(
3425    resolved_program: &Path,
3426    mut argv: Vec<String>,
3427) -> Result<(PathBuf, Vec<String>, Vec<u8>), Error> {
3428    let mut load_path = resolved_program.to_path_buf();
3429    let mut image = fs::read(&load_path)
3430        .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to read KVM guest executable {load_path:?}: {error}"))?;
3431
3432    let mut depth = 0;
3433    while image.starts_with(b"#!") {
3434        depth += 1;
3435        if depth > MAX_SHEBANG_DEPTH {
3436            return Err(anyhow!(
3437                "too many levels of `#!` interpreter indirection loading {resolved_program:?}"
3438            ));
3439        }
3440        let (interpreter, shebang_args) = Shebang::from_buf(&image)
3441            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("malformed `#!` interpreter line in {load_path:?}"))?
3442            .into_parts();
3443        let interpreter_str = interpreter
3444            .to_str()
3445            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("non-UTF-8 `#!` interpreter path in {load_path:?}"))?
3446            .to_owned();
3447
3448        // Rewrite argv in kernel order. The prior argv[0] (the script's own
3449        // name) is dropped on the first level; on deeper levels the previous
3450        // interpreter path is preserved as a positional argument, matching
3451        // `binfmt_script`.
3452        let mut rewritten = Vec::with_capacity(argv.len() + shebang_args.len() + 2);
3453        rewritten.push(interpreter_str);
3454        for arg in &shebang_args {
3455            rewritten.push(
3456                arg.to_str()
3457                    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("non-UTF-8 `#!` interpreter argument in {load_path:?}"))?
3458                    .to_owned(),
3459            );
3460        }
3461        rewritten.push(load_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
3462        rewritten.extend_from_slice(&argv[1..]);
3463        argv = rewritten;
3464
3465        load_path = interpreter;
3466        image = fs::read(&load_path).map_err(|error| {
3467            anyhow!(
3468                "failed to read `#!` interpreter {load_path:?} for {resolved_program:?}: {error}"
3469            )
3470        })?;
3471    }
3472
3473    Ok((load_path, argv, image))
3474}
3475
3476/// The container replaces this host directory with a private, empty tmpfs, so
3477/// nothing beneath it is visible to the guest. Kept next to the diagnostic that
3478/// depends on it; `run.rs` has its own `TMP_DIR` for the mount itself.
3479const CONTAINER_REPLACED_TMP: &str = "/tmp";
3480
3481/// Explain why a working directory that plainly exists on the host could not be
3482/// resolved for the guest.
3483///
3484/// ⚠️ THIS FUNCTION EXISTS BECAUSE THE BARE ERROR CAUSED A MISDIAGNOSIS, not to
3485/// be tidy. `fs::canonicalize` runs after the container's mounts are applied, and
3486/// the container bind-mounts a fresh empty tmpfs over `/tmp`
3487/// (`bin/hermit/container.rs`). So a cwd beneath `/tmp` is genuinely absent from
3488/// the guest's mount namespace and `canonicalize` returns a perfectly correct
3489/// `NotFound` -- for a directory the user can `ls`.
3490///
3491/// Reported 2026-08-25 as "run_kvm_ cli tests fail from a git worktree". They do
3492/// not. Measured across five working directories with one binary: a PLAIN
3493/// directory under `/tmp` with no git in it FAILS, and a linked git worktree
3494/// under `/home` WORKS. The only property that tracks the failure is "the cwd is
3495/// under /tmp"; `/tmp` itself resolves because the mount POINT exists. The git
3496/// hypothesis cost real investigation time, and it came from this message saying
3497/// only "No such file or directory".
3498///
3499/// It mattered more than a stray report because the historical landing recipe
3500/// placed detached worktrees below `/tmp`, exactly where this fires. Current
3501/// dev-hermit worktrees are created through wrkslots below `worktrees/`, but the
3502/// diagnostic remains necessary for arbitrary callers and older checkouts.
3503///
3504/// The message names the mechanism and both ways out. It deliberately does NOT
3505/// silently fall back to `/`: changing the guest's working directory out from
3506/// under a caller who asked for a specific one would trade a loud, correct
3507/// failure for a quiet, wrong success.
3508fn kvm_cwd_resolution_error(requested_cwd: &Path, error: &std::io::Error) -> Error {
3509    let under_replaced_tmp = requested_cwd.starts_with(CONTAINER_REPLACED_TMP)
3510        && requested_cwd != Path::new(CONTAINER_REPLACED_TMP);
3511    if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound && under_replaced_tmp {
3512        anyhow!(
3513            "failed to resolve KVM guest working directory {:?}: {error}\n\
3514             \n\
3515             This directory may well exist on the host. The container replaces \
3516             {CONTAINER_REPLACED_TMP} with a private, empty tmpfs, so nothing beneath \
3517             {CONTAINER_REPLACED_TMP} is visible to the guest, and resolving the working \
3518             directory happens inside that mount namespace.\n\
3519             Either run from a directory outside {CONTAINER_REPLACED_TMP}, or pass \
3520             --workdir with a path that exists inside the guest.",
3521            requested_cwd
3522        )
3523    } else {
3524        anyhow!(
3525            "failed to resolve KVM guest working directory {:?}: {error}",
3526            requested_cwd
3527        )
3528    }
3529}
3530
3531/// Bind KVM's raw mountinfo and fdinfo to the same filesystem namespace.
3532///
3533/// The CLI supplies IdentityGuard provenance from the completed container: the
3534/// namespace's row/parent order and the namespace it was captured in
3535/// ([`detcore_model::config::MountNamespaceIdentity`], whose kernel ID Linux
3536/// never reuses during a boot). The backend requires its own mount namespace
3537/// to be that one and keeps the producer's order, the same snapshot the
3538/// container mount table was built from; it does not take a second one, and
3539/// it refuses provenance that is not well formed (a duplicate ID, an empty
3540/// order, an assignment Detcore's pool would refuse, a root rewrite or table
3541/// row outside the order).
3542///
3543/// Two captures of one private namespace need not agree. When a host process
3544/// removes the directory a host mount was on, Linux detaches the mounts on that
3545/// dentry in every mount namespace (`vfs_rmdir`, `vfs_unlink` and rename call
3546/// `detach_mounts`, and `__detach_mounts` in fs/namespace.c unmounts each
3547/// mount on the dentry with `umount_tree`), so a copied host row can leave the
3548/// container between two reads although nothing propagates into it. The
3549/// snapshot keeps naming that row. A detached mount stays usable through what
3550/// still holds it (an open descriptor, a working directory, a directory
3551/// descriptor), and fdinfo `mnt_id` and STATX_MNT_ID still number it through
3552/// the order; later mountinfo views lack it and stay ordered subsets of the
3553/// snapshot, which Detcore's validation accepts. A kernel automount (an autofs
3554/// trigger reached by an ordinary path lookup) can add a row after the
3555/// snapshot despite the private propagation: fdinfo and statx number its new
3556/// ID on first observation, and a later kernel-view mountinfo that shows it is
3557/// not an ordered subset and is refused. The container mount table never shows
3558/// it.
3559/// A library caller that built no container and supplies no provenance gets
3560/// this capture; `--no-namespace` runs supply it from Hermit's own namespace
3561/// (`complete_container_config`). Either way Detcore renders the guest's mount
3562/// files from the container mount table. KVM does not permit guest namespace
3563/// changes.
3564fn prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config(
3565    config: &mut DetConfig,
3566    namespace: impl FnOnce() -> Result<detcore_model::config::MountNamespaceIdentity, Error>,
3567    capture: impl FnOnce() -> Result<Vec<u64>, Error>,
3568) -> Result<(), Error> {
3569    if !config.mountinfo_mount_ids_captured
3570        && (!config.mountinfo_mount_ids.is_empty()
3571            || !config.mount_id_assignment_order.is_empty()
3572            || config.mountinfo_mount_namespace.is_some())
3573    {
3574        anyhow::bail!("KVM mount identities have no producer-captured namespace");
3575    }
3576    if config.mountinfo_mount_ids_captured {
3577        let Some(producer) = config.mountinfo_mount_namespace else {
3578            anyhow::bail!(
3579                "KVM producer-captured mount identities do not name their mount namespace"
3580            );
3581        };
3582        // Every mount namespace has its root, so a real one never yields an
3583        // empty order; and Detcore's pool refuses a malformed one.
3584        if config.mountinfo_mount_ids.is_empty()
3585            || !detcore_model::procfs::mount_identity_provenance_is_well_formed(
3586                &config.mountinfo_mount_ids,
3587                &config.mount_id_assignment_order,
3588            )
3589        {
3590            anyhow::bail!(
3591                "KVM producer-captured mount identities are malformed ({} listed, {} assigned)",
3592                config.mountinfo_mount_ids.len(),
3593                config.mount_id_assignment_order.len()
3594            );
3595        }
3596        if let Some(missing) = config
3597            .mountinfo_root_rewrites
3598            .iter()
3599            .map(|rewrite| rewrite.raw_mount_id)
3600            .find(|id| !config.mountinfo_mount_ids.contains(id))
3601        {
3602            anyhow::bail!(
3603                "KVM mount root rewrite names mount {missing}, which the producer's snapshot does \
3604                 not have"
3605            );
3606        }
3607        let backend = namespace().context("failed to identify the KVM backend mount namespace")?;
3608        if producer != backend {
3609            anyhow::bail!(
3610                "KVM producer-captured mount identities name another mount namespace \
3611                 (captured in {producer:?}, backend in {backend:?})"
3612            );
3613        }
3614    } else {
3615        let order = capture().context("failed to capture the KVM backend mount namespace")?;
3616        config.mountinfo_mount_ids = order;
3617        config.mountinfo_mount_ids_captured = true;
3618    }
3619    // The container mount table Detcore renders on KVM too names mounts of
3620    // this same namespace: refuse one built in another.
3621    if let Some(table) = &config.container_mount_table
3622        && let Some(missing) = table
3623            .mounts
3624            .iter()
3625            .map(|row| row.raw_mount_id)
3626            .find(|id| !config.mountinfo_mount_ids.contains(id))
3627    {
3628        anyhow::bail!(
3629            "KVM container mount table names mount {missing}, which the backend namespace does \
3630             not have"
3631        );
3632    }
3633    // The backend now exposes the actual namespace's devices. There is no
3634    // synthetic 0:1 root device to translate; stat and mountinfo use the same
3635    // raw identities before entering Detcore's shared DevicePool.
3636    config.mountinfo_device_rewrites.clear();
3637    Ok(())
3638}
3639
3640// AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
3641// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3695): Review
3642// host metadata timestamps for KVM runs.
3643/// Whether a KVM run declares to the backend that Detcore rewrites every
3644/// metadata timestamp (`set_host_metadata_timestamps`).
3645///
3646/// The backend reports the kernel's timestamps for host files in every run;
3647/// Detcore decides what the guest sees, and with virtual metadata it rewrites
3648/// every timestamp that a stat call returns and reads the stored host values
3649/// for its own checks (`set_file_times` confirms that `utimensat` stored the
3650/// requested mtime). The setting additionally makes the backend classify the
3651/// carriers it makes for its own data (virtual files, `/proc` snapshots, the
3652/// virtual signalfd's eventfd, the self-pidfd proxy) so that they keep fixed
3653/// timestamps through every alias; without it they report the carrier's
3654/// kernel timestamps. The backend refuses the setting unless Detcore owns
3655/// every guest thread, which `run_kvm` never opts out of. It is enabled only
3656/// with virtual metadata, so that something rewrites the timestamps, and with
3657/// sequentialized threads. The setting no longer decides whether another
3658/// guest thread can read a host file's kernel timestamps before Detcore
3659/// rewrites them: the backend reports them either way, and sequentialization
3660/// alone closes that window.
3661fn kvm_reports_stored_metadata_timestamps(config: &DetConfig) -> bool {
3662    config.virtualize_metadata && config.sequentialize_threads
3663}
3664
3665/// Dispatch a command onto the real reverie-kvm Tool runtime.
3666async fn run_kvm(
3667    command: &Command,
3668    mut config: DetConfig,
3669    print_summary: bool,
3670    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
3671    capture_output: bool,
3672) -> Result<Output, Error> {
3673    let dispatch_started = Instant::now();
3674    // A caller that built no container (a library caller): the KVM guest's
3675    // host file operations run in this process's namespace, whatever its
3676    // command asks (the backend applies no chroot or mount of the command),
3677    // so its table is this namespace's. A caller with no provenance at all
3678    // takes the order from the same read; malformed provenance is still
3679    // refused below.
3680    if config.container_mount_table.is_none() {
3681        let launch_cwd = command
3682            .get_current_dir()
3683            .map_or_else(|| Path::new(".").to_owned(), Path::to_owned);
3684        let (table, order) = unplanned_container_mount_table(&launch_cwd)?;
3685        if !config.mountinfo_mount_ids_captured
3686            && config.mountinfo_mount_ids.is_empty()
3687            && config.mount_id_assignment_order.is_empty()
3688            && config.mountinfo_mount_namespace.is_none()
3689        {
3690            config.mountinfo_mount_namespace = Some(current_mount_namespace()?);
3691            config.mountinfo_mount_ids = order;
3692            config.mountinfo_mount_ids_captured = true;
3693        }
3694        config.container_mount_table = Some(table);
3695    }
3696    let keep = config
3697        .container_mount_table
3698        .as_ref()
3699        .map(detcore_model::container_mounts::ContainerMountTable::shown_mount_ids)
3700        .unwrap_or_default();
3701    prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config(&mut config, current_mount_namespace, || {
3702        capture_mountinfo_identity_order_keeping(&keep)
3703    })?;
3704    let stdin = if capture_output {
3705        let (snapshot_reserved, snapshot) = output_backend_stdin_reservation()?;
3706        if snapshot_reserved {
3707            snapshot
3708        } else {
3709            // Public KVM output-capture callers do not pass through the CLI's
3710            // verify setup. Preserve their existing stdin behavior instead of
3711            // silently replacing it with /dev/null merely because output is
3712            // captured.
3713            reserved_kvm_stdin()?
3714        }
3715    } else {
3716        reserved_kvm_stdin()?
3717    };
3718    let requested_cwd = command
3719        .get_current_dir()
3720        .map(Path::to_owned)
3721        .unwrap_or(std::env::current_dir()?);
3722    let cwd = fs::canonicalize(&requested_cwd)
3723        .map_err(|error| kvm_cwd_resolution_error(&requested_cwd, &error))?;
3724    let program = command
3725        .get_program()
3726        .to_str()
3727        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("KVM guest executable path is not valid UTF-8"))?
3728        .to_owned();
3729    if !cwd.is_dir() {
3730        return Err(anyhow!(
3731            "KVM guest working directory is not a directory: {:?}",
3732            cwd
3733        ));
3734    }
3735    let resolved_program = command.find_program().map_err(|error| {
3736        anyhow!("failed to resolve KVM guest executable {program:?} in the guest PATH: {error}")
3737    })?;
3738    let mut argv = Vec::with_capacity(1 + command.get_args().count());
3739    argv.push(program.clone());
3740    for argument in command.get_args() {
3741        argv.push(
3742            argument
3743                .to_str()
3744                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("KVM guest argument is not valid UTF-8"))?
3745                .to_owned(),
3746        );
3747    }
3748
3749    // Rewrite `#!`-scripts to their interpreter before the ELF loader sees them.
3750    let (_interpreter_path, argv, image) = resolve_kvm_shebang(&resolved_program, argv)?;
3751    // After shebang resolution the executable is the interpreter (argv[0]).
3752    let program = argv.first().cloned().unwrap_or(program);
3753    let envp = command
3754        .get_captured_envs()
3755        .into_iter()
3756        .map(|(key, value)| {
3757            let key = key
3758                .to_str()
3759                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("KVM guest environment key is not valid UTF-8"))?;
3760            let value = value
3761                .to_str()
3762                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("KVM guest environment value is not valid UTF-8"))?;
3763            Ok(format!("{key}={value}"))
3764        })
3765        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, Error>>()?;
3766    tracing::info!(
3767        target: "hermit::kvm",
3768        program = %program,
3769        argv = ?argv,
3770        cwd = %cwd.display(),
3771        env_count = envp.len(),
3772        "launching guest through reverie-kvm",
3773    );
3774    let argv = argv.iter().map(String::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>();
3775    let envp = envp.iter().map(String::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>();
3776
3777    let setup_started = Instant::now();
3778    // `prepare_backend_config` already copied `KvmBackend::capabilities()`,
3779    // which reports the backend's own CPUID table and that, of the madvise
3780    // advice with guest-visible semantics, it implements only MADV_DONTNEED.
3781    // KVM does not enter Hermit's UTS namespace, so Detcore must provide the
3782    // same synthetic identity that the namespace-backed ptrace path exposes.
3783    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-998): Review KVM UTS namespace parity.
3784    config.has_uts_namespace = false;
3785    let mut backend = reverie_kvm::KvmBackend::new_with_stdin(KVM_GUEST_MEMORY_BYTES, stdin)
3786        .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to initialize reverie-kvm: {error}"))?;
3787    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
3788    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1120): Review KVM's canonical Detcore root identity.
3789    backend
3790        .set_root_pid(detcore::ROOT_DETPID.as_raw())
3791        .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to configure KVM root PID: {error}"))?;
3792    // Guests see their task IDs, so number them as the ptrace reference does
3793    // (one extra ID per task for its tracer thread; see reverie::task_ids).
3794    backend
3795        .set_ids_per_task(reverie::task_ids::HERMIT_PTRACE_IDS_PER_TASK)
3796        .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to configure KVM task IDs: {error}"))?;
3797    // The ptrace launcher execs the path `find_program` resolved, so that is
3798    // the filename Linux records in AT_EXECFN and copies to the top of the
3799    // stack, including for a `#!` script whose argv now starts with the
3800    // interpreter.
3801    backend
3802        .install_static_elf_with_exec_context(
3803            &image,
3804            resolved_program.as_os_str(),
3805            &argv,
3806            &envp,
3807            &cwd,
3808        )
3809        .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to load KVM guest executable {program:?}: {error}"))?;
3810    // The loader has copied the image's segments into guest memory, so the
3811    // file's bytes are no longer needed. Holding them until the run ends kept
3812    // a second copy of the program in host memory for the whole run: 75 MB
3813    // for node (https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/1063).
3814    drop(image);
3815    // The KVM backend defaults to Tool-owned guest threads: CLONE_THREAD
3816    // workers are driven through the Detcore tool loop and their futex/CLEARTID
3817    // synchronization routes to Detcore, matching the golden ptrace model
3818    // ("follow children"). Detcore registers every cloned thread as a tool
3819    // thread (detcore/src/syscalls/threads.rs), so the backend must stay in
3820    // that mode: host-owned threads would split worker execution and futex
3821    // ownership across two synchronization domains, which deadlocks
3822    // pthread_join.
3823    if kvm_reports_stored_metadata_timestamps(&config) {
3824        backend
3825            .set_host_metadata_timestamps(true)
3826            .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to configure KVM metadata timestamps: {error}"))?;
3827    }
3828
3829    let execution_started = Instant::now();
3830    let completion = hermit_run_kvm::run_detcore(&mut backend, config, capture_output)
3831        .await
3832        .map_err(|error| kvm_execution_error(error, None))?;
3833    let cleanup_started = Instant::now();
3834    let result =
3835        finish_kvm_tool_completion(completion, print_summary, print_summary_to_json_file).await;
3836    let teardown_started = Instant::now();
3837    // Drop explicitly so the host's KVM VM teardown cost remains observable.
3838    drop(backend);
3839    let teardown_finished = Instant::now();
3840    let (status, stdout, stderr) = result?;
3841
3842    // Every field below is a host wall-clock duration. Keep this diagnostic at
3843    // DEBUG so it remains available for backend profiling without entering the
3844    // INFO stream exposed to canonical comparison. KVM's built-in verification
3845    // is still output/status-only; this classification does not claim KVM L2.
3846    tracing::debug!(
3847        target: "hermit::kvm",
3848        prepare_us = setup_started.duration_since(dispatch_started).as_micros() as u64,
3849        setup_us = execution_started.duration_since(setup_started).as_micros() as u64,
3850        execution_us = cleanup_started.duration_since(execution_started).as_micros() as u64,
3851        cleanup_us = teardown_started.duration_since(cleanup_started).as_micros() as u64,
3852        teardown_us = teardown_finished.duration_since(teardown_started).as_micros() as u64,
3853        lifecycle_us = teardown_finished.duration_since(dispatch_started).as_micros() as u64,
3854        "reverie-kvm lifecycle phase timings",
3855    );
3856
3857    if !capture_output {
3858        std::io::stdout().write_all(&stdout)?;
3859        std::io::stderr().write_all(&stderr)?;
3860    }
3861
3862    Ok(Output {
3863        status,
3864        stdout,
3865        stderr,
3866    })
3867}
3868
3869// A runtime error still owns GlobalState. Finish its terminal daemon before
3870// returning the typed cause to the CLI's error classifier.
3871async fn finish_kvm_tool_completion(
3872    completion: reverie_kvm::ToolRunCompletion<detcore::GlobalState>,
3873    print_summary: bool,
3874    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
3875) -> Result<(ExitStatus, Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>), Error> {
3876    match completion.result {
3877        Ok(output) => {
3878            completion
3879                .global_state
3880                .clean_up(print_summary, print_summary_to_json_file)
3881                .await?;
3882            Ok(output)
3883        }
3884        Err(error) => {
3885            let cleanup = completion
3886                .global_state
3887                .clean_up_after_backend_failure()
3888                .await;
3889            Err(kvm_execution_error(error, Some(cleanup)))
3890        }
3891    }
3892}
3893
3894fn kvm_execution_error(
3895    primary: reverie_kvm::Error,
3896    cleanup: Option<detcore::BackendFailureCleanup>,
3897) -> Error {
3898    // The manifest runner retains the first Error line. Keep the cause there,
3899    // as well as the typed backend and optional scheduler errors in the chain.
3900    let message = format!("KVM guest execution failed: {primary}");
3901    let mut error = Error::new(primary).context(BackendRunFailure);
3902    if let Some(cleanup) = cleanup {
3903        if let Err(recording) = cleanup.preemption_recording {
3904            error = error.context(format!("partial preemption recording failed: {recording}"));
3905        }
3906        if let Err(scheduler) = cleanup.scheduler {
3907            error = error.context(scheduler);
3908        }
3909    }
3910    error.context(message)
3911}

3921fn dbt_client_thread_start_failed(status: &std::process::ExitStatus) -> bool {
3922    status.code() == Some(reverie_dbt::CLIENT_THREAD_START_FAILURE_EXIT_CODE)

3925/// Keys that `HERMIT_DBT_DETCONFIG` still carries although [`DetConfig`] no
3926/// longer has the switches they named. Each entry is the key, its fixed value,
3927/// and the key it preceded in the old field order.
3928///
3929/// These are serialization constants. Nothing reads them back: the admitted
3930/// DBT standalone path decodes the variable with
3931/// [`detcore::decode_backend_config_json`], whose legacy reader ignores these
3932/// keys. The values are the only ones the deleted switches ever took on any
3933/// backend.
3934const LEGACY_DBT_DETCONFIG_KEYS: [(&str, bool, &str); 3] = [
3935    (
3936        "use_thread_local_clock_reads",
3937        false,
3938        "detect_host_clock_futex_timeouts",
3939    ),
3940    (
3941        "backend_serializes_fork_children",
3942        false,
3943        "backend_tracks_process_children",
3944    ),
3945    (
3946        "backend_dispatches_thread_tools",
3947        true,
3948        "backend_tracks_process_children",
3949    ),
3950];
3951
3952/// Serialize `config` for the DBT runtime's `HERMIT_DBT_DETCONFIG` variable.
3953///
3954/// This is not plain `serde_json::to_string` because the variable sits in the
3955/// guest's own environment. A guest can read it through `getenv`, `printenv`
3956/// or `/proc/self/environ`, so its bytes are guest-visible. Two later changes
3957/// to [`DetConfig`] would otherwise have changed what every DBT guest
3958/// observes, and each is undone here:
3959///
3960/// - The backend facts moved into [`DetConfig::backend`].
3961///   [`detcore::to_legacy_backend_json`] writes them back out as the fifteen
3962///   separate keys they were, at the position the object carried them.
3963/// - Three always-constant switches were deleted, which would have shortened
3964///   the variable by 117 bytes. The keys in `LEGACY_DBT_DETCONFIG_KEYS` are
3965///   re-inserted at their old positions.
3966///
3967/// When the legacy keys express every backend capability exactly, the output
3968/// is byte-identical to what the same config produced before either change.
3969/// That is pinned by golden bytes in the tests below. Otherwise a versioned
3970/// envelope carries the exact capabilities alongside the legacy config.
3971///
3972/// Coordinated DBT startup receives the authoritative typed Config through the
3973/// RPC handshake. This JSON remains guest-visible and supplies the admitted
3974/// standalone fallback, so its representable bytes still need preservation.
3975/// Remove this shim only when that variable no longer reaches the guest.
3976#[doc(hidden)]
3977pub fn dbt_detconfig_json(config: &DetConfig) -> serde_json::Result<String> {
3978    let legacy = insert_legacy_dbt_detconfig_keys(&detcore::to_legacy_backend_json(config)?)?;
3979    detcore::encode_backend_config_json(legacy, config.backend)
3980}
3981
3982/// Re-insert [`LEGACY_DBT_DETCONFIG_KEYS`] into a serialized [`DetConfig`].
3983///
3984/// The insertion works on the parsed top-level object, never on substrings,
3985/// so string values that happen to contain a key name cannot move it. It
3986/// refuses, rather than guessing, when an anchor key is missing or repeated or
3987/// when a legacy key is already present.
3988fn insert_legacy_dbt_detconfig_keys(serialized: &str) -> serde_json::Result<String> {
3989    use serde::de::MapAccess;
3990    use serde::ser::Error as _;
3991    use serde::ser::SerializeMap;
3992    use serde_json::value::RawValue;
3993
3994    /// The top-level members of a JSON object in document order, each value
3995    /// kept as its exact serialized bytes.
3996    struct Members<'a>(Vec<(&'a str, &'a RawValue)>);
3997
3998    impl<'de> serde::Deserialize<'de> for Members<'de> {
3999        fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
4000            struct MembersVisitor;
4001            impl<'de> serde::de::Visitor<'de> for MembersVisitor {
4002                type Value = Members<'de>;
4003                fn expecting(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
4004                    formatter.write_str("a serialized Detcore config object")
4005                }
4006                fn visit_map<A: MapAccess<'de>>(self, mut map: A) -> Result<Self::Value, A::Error> {
4007                    let mut members = Vec::new();
4008                    while let Some(member) = map.next_entry()? {
4009                        members.push(member);
4010                    }
4011                    Ok(Members(members))
4012                }
4013            }
4014            deserializer.deserialize_map(MembersVisitor)
4015        }
4016    }
4017
4018    impl serde::Serialize for Members<'_> {
4019        fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
4020            let mut map = serializer.serialize_map(None)?;
4021            for (key, value) in &self.0 {
4022                for (legacy_key, fixed_value, anchor) in LEGACY_DBT_DETCONFIG_KEYS {
4023                    if anchor == *key {
4024                        map.serialize_entry(legacy_key, &fixed_value)?;
4025                    }
4026                }
4027                map.serialize_entry(key, value)?;
4028            }
4029            map.end()
4030        }
4031    }
4032
4033    let members: Members<'_> = serde_json::from_str(serialized)?;
4034    for (legacy_key, _, anchor) in LEGACY_DBT_DETCONFIG_KEYS {
4035        let anchors = members.0.iter().filter(|(key, _)| *key == anchor).count();
4036        if anchors != 1 {
4037            return Err(serde_json::Error::custom(format!(
4038                "cannot place legacy DBT config key {legacy_key:?}: its anchor key {anchor:?} \
4039                 appears {anchors} times, expected exactly once"
4040            )));
4041        }
4042        if members.0.iter().any(|(key, _)| *key == legacy_key) {
4043            return Err(serde_json::Error::custom(format!(
4044                "legacy DBT config key {legacy_key:?} is already present; it must come only \
4045                 from the fixed legacy table"
4046            )));
4047        }
4048    }
4049    serde_json::to_string(&members)
4050}

4052#[cfg(test)]
4053mod dbt_detconfig_tests {
4054    use std::path::PathBuf;
4055
4056    use clap::Parser;
4057    use detcore_model::config::MountInfoRootRewrite;
4058
4059    use super::Backend;
4060    use super::DetConfig;
4061    use super::dbt_detconfig_json;
4062    use super::insert_legacy_dbt_detconfig_keys;
4063    use super::prepare_backend_config;
4064
4065    /// `HERMIT_DBT_DETCONFIG` bytes for each config below, captured with
4066    /// `serde_json::to_string` from a build of
4067    /// 806cf2fa38d13b806195d54aeba22d282d79f33d, which still had the legacy
4068    /// switches. Any later change to `DetConfig`'s serialized fields also
4069    /// changes this guest-visible variable, so this test is meant to fail on
4070    /// it and make that change a deliberate one.
4071    ///
4072    /// Two deliberate changes since that capture: the empty
4073    /// `fdinfo_unlisted_mount_ids` key was renamed `mount_id_assignment_order`
4074    /// when Detcore began numbering mount IDs in first-observation order
4075    /// (RECORD_VERSION 0x122), and the `proc_level` key was added by the
4076    /// `/proc` levels (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4266), whose
4077    /// default is `Minimal`. Every other byte is the 806cf2fa output.
4078    const GOLDEN: [(&str, &str); 3] = [
4079        (
4080            "default",
4081            include_str!("../tests/fixtures/dbt/detconfig-806cf2fa-default.json"),
4082        ),
4083        (
4084            "dbt",
4085            include_str!("../tests/fixtures/dbt/detconfig-806cf2fa-dbt.json"),
4086        ),
4087        (
4088            "rich_dbt",
4089            include_str!("../tests/fixtures/dbt/detconfig-806cf2fa-rich_dbt.json"),
4090        ),
4091    ];
4092
4093    /// `Config::default()` with its three environment-backed fields
4094    /// (`HERMIT_EPOCH`, `HERMIT_PRNG`, `HERMIT_SCHED_SEED`) pinned, so the
4095    /// result does not depend on the test process's environment.
4096    fn env_free(epoch: &str, seed: &str) -> DetConfig {
4097        let mut config = DetConfig::parse_from(["hermit", epoch, seed, "--sched-seed=0"]);
4098        config.sched_seed = None;
4099        config
4100    }
4101
4102    fn default_config() -> DetConfig {
4103        env_free("--epoch=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", "--seed=0")
4104    }
4105
4106    /// Non-default values in fields that serialize as strings, floats,
4107    /// options, and nested arrays. The path holds legacy anchor key names, so
4108    /// a substring-based insertion would put a key inside a string value.
4109    fn rich_config() -> DetConfig {
4110        let mut config = env_free("--epoch=2000-12-31T23:59:59Z", "--seed=7");
4111        config.rng_seed = Some(13);
4112        config.sched_seed = Some(11);
4113        config.clock_multiplier = Some(1.5);
4114        config.chaos = true;
4115        config.record_preemptions_to = Some(PathBuf::from(
4116            "/tmp/a,\"detect_host_clock_futex_timeouts\":true,\"backend_tracks_process_children\":{",
4117        ));
4118        config.mountinfo_root_rewrites = vec![MountInfoRootRewrite {
4119            raw_mount_id: 41,
4120            deterministic_root: b"/".to_vec(),
4121            raw_root_prefix: Some(b"/tmp/x".to_vec()),
4122            deterministic_root_prefix: Some(b"/tmp".to_vec()),
4123            raw_mountpoint_prefix: None,
4124            deterministic_mountpoint_prefix: None,
4125        }];
4126        config.stacktrace_event = vec![(3, Some(PathBuf::from("/s")))];
4127        config
4128    }
4129
4130    fn cases() -> [(&'static str, DetConfig); 3] {
4131        [
4132            ("default", default_config()),
4133            (
4134                "dbt",
4135                prepare_backend_config(default_config(), Backend::Dbt),
4136            ),
4137            (
4138                "rich_dbt",
4139                prepare_backend_config(rich_config(), Backend::Dbt),
4140            ),
4141        ]
4142    }
4143
4144    #[test]
4145    fn default_case_is_config_default_with_pinned_environment_fields() {
4146        let pinned = default_config();
4147        let from_default = DetConfig {
4148            epoch: pinned.epoch,
4149            seed: pinned.seed,
4150            sched_seed: pinned.sched_seed,
4151            ..DetConfig::default()
4152        };
4153        assert_eq!(
4154            serde_json::to_string(&from_default).unwrap(),
4155            serde_json::to_string(&pinned).unwrap()
4156        );
4157    }
4158
4159    #[test]
4160    fn dbt_detconfig_matches_806cf2fa_bytes() {
4161        for ((name, mut config), (golden_name, golden)) in cases().into_iter().zip(GOLDEN) {
4162            // Keep the historical capability value as well as its byte oracle.
4163            // Current DBT descriptor facts need the versioned transport below.
4164            config.backend.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table = false;
4165            config.backend.rediscovers_descriptors_after_exec = false;
4166            // These three were `Config` fields, false unless the host set them
4167            // for the backend, until they became stated capabilities.
4168            config.backend.supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption = false;
4169            config.backend.delivers_preemption_timer_events = false;
4170            config.backend.runs_guest_code_between_injections = false;
4171            assert_eq!(name, golden_name);
4172            let encoded = dbt_detconfig_json(&config).unwrap();
4173            assert_eq!(
4174                encoded, golden,
4175                "HERMIT_DBT_DETCONFIG for the {name} config differs from the 806cf2fa bytes"
4176            );
4177        }
4178    }
4179
4180    /// The DBT standalone fallback decodes the variable with
4181    /// `detcore::decode_backend_config_json` and falls back to its default
4182    /// config on a parse error. The three deleted switches' keys must be
4183    /// accepted and ignored, and the fifteen backend keys must decode back to
4184    /// the backend facts, so the runtime sees exactly the config that was
4185    /// encoded.
4186    #[test]
4187    fn dbt_detconfig_decodes_to_the_encoded_config() {
4188        for (name, config) in cases() {
4189            let encoded = dbt_detconfig_json(&config).unwrap();
4190            let decoded = detcore::decode_backend_config_json(&encoded)
4191                .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{name}: DBT config does not decode: {error}"));
4192            assert_eq!(
4193                serde_json::to_string(&decoded).unwrap(),
4194                serde_json::to_string(&config).unwrap(),
4195                "{name}: decoded config differs from the encoded one"
4196            );
4197        }
4198    }

4210        assert_eq!(decoded.backend, reverie::BackendCapabilities::DBT);

4214    #[test]

4218        // opt into host-timed turns or loopback poller yielding.
4219        for mask in 0_u8..16 {

4229                "only coupled facts fit the legacy form: mask {mask}"
4230            );

4257    #[test]
4258    fn versioned_dbt_config_rejects_unknown_or_malformed_envelopes() {
4259        let config = prepare_backend_config(default_config(), Backend::Dbt);
4260        let legacy =
4261            insert_legacy_dbt_detconfig_keys(&detcore::to_legacy_backend_json(&config).unwrap())
4262                .unwrap();
4263        let legacy_backend = detcore::from_legacy_backend_json(&legacy).unwrap().backend;
4264        let backend = serde_json::to_string(&config.backend).unwrap();
4265        let envelope = |version: &str| {
4266            format!(
4267                "{{\"dbt_config_version\":{version},\"config\":{legacy},\"backend\":{backend}}}"
4268            )
4269        };
4270        for version in ["0", "2", "-1", "null", "\"1\""] {
4271            assert!(
4272                detcore::decode_backend_config_json(&envelope(version)).is_err(),
4273                "version {version} must be refused"
4274            );
4275            let tagged_legacy =
4276                legacy.replacen('{', &format!("{{\"dbt_config_version\":{version},"), 1);
4277            assert_eq!(
4278                detcore::decode_backend_config_json(&tagged_legacy)
4279                    .unwrap()
4280                    .backend,
4281                legacy_backend,
4282                "an unknown legacy key must remain ignored"
4283            );
4284        }
4285        let duplicate = format!(
4286            "{{\"dbt_config_version\":1,\"dbt_config_version\":1,\"config\":{legacy},\"backend\":{backend}}}"
4287        );
4288        assert!(detcore::decode_backend_config_json(&duplicate).is_err());
4289        let missing_backend = format!("{{\"dbt_config_version\":1,\"config\":{legacy}}}");
4290        assert!(detcore::decode_backend_config_json(&missing_backend).is_err());
4291        let missing_config = format!("{{\"dbt_config_version\":1,\"backend\":{backend}}}");
4292        assert!(detcore::decode_backend_config_json(&missing_config).is_err());
4293        for duplicate in [
4294            format!("\"config\":{legacy}"),
4295            format!("\"backend\":{backend}"),
4296            "\"unknown\":true".to_owned(),
4297        ] {
4298            let json = envelope("1").replacen('{', &format!("{{{duplicate},"), 1);
4299            assert!(detcore::decode_backend_config_json(&json).is_err());
4300        }
4301    }

4340/// The program a DBT launch runs and the working directory it runs from, as
4341/// reverie-dbt's launcher finds them: a name without a `/` through `path`,
4342/// whose relative entries are taken from the guest's working directory;
4343/// `cwd` relative to `current` (the launcher's own directory) when it is
4344/// relative, and `current` when there is none. `None` where the search finds
4345/// no executable file.
4346#[cfg(feature = "dbt")]
4347fn dbt_launched_program(
4348    program: &std::path::Path,
4349    cwd: Option<&std::path::Path>,
4350    path: Option<&std::ffi::OsStr>,
4351    current: &std::path::Path,
4352) -> Option<(PathBuf, PathBuf)> {
4353    use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
4354    use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
4355    let cwd = cwd.map_or_else(|| current.to_owned(), |cwd| current.join(cwd));
4356    let spelled = if program.as_os_str().as_bytes().contains(&b'/') {
4357        program.to_owned()
4358    } else {
4359        std::env::split_paths(path?)
4360            .map(|directory| cwd.join(directory).join(program))
4361            .find(|candidate| {
4362                candidate.metadata().is_ok_and(|metadata| {
4363                    metadata.is_file() && metadata.permissions().mode() & 0o111 != 0
4364                })
4365            })?
4366    };
4367    Some((spelled, cwd))
4368}
4369
4370#[cfg(all(test, feature = "dbt"))]
4371mod dbt_launched_program_tests {
4372    use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
4373
4374    use super::*;
4375
4376    fn executable(path: &std::path::Path) {
4377        std::fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
4378        std::fs::write(path, b"").unwrap();
4379        std::fs::set_permissions(path, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755)).unwrap();
4380    }
4381
4382    #[test]
4383    fn a_relative_path_entry_is_taken_from_the_guests_directory_not_the_launchers() {
4384        let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
4385        let launcher_dir = root.path().join("launcher");
4386        // A decoy where the launcher's own directory would find it, and the
4387        // program where the guest's directory does.
4388        executable(&launcher_dir.join("bin/prog"));
4389        executable(&root.path().join("guest/bin/prog"));
4390        std::fs::write(root.path().join("guest/plain"), b"").unwrap();
4391        let path = std::ffi::OsStr::new("bin");
4392        let found = |program: &str, cwd: Option<&str>| {
4393            dbt_launched_program(
4394                std::path::Path::new(program),
4395                cwd.map(std::path::Path::new),
4396                Some(path),
4397                &launcher_dir,
4398            )
4399        };
4400        let guest = root.path().join("guest");
4401        // An absolute and a relative working directory find the same file.
4402        let expected = Some((guest.join("bin/prog"), guest.clone()));
4403        assert_eq!(found("prog", Some(guest.to_str().unwrap())), expected);
4404        assert_eq!(
4405            found("prog", Some("../guest")),
4406            Some((
4407                launcher_dir.join("../guest/bin/prog"),
4408                launcher_dir.join("../guest")
4409            ))
4410        );
4411        // Without a working directory, the launcher's own is the guest's.
4412        assert_eq!(
4413            found("prog", None),
4414            Some((launcher_dir.join("bin/prog"), launcher_dir.clone()))
4415        );
4416        // A name with a `/` is not searched for.
4417        assert_eq!(
4418            found("./plain", Some(guest.to_str().unwrap())),
4419            Some((std::path::PathBuf::from("./plain"), guest.clone()))
4420        );
4421        // A file that is not executable is not found.
4422        assert_eq!(found("plain", Some(guest.to_str().unwrap())), None);
4423    }
4424}
