4426/// Records, for a DBT run, the guest's first image: `program`, found and
4427/// run from `cwd` with the guest's `PATH`, `path`, as the launch finds it
4428/// (`dbt_launched_program`), then resolved as the kernel resolves an
4429/// `execve`. Both DBT launch paths call it in the container, whose root is
4430/// the guest's, in place of `launched_image`'s search, which takes a
4431/// relative `PATH` entry from the coordinator's directory rather than the
4432/// guest's. Where nothing is found the record stays unset, and the image's
4433/// own `AT_EXECFN` gives it after the exec.
4434#[cfg(feature = "dbt")]
4435pub fn record_dbt_launched_image(
4436    config: &mut DetConfig,
4437    program: &std::path::Path,
4438    cwd: Option<&std::path::Path>,
4439    path: Option<&std::ffi::OsStr>,
4440) {
4441    let exe = std::env::current_dir()
4442        .ok()
4443        .and_then(|current| dbt_launched_program(program, cwd, path, &current))
4444        .and_then(|(spelled, cwd)| {
4445            detcore::exec_record::ExecRecord::resolve(std::path::Path::new("/"), &cwd, &spelled)
4446        })
4447        .map(|record| record.exe);
4448    config
4449        .launch_image
4450        .get_or_insert(detcore::LaunchImage {
4451            exe: None,
4452            launcher: None,
4453        })
4454        .exe = exe;
4455}
4456
4457/// Declares, for a DBT run through `drrun`, the image the kernel execs in the
4458/// guest's place: DynamoRIO's library (`lib64/release/libdynamorio.so` beside
4459/// `drrun`'s `bin64`), which loads the guest itself. So the kernel's `exe`
4460/// link and program break are DynamoRIO's (`detcore::LaunchImage::launcher`),
4461/// and Detcore answers the guest's brk from its own model; the runner tells
4462/// DynamoRIO to reserve nothing for the break
4463/// (`reverie_dbt::DbtRunner::tool_answers_brk`).
4464/// An error where that library is missing: the run would otherwise
4465/// declare a launcher the kernel never execs, and refuse every brk for want
4466/// of a record the launcher check can accept.
4467#[cfg(feature = "dbt")]
4468pub fn declare_dbt_launcher(config: &mut DetConfig, drrun: &std::path::Path) -> Result<(), Error> {
4469    let library = drrun
4470        .parent()
4471        .and_then(std::path::Path::parent)
4472        .unwrap_or(std::path::Path::new("/"))
4473        .join("lib64/release/libdynamorio.so");
4474    if !library.is_file() {
4475        return Err(anyhow!(
4476            "DynamoRIO's library is not at {} beside drrun {}",
4477            library.display(),
4478            drrun.display()
4479        ));
4480    }
4481    config
4482        .launch_image
4483        .get_or_insert(detcore::LaunchImage {
4484            exe: None,
4485            launcher: None,
4486        })
4487        .launcher = Some(library);
4488    Ok(())
4489}
4490
4491// AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
4492// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-737): Review public DBT dispatch and child environment ownership.
4493/// Dispatch a command onto the Detcore-linked reverie-dbt runtime.
4494#[cfg(feature = "dbt")]
4495async fn run_dbt(
4496    command: Command,
4497    config: DetConfig,
4498    print_summary: bool,
4499    capture_output: bool,
4500) -> Result<Output, Error> {
4501    if !config.sequentialize_threads {
4502        return Err(anyhow!(
4503            "the dbt backend requires sequentialized threads; remove \
4504             --no-sequentialize-threads (or --strace-only) to run under --backend dbt"
4505        ));
4506    }
4507
4508    // The guest sees this string in its environment, so it keeps the encoding
4509    // it had before the backend facts moved into `Config::backend` and before
4510    // three constant switches were deleted; see `dbt_detconfig_json`. The DBT
4511    // runtime decodes the backend facts back out of it (here DBT's own); when
4512    // the string is absent or does not parse, it uses the strict default's
4513    // facts, which are ptrace's.
4514    let (drrun, client) = detcore_dbt::prepare_native_client()
4515        .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to prepare the Detcore DynamoRIO client: {error}"))?;
4516    let mut config = config;
4517    declare_dbt_launcher(&mut config, &drrun)?;
4518    record_dbt_launched_image(
4519        &mut config,
4520        std::path::Path::new(command.get_program()),
4521        command.get_current_dir(),
4522        command
4523            .get_captured_envs()
4524            .get(std::ffi::OsStr::new("PATH"))
4525            .map(std::ffi::OsString::as_os_str),
4526    );
4527    let config_json = dbt_detconfig_json(&config)
4528        .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to serialize the Detcore config for DBT: {error}"))?;
4529    let panic_on_unsupported_syscalls = config.panic_on_unsupported_syscalls;
4530    // Bind native diagnostics to the controller before guest output capture.
4531    let diagnostics = std::fs::File::from(
4532        std::io::stderr()
4533            .as_fd()
4534            .try_clone_to_owned()
4535            .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to retain DBT diagnostic stderr: {error}"))?,
4536    );
4537    let mut runner = reverie_dbt::DbtRunner::new(&drrun, &client)
4538        .map_err(|error| {
4539            anyhow!(
4540                "failed to configure the DynamoRIO DBT runner (drrun={}, client={}): {error}",
4541                drrun.display(),
4542                client.display()
4543            )
4544        })?
4545        .summary(print_summary)
4546        .isolated_process_group(panic_on_unsupported_syscalls)
4547        .tool_answers_brk(true)
4548        .diagnostic_file(&diagnostics)
4549        .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to configure DBT diagnostic stderr: {error}"))?;
4550    drop(diagnostics);
4551    if panic_on_unsupported_syscalls {
4552        runner = runner.client_argument("-panic-on-unsupported-syscalls");
4553    }
4554
4555    let program = command.get_program().to_owned();
4556    let mut environment = command.get_captured_envs();
4557    environment.insert(detcore_dbt::DETCONFIG_ENV.into(), config_json.into());
4558    let guest = command.into_std_lossy();
4559    tracing::info!(
4560        target: "hermit::dbt",
4561        program = ?program,
4562        drrun = %drrun.display(),
4563        client = %client.display(),
4564        "launching guest through reverie-dbt with Detcore<DbtGuest>",
4565    );
4566
4567    let (status, stdout, stderr, mut global) = if capture_output {
4568        let launch = || {
4569            runner.output_with_environment_and_global::<detcore::GlobalState>(
4570                &guest,
4571                &environment,
4572                config.clone(),
4573            )
4574        };
4575        let (mut output, mut global) = launch()
4576            .await
4577            .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to launch drrun ({}): {error}", drrun.display()))?;
4578        if dbt_client_thread_start_failed(&output.status) {
4579            tracing::warn!(
4580                target: "hermit::dbt",
4581                "DynamoRIO client thread failed before guest start; retrying once",
4582            );
4583            global.force_shutdown_with_error();
4584            global.cancel_internal_scheduler().await;
4585            global.clean_up(false, &None).await.map_err(|error| {
4586                error.context(format!(
4587                    "DBT cleanup after observed guest status {:?}",
4588                    output.status
4589                ))
4590            })?;
4591            (output, global) = launch().await.map_err(|error| {
4592                anyhow!("failed to launch drrun ({}): {error}", drrun.display())
4593            })?;
4594        }
4595        (output.status, output.stdout, output.stderr, global)
4596    } else {
4597        let launch = || {
4598            runner.status_with_environment_and_global::<detcore::GlobalState>(
4599                &guest,
4600                &environment,
4601                config.clone(),
4602            )
4603        };
4604        let (mut status, mut global) = launch()
4605            .await
4606            .map_err(|error| anyhow!("failed to launch drrun ({}): {error}", drrun.display()))?;
4607        if dbt_client_thread_start_failed(&status) {
4608            tracing::warn!(
4609                target: "hermit::dbt",
4610                "DynamoRIO client thread failed before guest start; retrying once",
4611            );
4612            global.force_shutdown_with_error();
4613            global.cancel_internal_scheduler().await;
4614            global.clean_up(false, &None).await.map_err(|error| {
4615                error.context(format!(
4616                    "DBT cleanup after observed guest status {status:?}"
4617                ))
4618            })?;
4619            (status, global) = launch().await.map_err(|error| {
4620                anyhow!("failed to launch drrun ({}): {error}", drrun.display())
4621            })?;
4622        }
4623        (status, Vec::new(), Vec::new(), global)
4624    };
4625
4626    if !status.success() {
4627        global.force_shutdown_with_error();
4628        global.cancel_internal_scheduler().await;
4629    }
4630    global
4631        .clean_up(print_summary, &None)
4632        .await
4633        .map_err(|error| {
4634            error.context(format!(
4635                "DBT cleanup after observed guest status {status:?}"
4636            ))
4637        })?;
4638    Ok(Output {
4639        status: status.into(),
4640        stdout,
4641        stderr,
4642    })
4643}
4644
4645// NOTE: A single-threaded executor is used here so that the tokio threads
4646// themselves wouldn't contribute non-determinism to the PID namespace. This
4647// could also be changed to a specific number of threads and that would be
4648// deterministic, but it shouldn't be based on the number of cores. When the
4649// thread count is based off of the number of cores in the machine, then two
4650// runs on different machines with a different number of cores will not be the
4651// same.
4652/// Run the given command as deterministically as possible.
4653///
4654/// # Stack size
4655///
4656/// On the ptrace backend this and the other launch functions (`run*`,
4657/// `record*`, `replay*`, [`HermitData::record`]) run the whole ptrace session
4658/// on a tracer thread of their own, with an 8 MiB stack (the main thread's
4659/// usual size, the default `ulimit -s`), so the calling thread needs no
4660/// particular stack: a recording through the library returned on a 95 KiB
4661/// caller thread. One tracer thread serves each calling thread for the
4662/// caller's lifetime, so an operation kept at a [`HermitCleanupUnconfirmed`]
4663/// checkpoint is resumed from the same caller. That thread stays, idle, until
4664/// the caller exits, and a tracing subscriber set for the calling thread only
4665/// does not see the session's events (a global subscriber does). The session itself, in a debug
4666/// build, needs about 2 MiB, mostly Detcore's syscall handler, which at
4667/// opt-level 0 keeps every syscall arm's temporaries in one frame
4668/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4389>).
4669///
4670/// The other backends still run on the calling thread, which then needs that
4671/// stack itself: launching from a thread spawned with 4 MiB
4672/// (`std::thread::Builder::stack_size`) is recommended for them, and Rust's
4673/// default 2 MiB for a spawned thread or a test is not enough in a debug build
4674/// with the `third-party-backends` feature. Optimised builds need much less:
4675/// in the `validate` profile a 512 KiB thread was enough.
4676pub fn run(
4677    command: Command,
4678    config: DetConfig,
4679    print_summary: bool,
4680    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
4681) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
4682    run_with_backend(
4683        command,
4684        config,
4685        print_summary,
4686        print_summary_to_json_file,
4687        Backend::Ptrace,
4688    )
4689}
4690
4691/// Run the given command using the selected instrumentation backend.
4692///
4693/// On ptrace it needs no particular stack from the calling thread; see [`run`].
4694pub fn run_with_backend(
4695    command: Command,
4696    config: DetConfig,
4697    print_summary: bool,
4698    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
4699    backend: Backend,
4700) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
4701    run_with_backend_timeout(
4702        command,
4703        config,
4704        print_summary,
4705        print_summary_to_json_file,
4706        backend,
4707        None,
4708    )
4709}
4710
4711/// [`run_with_backend`] with a hermit-enforced wall-clock bound on the guest.
4712///
4713/// On ptrace it needs no particular stack from the calling thread; see [`run`].
4714///
4715/// This library never installs a process alarm. Ordinary ptrace keeps the
4716/// original runtime, operation, failed GlobalState and backing guards when a
4717/// finite cleanup attempt is unconfirmed; downcast [`HermitCleanupUnconfirmed`]
4718/// and recover it on the original process/thread. A timeout is measured before
4719/// startup and is not a certificate of cleanup. `None` leaves execution
4720/// unbounded, but fatal cleanup attempts remain finite. Nonordinary backends
4721/// retain their existing cooperative timeout/drop semantics. Synchronous stalls
4722/// require caller-owned supervision; only the CLI owns its hard alarm fallback.
4723///
4724/// ⚠️ NOT PART OF `DetConfig`, DELIBERATELY. A wall-clock bound is host state,
4725/// and `DetConfig` is the determinism configuration that is serialized to disk
4726/// and reasoned about as guest-visible. Threading a real-time deadline through
4727/// it would put a nondeterministic quantity inside the structure whose entire
4728/// job is to exclude them.
4729pub fn run_with_backend_timeout(
4730    command: Command,
4731    config: DetConfig,
4732    print_summary: bool,
4733    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
4734    backend: Backend,
4735    timeout: Option<Duration>,
4736) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
4737    if backend == Backend::Ptrace {
4738        let summary_path = print_summary_to_json_file.clone();
4739        let command = tracer_thread::SendCommand::new(command);
4740        return ptrace_completion::run_on_tracer_thread(timeout, move |control| async move {
4741            let command = command.into_inner();
4742            let report = SkidOvershootReport::begin(true);
4743            let config = prepare_backend_config(config, backend);
4744            let result = dispatch_backend(
4745                command,
4746                config,
4747                print_summary,
4748                &summary_path,
4749                backend,
4750                Some(control),
4751            )
4752            .await;
4753            report.finish(result)
4754        });
4755    }
4756    let skid_overshoot_report = SkidOvershootReport::begin(backend.uses_ptrace_pmu_timers());
4757    if backend == Backend::Kvm {
4758        ensure_kvm_stdin_reserved()?;
4759    }
4760    let config = prepare_backend_config(config, backend);
4761    let result = run_with_backend_inner(
4762        command,
4763        config,
4764        print_summary,
4765        print_summary_to_json_file,
4766        backend,
4767        timeout,
4768    );
4769    skid_overshoot_report.finish(result)
4770}
4771
4772// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-749): Review LiteInst backend configuration normalization.
4773#[doc(hidden)]
4774pub fn prepare_backend_config(mut config: DetConfig, backend: Backend) -> DetConfig {
4775    // Detcore reads what the selected backend can do, never which backend it is.
4776    // Each backend states its own facts in `Backend::capabilities()`.
4777    //
4778    // Three properties hold on every backend, so they are not capabilities:
4779    // - Guest-visible wall and monotonic clocks stay in the same global
4780    //   virtual-time domain as timers, sleeps, and timeout deadlines. SaBRe's
4781    //   per-thread execution clock does not advance when the scheduler skips
4782    //   global time while a thread is blocked.
4783    // - A forked process child runs concurrently with its parent. Detcore
4784    //   blocks the parent only for CLONE_VFORK.
4785    // - Detcore dispatches every cloned thread's syscalls through its tool.
4786    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
4787    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-845): Review backend-local guest clock observations.
4788    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1013): Review backend child process execution ordering.
4789    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1013): Review backend thread callback coverage.
4790    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1122): Review concurrent KVM process-child scheduling.
4791    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
4792    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3635): Review in-guest LiteInst killed-thread RPC cancellation.
4793    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
4794    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1152): KVM defers the vfork child spawn, so the child
4795    // registers its vfork barrier only after the parent posts BlockedExternalContinue. ptrace keeps
4796    // the parent kernel-blocked until the child registers.
4797    config.backend = backend_capabilities(backend);
4798    // Whether the run's process signals are tool-controlled is not decided
4799    // here: Detcore installs the backend's process signal control when the
4800    // backend offers it and threads are sequentialized, and reads the installed
4801    // control from then on.
4802    // Whether blocked waits decide signal interruption from the kernel's
4803    // signal state (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146), whether a
4804    // `--max-timeslice` really preempts (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4068)
4805    // and whether guest code can run between two injected calls are the
4806    // backend's own stated facts in `config.backend`
4807    // (`supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`,
4808    // `delivers_preemption_timer_events`, `runs_guest_code_between_injections`),
4809    // not derived from its name here (audit step A9 of
4810    // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4485).
4811    // Only backends where Detcore treats a terminal's signals as reaching the
4812    // guest from the host read it (`Config::guest_may_inherit_a_terminal`, and
4813    // `BackendCapabilities::host_timed_signals_are_physical`), so the host is
4814    // asked only for them.
4815    config.guest_may_inherit_a_terminal =
4816        config.backend.host_timed_signals_are_physical && launcher_may_pass_a_terminal();
4817    // The in-guest runtime's reserved signals are set only for the default
4818    // in-guest route, after this preparation (`in_guest_reserved_signals`),
4819    // so whatever a caller's configuration carried, every backend and every
4820    // other route starts from the empty set (A5 step 3c, D13(a)).
4821    config.in_guest_reserved_signals = 0;
4822    // So is the refusal of host-timed signal producers
4823    // (`in_guest_refuses_host_timed_producers`, A5 step 3c slice 0b).
4824    config.in_guest_refuses_host_timed_producers = false;
4825    // And the in-guest delivery gate, which only the default route's launch
4826    // sets, from the final configuration and the process's PID-namespace
4827    // ownership (`in_guest_signal_delivery_gate`, A5 step 3c.1, D35 and D52).
4828    config.in_guest_signal_delivery = false;
4829    config
4830}
4831
4832/// The configuration of an in-guest run on the loader route (the exec-stop,
4833/// native-exec and mapped-first-admission launchers of `hermit run`): the
4834/// `in-guest-trap` backend's preparation with site patching off. It keeps
4835/// today's behaviour on that route (D13(a), and D26 of the A5 step 3c design:
4836/// the route's own comparison gates any change), so the in-guest runtime's
4837/// reserved-signal set stays empty here whatever `config` carried; only the
4838/// default route sets it (`in_guest_reserved_signals`).
4839pub fn prepare_in_guest_loader_route_config(config: DetConfig) -> DetConfig {
4840    let mut config = prepare_backend_config(config, Backend::InGuestTrap);
4841    config.in_guest_site_patching_off = true;
4842    config
4843}
4844
4845/// Whether the guest may start with a terminal, which can make Linux send the
4846/// guest signals at moments the host sets, such as SIGHUP when the terminal
4847/// hangs up and SIGWINCH when it is resized
4848/// (`Config::guest_may_inherit_a_terminal`): one of this process's standard
4849/// descriptors, which the guest inherits, is a terminal, or this process has a
4850/// controlling terminal, which the guest inherits with its session because
4851/// neither Hermit nor Reverie starts a new session for it. When the
4852/// controlling terminal cannot be read, the answer is yes.
4853fn launcher_may_pass_a_terminal() -> bool {
4854    // SAFETY: isatty only inspects the descriptor.
4855    let standard_terminal = (0..=2).any(|fd| unsafe { libc::isatty(fd) } == 1);
4856    may_pass_a_terminal(standard_terminal, controlling_terminal_device())
4857}
4858
4859/// The rule of `launcher_may_pass_a_terminal`: a terminal standard descriptor,
4860/// a controlling terminal (a nonzero device number), or an unknown one.
4861fn may_pass_a_terminal(standard_terminal: bool, controlling_terminal: Option<i64>) -> bool {
4862    standard_terminal || controlling_terminal != Some(0)
4863}
4864
4865/// This process's controlling terminal as `/proc/self/stat` reports it: field
4866/// 7, `tty_nr`, the terminal's device number, or 0 when there is none. `None`
4867/// when it cannot be read.
4868fn controlling_terminal_device() -> Option<i64> {
4869    parse_controlling_terminal_device(&std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/self/stat").ok()?)
4870}
4871
4872/// `tty_nr` from the text of a `/proc/<pid>/stat` file. The command name in
4873/// field 2 is parenthesized and may hold spaces and parentheses, so the fields
4874/// after it are counted from its last `)`: state, ppid, pgrp, session, tty_nr.
4875fn parse_controlling_terminal_device(stat: &str) -> Option<i64> {
4876    let after_command = stat.get(stat.rfind(')')? + 1..)?;
4877    after_command.split_ascii_whitespace().nth(4)?.parse().ok()
4878}
4879
4880/// What the selected backend can do, as Detcore consumes it.
4881///
4882/// Backends whose crate is always linked are asked directly. The LiteInst and
4883/// DBT constants are checked against their crates by tests built with those
4884/// features; the SaBRe value has no such check. e9patch takes ptrace's.
4885#[doc(hidden)]
4886pub fn backend_capabilities(backend: Backend) -> reverie::BackendCapabilities {
4887    match backend {
4888        // e9patch is binary-rewriting preprocessing whose guest runs on the
4889        // ptrace backend (`hermit run --backend=e9patch` configures its run as
4890        // `Backend::Ptrace`), so it has ptrace's capabilities. A direct caller
4891        // used to get two of them turned off by this name.
4892        Backend::Ptrace | Backend::E9patch => {
4893            <reverie_ptrace::PtraceBackend as reverie::Backend>::capabilities()
4894        }
4895        Backend::Kvm => reverie_kvm::KvmBackend::capabilities(),
4896        // Site patching changes how a syscall reaches the Tool, not what the
4897        // Tool host can do, so in-guest-trap has in-guest LiteInst's capabilities.
4898        Backend::Liteinst | Backend::InGuestTrap => reverie::BackendCapabilities::LITEINST_IN_GUEST,
4899        Backend::Sabre => reverie::BackendCapabilities::SABRE,
4900        Backend::Dbt => reverie::BackendCapabilities::DBT,
4901    }
4902}
4903
4904/// Whether `backend`'s runtime arms Reverie ptrace's PMU timer and delivers its
4905/// events, so `--max-timeslice` really preempts a thread that makes no syscall:
4906/// the backend's stated `delivers_preemption_timer_events`. Only ptrace does
4907/// (e9patch preprocessing runs on it). SaBRe and KVM accept a timer request and
4908/// deliver nothing; DBT and in-guest LiteInst refuse it.
4909pub fn backend_delivers_preemption_timer(backend: Backend) -> bool {
4910    backend_capabilities(backend).delivers_preemption_timer_events
4911}
4912
4913/// After an in-guest LiteInst run, waits (bounded) until the watcher has
4914/// reported every admitted process's physical exit, then releases any exit
4915/// barrier still recorded. Release comes only after that drain: an exit still
4916/// in flight is reported first.
4917///
4918/// Every report is applied again to the run's returned state. The backend
4919/// lets go of its own reference to that state when the run ends, and a report
4920/// that arrived afterwards reached nothing; applying a report twice consumes
4921/// nothing the second time.
4922///
4923/// A failed drain, a fired watchdog or a refused admission fails the run:
4924/// it records a determinism loss, so verification refuses to compare it, and
4925/// returns the failure, after the barriers are released.
4926#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
4927async fn settle_in_guest_exits(
4928    exits: &in_guest_exits::InGuestExitAdmission,
4929    global_state: &detcore::GlobalState,
4930) -> Result<(), Error> {
4931    let drained = exits.drain(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10)).await;
4932    for pid in exits.reported_exits() {
4933        global_state.complete_physical_process_exit(pid);
4934    }
4935    global_state.release_all_physical_process_exits();
4936    let failure = exits.failure().or_else(|| {
4937        drained
4938            .err()
4939            .map(|error| format!("not every in-guest LiteInst guest exit was reported: {error:?}"))
4940    });
4941    match failure {
4942        Some(reason) => {
4943            detcore::detlog::record_determinism_loss(&reason);
4944            Err(Error::msg(reason))
4945        }
4946        None => Ok(()),
4947    }
4948}
4949
4950// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-736): Review reserved LiteInst runtime failure statuses.
4951//
4952// ⚠️ THIS PREDICATE AND THE CLASSIFIER MUST AGREE ABOUT THE SIGNAL BAND, AND A
4953// HARD-CODED RANGE CANNOT. They do NOT cover the same statuses and are not meant
4954// to -- see the table below for what each covers. It is the SIGNAL half that has
4955// to move together, because both readers derive it from the same fact. When the reserved set grew to include the signal
4956// band, `Exited(130)` fell outside `122..=127` and is NOT `Signaled(_, _)` --
4957// it is a status hermit CHOSE, not an actual signal death -- so LiteInst
4958// skipped the forced shutdown and `clean_up` could wait forever on
4959// `handle.await` (detcore/src/tool_global.rs). The reserved set had grown past
4960// the range this hard-coded, and nothing connected the two.
4961//
4962// Keying the SIGNAL HALF on `signal_from_exit_status` -- the same predicate
4963// `classify_container_result` uses -- is what stops that half drifting again: a
4964// change to the band moves both readers or neither.
4965//
4966// ⚠️ THE TWO PREDICATES ARE NOT THE SAME SET, AND AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS
4967// COMMENT SAID THEY WERE. agent(hermit-007)'s codex lane caught the overclaim.
4968// They deliberately differ:
4969//
4970//   this predicate            122..=127        +  signal band  +  real Signaled
4971//   classify_container_result 122 + 123 + 124  +  signal band
4972//
4973// 123..=127 force a LiteInst shutdown and are classified as NEITHER a refusal
4974// nor a signal death. The classifier gives 123 and 124 arms of their own -- 123
4975// is the log byte cap (hermit's `--max-log-bytes`, and the value reserved for
4976// safehermit's log-cap kill, which still exits 125), 124 a deadline hermit
4977// enforced -- while 125 (hermit itself) and 126/127 (exec-level) have none, and
4978// each has a different producer. Only the signal half is shared, and only the
4979// signal half is protected from drift. Do not "simplify" this by assuming the
4980// two agree; the `122..=127` bound here is still hard-coded and still needs a
4981// human to widen it if the reserved set grows again.
4982#[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
4983fn liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(status: ExitStatus) -> bool {
4984    match status {
4985        // A real signal death: the process never chose a status at all.
4986        ExitStatus::Signaled(_, _) | ExitStatus::SignaledRaw(_, _) => true,
4987        ExitStatus::Exited(code) => {
4988            // The 122..=127 reserved band, plus any status hermit emits to mean
4989            // "killed by signal N".
4990            (122..=127).contains(&code) || detcore_model::signal_from_exit_status(code).is_some()
4991        }
4992    }
4993}
4994
4995/// The guest outlived the wall-clock bound the caller asked hermit to enforce.
4996///
4997/// A DISTINCT TYPE, NOT A STRING, because `failure_exit_code` and
4998/// `classify_failure` both have to recognise it and a prose match would break
4999/// silently the first time the wording changed.
5000#[derive(Debug)]
5001pub struct GuestTimedOut {
5002    /// The bound that was exceeded, as the caller spelled it.
5003    pub limit: Duration,
5004}
5005
5006impl std::fmt::Display for GuestTimedOut {
5007    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
5008        write!(
5009            f,
5010            "Guest exceeded the --timeout bound of {} seconds",
5011            self.limit.as_secs()
5012        )
5013    }
5014}
5015
5016impl std::error::Error for GuestTimedOut {}
5017
5018/// Nonordinary backends retain their existing cooperative timeout behavior.
5019/// There is no process-wide alarm in this library. A caller needing a bound on
5020/// synchronous stalls must own external supervision; the CLI arms its own
5021/// separate init-process fallback before invoking the library. Ordinary ptrace
5022/// uses the retained whole-operation driver instead of cancelling this future.
5023async fn with_run_deadline<F>(timeout: Option<Duration>, guest: F) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error>
5024where
5025    F: std::future::Future<Output = Result<ExitStatus, Error>>,
5026{
5027    match timeout {
5028        None => guest.await,
5029        Some(limit) => match tokio::time::timeout(limit, guest).await {
5030            Ok(result) => result,
5031            Err(_) => Err(Error::new(GuestTimedOut { limit })),
5032        },
5033    }
5034}
5035
5036#[tokio::main(flavor = "current_thread")]
5037async fn run_with_backend_inner(
5038    command: Command,
5039    config: DetConfig,
5040    print_summary: bool,
5041    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
5042    backend: Backend,
5043    timeout: Option<Duration>,
5044) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
5045    refuse_in_guest_liteinst_timeout(backend, timeout)?;
5046    // Keep the large backend future off the container supervisor's stack
5047    // before the deadline and Tokio wrappers capture it. Polling and dropping
5048    // stay inline, including the backend teardown on timeout.
5049    let guest = Box::pin(dispatch_backend(
5050        command,
5051        config,
5052        print_summary,
5053        print_summary_to_json_file,
5054        backend,
5055        None,
5056    ));
5057    with_run_deadline(timeout, guest).await
5058}
5059
5060/// The guest's first image, as its `/proc/self/exe` link names it
5061/// (`detcore::Config::launch_image`): the program the launch executes, found
5062/// as the launch finds it, then resolved as the kernel resolves an `execve`
5063/// (`detcore::exec_record::ExecRecord::resolve`). Read in the container,
5064/// whose root is the guest's. A launch through a launcher names it itself
5065/// (`run_sabre`). `None` when it cannot be found, which leaves the link to the
5066/// kernel, and the launch reports the missing program itself.
5067fn launched_image(command: &Command) -> Option<detcore::LaunchImage> {
5068    let program = command.find_program().ok()?;
5069    let cwd = match command.get_current_dir() {
5070        Some(cwd) => cwd.to_owned(),
5071        None => std::env::current_dir().ok()?,
5072    };
5073    let record = detcore::exec_record::ExecRecord::resolve(Path::new("/"), &cwd, &program)?;
5074    Some(detcore::LaunchImage {
5075        exe: Some(record.exe),
5076        launcher: None,
5077    })
5078}
5079
5080async fn dispatch_backend(
5081    command: Command,
5082    mut config: DetConfig,
5083    print_summary: bool,
5084    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
5085    backend: Backend,
5086    control: Option<std::rc::Rc<ptrace_completion::Control>>,
5087) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
5088    // Every launch path, ptrace's included, reaches the guest through here.
5089    crate::cpu_profile_admission::refuse_unadmitted_launch(&config, backend == Backend::Ptrace)?;
5090    config.launch_image = launched_image(&command);
5091    if backend == Backend::Kvm {
5092        return Ok(run_kvm(
5093            &command,
5094            config,
5095            print_summary,
5096            print_summary_to_json_file,
5097            false,
5098        )
5099        .await?
5100        .status);
5101    }
5102    if backend == Backend::Dbt {
5103        #[cfg(feature = "dbt")]
5104        {
5105            return Ok(run_dbt(command, config, print_summary, false).await?.status);
5106        }
5107        #[cfg(not(feature = "dbt"))]
5108        {
5109            backend.ensure_available()?;
5110            unreachable!("DBT availability must fail when the feature is disabled");
5111        }
5112    }
5113    if backend == Backend::Sabre {
5114        return Ok(run_sabre(
5115            command,
5116            config,
5117            print_summary,
5118            print_summary_to_json_file,
5119            false,
5120        )
5121        .await?
5122        .status);
5123    }
5124    if backend.is_in_guest_liteinst() {
5125        #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
5126        {
5127            let stats_request = in_guest_stats_request(backend, print_summary_to_json_file);
5128            let mut command = command;
5129            refuse_in_guest_liteinst_run(&mut command, &config, backend)?;
5130            let (launch, _detlog_descriptor) =
5131                in_guest_liteinst_launch(&mut command, &in_guest_detlog_forward_policy())?;
5132            // After Hermit's other callbacks, so the guest's own check is the
5133            // last one that can change what it checks (`LaunchAudit::install`).
5134            let audit = neutralize_inherited_signal_producers(&mut command, backend)?;
5135            let tool_data = launch.encode();
5136            // Every Tool image must forward on that socket, by that policy;
5137            // see detcore::Config::in_guest_detlog_forward_policy.
5138            let mut config = config;
5139            config.in_guest_detlog_forward_policy = _detlog_descriptor
5140                .is_some()
5141                .then(|| in_guest_detlog_forward_policy().encode());
5142            config.in_guest_site_patching_off = in_guest_site_patching_off(backend);
5143            config.in_guest_refuses_host_timed_producers =
5144                in_guest_refuses_host_timed_producers(backend);
5145            // Last, from the configuration every Tool image receives.
5146            config.in_guest_reserved_signals = in_guest_reserved_signals(&config, backend);
5147            // The delivery gate, from the final configuration and whether
5148            // this process owns the guests' PID namespace; off until the
5149            // runtime takes it (A5 step 3c.1, D35, D52).
5150            config.in_guest_signal_delivery = IN_GUEST_RUNTIME_DELIVERS_SIGNALS
5151                && in_guest_signal_delivery_gate(
5152                    &config,
5153                    backend,
5154                    scheduler_owns_guest_pid_namespace(),
5155                );
5156            let preload = liteinst_tool_runtime_library_path()?;
5157            let exits = std::sync::Arc::new(in_guest_exits::InGuestExitAdmission::default());
5158            let (exit_status, mut global_state, dispatch_stats, process_reports) =
5159                reverie_liteinst::LiteinstBackend::with_connection_admission(
5160                    exits.clone(),
5161                    async {
5162                        if stats_request.is_enabled() {
5163                            let (exit_status, global_state, source) =
5164                                reverie_liteinst::LiteinstBackend::run_with_preload_data_and_stats::<
5165                                    Detcore,
5166                                >(command, config, preload, tool_data)
5167                                .await?;
5168                            let dispatch_stats =
5169                                backend_stats::report(backend, stats_request, &source);
5170                            let process_reports = source.snapshot().process_reports();
5171                            Ok::<_, reverie::Error>((
5172                                exit_status,
5173                                global_state,
5174                                dispatch_stats,
5175                                process_reports,
5176                            ))
5177                        } else {
5178                            let (exit_status, global_state) =
5179                                reverie_liteinst::LiteinstBackend::run_with_preload_data::<Detcore>(
5180                                    command, config, preload, tool_data,
5181                                )
5182                                .await?;
5183                            Ok((exit_status, global_state, None, 0))
5184                        }
5185                    },
5186                )
5187                .await
5188                .inspect_err(|error| exits.fail_launch(error))
5189                // A standard descriptor the guest's own check refused
5190                // (D25) fails the launch; name it.
5191                .map_err(|error| match &audit {
5192                    Some(audit) => audit.launch_error(backend, error),
5193                    None => Error::from(error),
5194                })?;
5195            let patched =
5196                in_guest_trap_patching_evidence(backend, dispatch_stats.as_ref(), process_reports);
5197            let settled = settle_in_guest_exits(&exits, &global_state).await;
5198            let policy_refusal = global_state.policy_refusal();
5199            if settled.is_err() || liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(exit_status) {
5200                global_state.force_shutdown_with_error();
5201                global_state.cancel_internal_scheduler().await;
5202            }
5203            let finalized = global_state
5204                .clean_up_with_dispatch_stats(
5205                    print_summary,
5206                    print_summary_to_json_file,
5207                    dispatch_stats,
5208                )
5209                .await;
5210            // After the scheduler has shut down, so the line's place among
5211            // the run's INFO lines is fixed (D25); a stopping refusal logs it
5212            // just before it exits instead.
5213            detcore::host_timed_producers::emit_run_end_log();
5214            let result = (|| {
5215                refuse_in_guest_policy(backend, policy_refusal)?;
5216                settled?;
5217                refuse_in_guest_trap_patching(backend, patched)
5218            })();
5219            detcore::combine_finalization(result, finalized)?;
5220            return Ok(exit_status);
5221        }
5222        #[cfg(not(feature = "liteinst"))]
5223        {
5224            backend.ensure_available()?;
5225            unreachable!("LiteInst availability must fail when the feature is disabled");
5226        }
5227    }
5228    ensure_backend_dispatch(backend)?;
5229
5230    let stats_request = backend_stats::request(print_summary_to_json_file);
5231    let control = control
5232        .ok_or_else(|| Error::msg("ordinary ptrace requires its retained operation owner"))?;
5233    // A sequentialized guest tells gdbserver not to serialize its threads;
5234    // see hermit_run_ptrace::spawn_tracer.
5235    let tracer = hermit_run_ptrace::spawn_tracer(
5236        command,
5237        config.clone(),
5238        config.gdbserver.then_some(config.gdbserver_port),
5239        config.sequentialize_threads,
5240        stats_request,
5241    )
5242    .await?;
5243    let stats_source = tracer.backend_stats();
5244    let (exit_status, global_state) = ptrace_completion::wait(tracer, control).await?;
5245    let dispatch_stats =
5246        backend_stats::report_if_collected(backend, stats_request, stats_source.as_ref());
5247    global_state
5248        .clean_up_with_dispatch_stats(print_summary, print_summary_to_json_file, dispatch_stats)
5249        .await
5250        .map_err(|error| {
5251            error.context(format!(
5252                "ptrace cleanup after observed guest status {exit_status:?}"
5253            ))
5254        })?; // Before it's dropped by this function.
5255    Ok(exit_status)
5256}
5257
5258/// Variant of `run` that also captures stdout/stderr.
5259///
5260/// On ptrace it needs no particular stack from the calling thread; see [`run`].
5261pub fn run_with_output(
5262    command: Command,
5263    config: DetConfig,
5264    print_summary: bool,
5265    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
5266) -> Result<Output, Error> {
5267    run_with_output_backend(
5268        command,
5269        config,
5270        print_summary,
5271        print_summary_to_json_file,
5272        Backend::Ptrace,
5273    )
5274}

5276/// Variant of [`run_with_backend`] that also captures stdout/stderr.
5277///
5278/// On ptrace it needs no particular stack from the calling thread; see [`run`].
5279pub fn run_with_output_backend(
5280    command: Command,
5281    config: DetConfig,
5282    print_summary: bool,
5283    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
5284    backend: Backend,
5285) -> Result<Output, Error> {
5286    if backend == Backend::Kvm {
5287        ensure_kvm_stdin_reserved()?;
5288    }
5289    run_with_output_backend_timeout(
5290        command,
5291        config,
5292        print_summary,
5293        print_summary_to_json_file,
5294        backend,
5295        None,
5296    )
5297}
