5299/// [`run_with_output_backend`] with a hermit-enforced wall-clock bound.
5300///
5301/// See [`run_with_backend_timeout`]; the teardown semantics are identical. On
5302/// ptrace it needs no particular stack from the calling thread; see [`run`].
5303pub fn run_with_output_backend_timeout(
5304    command: Command,
5305    config: DetConfig,
5306    print_summary: bool,
5307    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
5308    backend: Backend,
5309    timeout: Option<Duration>,
5310) -> Result<Output, Error> {
5311    if backend == Backend::Ptrace {
5312        let summary_path = print_summary_to_json_file.clone();
5313        let command = tracer_thread::SendCommand::new(command);
5314        return ptrace_completion::run_on_tracer_thread(timeout, move |control| async move {
5315            let command = command.into_inner();
5316            let report = SkidOvershootReport::begin(true);
5317            // Box before the retained operation captures the backend state;
5318            // constructing and polling it still happen after admission here.
5319            let result = Box::pin(dispatch_output_backend(
5320                command,
5321                prepare_backend_config(config, backend),
5322                print_summary,
5323                &summary_path,
5324                backend,
5325                Some(control),
5326            ))
5327            .await;
5328            report.finish(result)
5329        });
5330    }
5331    let (output, skid_overshoots) = run_with_output_backend_timeout_and_skid_overshoots(
5332        command,
5333        config,
5334        print_summary,
5335        print_summary_to_json_file,
5336        backend,
5337        timeout,
5338    )?;
5339    if skid_overshoots > 0 {
5340        return Err(Error::new(SkidOvershootError::new(skid_overshoots)));
5341    }
5342    Ok(output)
5343}
5344
5345/// Run with captured output and return the number of precise PMU timer
5346/// overshoots alongside it instead of refusing before a caller can inspect the
5347/// completed output. The `--verify` path uses this to finish and publish its
5348/// comparison before it refuses the overshoot-tainted result.
5349#[doc(hidden)]
5350pub fn run_with_output_backend_timeout_and_skid_overshoots(
5351    command: Command,
5352    config: DetConfig,
5353    print_summary: bool,
5354    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
5355    backend: Backend,
5356    timeout: Option<Duration>,
5357) -> Result<(Output, u64), Error> {
5358    if backend == Backend::Ptrace {
5359        let summary_path = print_summary_to_json_file.clone();
5360        let command = tracer_thread::SendCommand::new(command);
5361        return ptrace_completion::run_on_tracer_thread(timeout, move |control| async move {
5362            let command = command.into_inner();
5363            let report = SkidOvershootReport::begin(true);
5364            let result = Box::pin(dispatch_output_backend(
5365                command,
5366                prepare_backend_config(config, backend),
5367                print_summary,
5368                &summary_path,
5369                backend,
5370                Some(control),
5371            ))
5372            .await;
5373            report.finish_with_count(result)
5374        });
5375    }
5376    let skid_overshoot_report = SkidOvershootReport::begin(backend.uses_ptrace_pmu_timers());
5377    if backend == Backend::Kvm {
5378        // Reserve before the Tokio runtime can reuse a closed fd 0. KVM
5379        // verification consumes the explicit output snapshot in `run_kvm`;
5380        // public output-capture callers without one retain this reservation.
5381        ensure_kvm_stdin_reserved()?;
5382    }
5383    let config = prepare_backend_config(config, backend);
5384    let result = run_with_output_backend_inner(
5385        command,
5386        config,
5387        print_summary,
5388        print_summary_to_json_file,
5389        backend,
5390        timeout,
5391    );
5392    skid_overshoot_report.finish_with_count(result)
5393}
5394
5395#[tokio::main(flavor = "current_thread")]
5396async fn run_with_output_backend_inner(
5397    command: Command,
5398    config: DetConfig,
5399    print_summary: bool,
5400    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
5401    backend: Backend,
5402    timeout: Option<Duration>,
5403) -> Result<Output, Error> {
5404    refuse_in_guest_liteinst_timeout(backend, timeout)?;
5405    // Keep the backend state off the caller's stack before Tokio and the
5406    // deadline future capture it. Polling and teardown stay on this thread.
5407    let guest = Box::pin(dispatch_output_backend(
5408        command,
5409        config,
5410        print_summary,
5411        print_summary_to_json_file,
5412        backend,
5413        None,
5414    ));
5415    match timeout {
5416        None => guest.await,
5417        Some(limit) => match tokio::time::timeout(limit, guest).await {
5418            Ok(result) => result,
5419            Err(_elapsed) => Err(Error::new(GuestTimedOut { limit })),
5420        },
5421    }
5422}
5423
5424async fn dispatch_output_backend(
5425    mut command: Command,
5426    mut config: DetConfig,
5427    print_summary: bool,
5428    print_summary_to_json_file: &Option<PathBuf>,
5429    backend: Backend,
5430    control: Option<std::rc::Rc<ptrace_completion::Control>>,
5431) -> Result<Output, Error> {
5432    // Every launch path, ptrace's included, reaches the guest through here.
5433    crate::cpu_profile_admission::refuse_unadmitted_launch(&config, backend == Backend::Ptrace)?;
5434    config.launch_image = launched_image(&command);
5435    if backend == Backend::Kvm {
5436        return run_kvm(
5437            &command,
5438            config,
5439            print_summary,
5440            print_summary_to_json_file,
5441            true,
5442        )
5443        .await;
5444    }
5445    if backend == Backend::Dbt {
5446        #[cfg(feature = "dbt")]
5447        {
5448            return run_dbt(command, config, print_summary, true).await;
5449        }
5450        #[cfg(not(feature = "dbt"))]
5451        {
5452            backend.ensure_available()?;
5453            unreachable!("DBT availability must fail when the feature is disabled");
5454        }
5455    }
5456    if backend == Backend::Sabre {
5457        #[cfg(not(feature = "sabre"))]
5458        backend.ensure_available()?;
5459        command.stdin(output_backend_stdin()?);
5460        command.stdout(Stdio::piped());
5461        command.stderr(Stdio::piped());
5462        return run_sabre(
5463            command,
5464            config,
5465            print_summary,
5466            print_summary_to_json_file,
5467            true,
5468        )
5469        .await;
5470    }
5471    if backend.is_in_guest_liteinst() {
5472        #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
5473        {
5474            command.stdin(output_backend_stdin()?);
5475            let stats_request = in_guest_stats_request(backend, print_summary_to_json_file);
5476            refuse_in_guest_liteinst_run(&mut command, &config, backend)?;
5477            let (launch, _detlog_descriptor) =
5478                in_guest_liteinst_launch(&mut command, &in_guest_detlog_forward_policy())?;
5479            // After Hermit's other callbacks, so the guest's own check is the
5480            // last one that can change what it checks (`LaunchAudit::install`).
5481            let audit = neutralize_inherited_signal_producers(&mut command, backend)?;
5482            let tool_data = launch.encode();
5483            // Every Tool image must forward on that socket, by that policy;
5484            // see detcore::Config::in_guest_detlog_forward_policy.
5485            let mut config = config;
5486            config.in_guest_detlog_forward_policy = _detlog_descriptor
5487                .is_some()
5488                .then(|| in_guest_detlog_forward_policy().encode());
5489            config.in_guest_site_patching_off = in_guest_site_patching_off(backend);
5490            config.in_guest_refuses_host_timed_producers =
5491                in_guest_refuses_host_timed_producers(backend);
5492            // Last, from the configuration every Tool image receives.
5493            config.in_guest_reserved_signals = in_guest_reserved_signals(&config, backend);
5494            // The delivery gate, from the final configuration and whether
5495            // this process owns the guests' PID namespace; off until the
5496            // runtime takes it (A5 step 3c.1, D35, D52).
5497            config.in_guest_signal_delivery = IN_GUEST_RUNTIME_DELIVERS_SIGNALS
5498                && in_guest_signal_delivery_gate(
5499                    &config,
5500                    backend,
5501                    scheduler_owns_guest_pid_namespace(),
5502                );
5503            let preload = liteinst_tool_runtime_library_path()?;
5504            let exits = std::sync::Arc::new(in_guest_exits::InGuestExitAdmission::default());
5505            let (output, mut global_state, dispatch_stats, process_reports) =
5506                reverie_liteinst::LiteinstBackend::with_connection_admission(exits.clone(), async {
5507                    if stats_request.is_enabled() {
5508                        let (output, global_state, source) =
5509                            reverie_liteinst::LiteinstBackend::run_with_output_and_preload_data_and_stats::<
5510                                Detcore,
5511                            >(command, config, preload, tool_data)
5512                            .await?;
5513                        let dispatch_stats = backend_stats::report(backend, stats_request, &source);
5514                        let process_reports = source.snapshot().process_reports();
5515                        Ok::<_, reverie::Error>((output, global_state, dispatch_stats, process_reports))
5516                    } else {
5517                        let (output, global_state) =
5518                            reverie_liteinst::LiteinstBackend::run_with_output_and_preload_data::<
5519                                Detcore,
5520                            >(command, config, preload, tool_data)
5521                            .await?;
5522                        Ok((output, global_state, None, 0))
5523                    }
5524                })
5525                .await
5526                .inspect_err(|error| exits.fail_launch(error))
5527                // A standard descriptor the guest's own check refused
5528                // (D25) fails the launch; name it.
5529                .map_err(|error| match &audit {
5530                    Some(audit) => audit.launch_error(backend, error),
5531                    None => Error::from(error),
5532                })?;
5533            let patched =
5534                in_guest_trap_patching_evidence(backend, dispatch_stats.as_ref(), process_reports);
5535            let settled = settle_in_guest_exits(&exits, &global_state).await;
5536            let policy_refusal = global_state.policy_refusal();
5537            let output = Output {
5538                status: output.status.into(),
5539                stdout: output.stdout,
5540                stderr: output.stderr,
5541            };
5542            let status = output.status;
5543            if settled.is_err() || liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(status) {
5544                global_state.force_shutdown_with_error();
5545                global_state.cancel_internal_scheduler().await;
5546            }
5547            let finalized = global_state
5548                .clean_up_with_dispatch_stats(
5549                    print_summary,
5550                    print_summary_to_json_file,
5551                    dispatch_stats,
5552                )
5553                .await;
5554            // After the scheduler has shut down, so the line's place among
5555            // the run's INFO lines is fixed (D25); a stopping refusal logs it
5556            // just before it exits instead.
5557            detcore::host_timed_producers::emit_run_end_log();
5558            let result = (|| {
5559                refuse_in_guest_policy(backend, policy_refusal)?;
5560                settled?;
5561                refuse_in_guest_trap_patching(backend, patched)
5562            })();
5563            detcore::combine_finalization(result, finalized)?;
5564            return Ok(Output {
5565                status,
5566                stdout: output.stdout,
5567                stderr: output.stderr,
5568            });
5569        }
5570        #[cfg(not(feature = "liteinst"))]
5571        {
5572            backend.ensure_available()?;
5573            unreachable!("LiteInst availability must fail when the feature is disabled");
5574        }
5575    }
5576    ensure_backend_dispatch(backend)?;
5577
5578    let stats_request = backend_stats::request(print_summary_to_json_file);
5579    command.stdin(output_backend_stdin()?);
5580    command.stdout(Stdio::piped());
5581    command.stderr(Stdio::piped());
5582    let control = control
5583        .ok_or_else(|| Error::msg("ordinary ptrace requires its retained operation owner"))?;
5584    // A sequentialized guest tells gdbserver not to serialize its threads;
5585    // see hermit_run_ptrace::spawn_tracer.
5586    let tracer = hermit_run_ptrace::spawn_tracer(
5587        command,
5588        config.clone(),
5589        config.gdbserver.then_some(config.gdbserver_port),
5590        config.sequentialize_threads,
5591        stats_request,
5592    )
5593    .await?;
5594    let stats_source = tracer.backend_stats();
5595    let (output, global_state) = ptrace_completion::wait_with_output(tracer, control).await?;
5596    let dispatch_stats =
5597        backend_stats::report_if_collected(backend, stats_request, stats_source.as_ref());
5598    global_state
5599        .clean_up_with_dispatch_stats(print_summary, print_summary_to_json_file, dispatch_stats)
5600        .await
5601        .map_err(|error| {
5602            error.context(format!(
5603                "ptrace cleanup after observed guest status {:?}",
5604                output.status
5605            ))
5606        })?;
5607    Ok(output)
5608}
5609
5610/// Holds the context necessary to run high-level hermit functions.
5611pub struct HermitData {
5612    // The data directory. Defaults to `~/.cache/hermit`. Note that we shouldn't
5613    // expect this to exist in any of the functions that are called.
5614    data_dir: PathBuf,
5615}
5616
5617fn collect_recording_ids(
5618    entries: impl IntoIterator<Item = io::Result<fs::DirEntry>>,
5619    data_dir: &Path,
5620    mut file_type: impl FnMut(&fs::DirEntry) -> io::Result<fs::FileType>,
5621) -> Result<Vec<Id>, Error> {
5622    let mut recordings = Vec::new();
5623    for entry in entries {
5624        let entry = entry.with_context(|| {
5625            format!(
5626                "Failed to read an entry in recording inventory {}",
5627                data_dir.display()
5628            )
5629        })?;
5630        let path = entry.path();
5631        if file_type(&entry)
5632            .with_context(|| {
5633                format!(
5634                    "Failed to inspect recording inventory entry {}",
5635                    path.display()
5636                )
5637            })?
5638            .is_dir()
5639            && let Some(id) = entry
5640                .file_name()
5641                .to_str()
5642                .and_then(|name| name.parse::<Id>().ok())
5643        {
5644            recordings.push(id);
5645        }
5646    }
5647    Ok(recordings)
5648}
5649
5650impl Default for HermitData {
5651    fn default() -> Self {
5652        Self::new()
5653    }
5654}
5655
5656impl HermitData {
5657    /// Creates an instance of `HermitData` using `~/.cache/hermit` as the data
5658    /// directory.
5659    pub fn new() -> Self {
5660        Self::with_dir(
5661            dirs::cache_dir()
5662                .map_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("/tmp/hermit"), |dir| dir.join("hermit")),
5663        )
5664    }
5665
5666    /// Creates a `HermitData` using the given directory as the base path for
5667    /// storing recording data.
5668    pub fn with_dir<P>(data_dir: P) -> Self
5669    where
5670        P: Into<PathBuf>,
5671    {
5672        Self {
5673            data_dir: data_dir.into(),
5674        }
5675    }
5676
5677    /// Returns the path to the data directory where recordings are stored.
5678    pub fn data_dir(&self) -> &Path {
5679        &self.data_dir
5680    }
5681
5682    /// Records the execution of the given command, returning its `Recording`.
5683    ///
5684    /// If recording failed, then an error is returned. Note that if the command
5685    /// itself failed, then we still return a successful recording, but its exit
5686    /// status will be non-zero.
5687    ///
5688    /// This low-level API does not create a Hermit container, so it has no
5689    /// authenticated private-mount provenance to supply. Detcore derives mount
5690    /// identities from the completed guest namespace. CLI container callers
5691    /// with producer-owned root provenance must use
5692    /// [`Self::record_with_mountinfo`].
5693    ///
5694    /// The ptrace session runs on a tracer thread, so the calling thread needs no
5695    /// particular stack; see [`run`].
5696    pub fn record(&self, command: Command) -> Result<Recording, Error> {
5697        let store = Self {
5698            data_dir: self.data_dir.clone(),
5699        };
5700        let command = tracer_thread::SendCommand::new(command);
5701        ptrace_completion::run_on_tracer_thread(None, move |control| async move {
5702            let command = command.into_inner();
5703            let data = store.create_recording_dir()?;
5704            let exit_status = record_to_async(
5705                command,
5706                data.path(),
5707                MountProvenance::default(),
5708                None,
5709                None,
5710                None,
5711                detcore_model::cpu_profile::CpuProfile::default(),
5712                control,
5713            )
5714            .await?;
5715            store.commit_recording(data, exit_status)
5716        })
5717    }
5718
5719    /// Records with mountinfo provenance captured from the active container.
5720    ///
5721    /// The ptrace session runs on a tracer thread, so the calling thread needs no
5722    /// particular stack; see [`run`].
5723    pub fn record_with_mountinfo(
5724        &self,
5725        command: Command,
5726        mountinfo_root_rewrites: Vec<detcore_model::config::MountInfoRootRewrite>,
5727    ) -> Result<Recording, Error> {
5728        let store = Self {
5729            data_dir: self.data_dir.clone(),
5730        };
5731        let command = tracer_thread::SendCommand::new(command);
5732        ptrace_completion::run_on_tracer_thread(None, move |control| async move {
5733            let command = command.into_inner();
5734            let data = store.create_recording_dir()?;
5735            let mount_ids = capture_mountinfo_identity_order()?;
5736            let exit_status = record_to_async(
5737                command,
5738                data.path(),
5739                MountProvenance {
5740                    root_rewrites: mountinfo_root_rewrites,
5741                    container_mount_table: None,
5742                    mount_ids: None,
5743                },
5744                Some(mount_ids),
5745                None,
5746                None,
5747                detcore_model::cpu_profile::CpuProfile::default(),
5748                control,
5749            )
5750            .await?;
5751            store.commit_recording(data, exit_status)
5752        })
5753    }
5754
5755    /// Creates a temporary directory for a recording that has not been committed yet.
5756    pub fn create_recording_dir(&self) -> Result<tempfile::TempDir, Error> {
5757        let tmp_data_dir = self.data_dir.join("tmp");
5758
5759        fs::create_dir_all(&tmp_data_dir).with_context(|| {
5760            format!(
5761                "Failed to create recording directory: {}",
5762                self.data_dir.display()
5763            )
5764        })?;
5765
5766        Ok(tempfile::TempDir::new_in(tmp_data_dir)?)
5767    }
5768
5769    /// Commits a completed temporary recording to the recording store.
5770    pub fn commit_recording(
5771        &self,
5772        data: tempfile::TempDir,
5773        exit_status: ExitStatus,
5774    ) -> Result<Recording, Error> {
5775        let id = Id::unique();
5776
5777        // Atomically move the temporary recording to its final location.
5778        fs::rename(data.keep(), self.data_dir.join(id.to_string()))?;
5779
5780        self.note_latest(&id, true)
5781            .with_context(|| format!("Failed to update {:?}", self.data_dir.join(LAST)))?;
5782
5783        Ok(Recording { id, exit_status })
5784    }
5785
5786    /// Replays the given recording ID.
5787    ///
5788    /// The ptrace session runs on a tracer thread, so the calling thread needs no
5789    /// particular stack; see [`run`].
5790    pub fn replay(&self, id: Id) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
5791        let data = self.data_dir.join(id.to_string());
5792        replay_from(&data)
5793    }
5794
5795    /// Replays the given recording ID with a gdbserver available to attach to.
5796    ///
5797    /// The ptrace session runs on a tracer thread, so the calling thread needs no
5798    /// particular stack; see [`run`].
5799    pub fn replay_with_gdbserver(&self, id: Id, port: u16) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
5800        let data = self.data_dir.join(id.to_string());
5801        replay_with_gdbserver(&data, port)
5802    }
5803
5804    /// Returns an iterator over the recordings.
5805    ///
5806    /// Use [`Self::recording_metadata`] to get more information about a recording.
5807    pub fn recordings(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = Id> + use<> {
5808        fs::read_dir(&self.data_dir)
5809            .ok()
5810            .into_iter()
5811            .flatten()
5812            .filter_map(|entry| {
5813                let entry = entry.ok()?;
5814
5815                if entry.file_type().ok()?.is_dir() {
5816                    Some(entry.file_name().to_str()?.parse::<Id>().ok()?)
5817                } else {
5818                    None
5819                }
5820            })
5821    }
5822
5823    /// Returns all recordings, or an error if the data directory cannot be
5824    /// enumerated completely.
5825    ///
5826    /// A missing data directory has no recordings. Other filesystem errors are
5827    /// returned rather than being mistaken for an empty or partial inventory.
5828    pub fn try_recordings(&self) -> Result<Vec<Id>, Error> {
5829        let entries = match fs::read_dir(&self.data_dir) {
5830            Ok(entries) => entries,
5831            Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(Vec::new()),
5832            Err(error) => {
5833                return Err(error).with_context(|| {
5834                    format!(
5835                        "Failed to read recording inventory in {}",
5836                        self.data_dir.display()
5837                    )
5838                });
5839            }
5840        };
5841
5842        collect_recording_ids(entries, &self.data_dir, fs::DirEntry::file_type)
5843    }
5844
5845    /// Returns the metadata of a recording.
5846    pub fn recording_metadata(&self, id: Id) -> Result<Metadata, Error> {
5847        Metadata::load(&self.data_dir.join(id.to_string()))
5848    }
5849
5850    /// Deletes a recording.
5851    pub fn remove(&self, id: Id) -> Result<(), Error> {
5852        let path = self.data_dir.join(id.to_string());
5853
5854        // Before deleting anything, make sure this file exists. This may not be a
5855        // recording if this file does not exist. A run manifest marks a
5856        // recording too: a run that drew an input from the host leaves only
5857        // that (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4271).
5858        let metadata_path = [METADATA_NAME, RUN_MANIFEST_NAME]
5859            .into_iter()
5860            .map(|name| path.join(name))
5861            .find(|marker| marker.exists())
5862            .unwrap_or_else(|| path.join(METADATA_NAME));
5863        let metadata = fs::metadata(&metadata_path)
5864            .with_context(|| format!("Failed to find {:?}", metadata_path))?;
5865
5866        if !metadata.is_file() {
5867            return Err(anyhow!("{:?} is not a file", metadata_path));
5868        }
5869
5870        // Do a recursive delete on the directory. Note that this does not follow
5871        // symlinks.
5872        fs::remove_dir_all(path)?;
5873
5874        Ok(())
5875    }
5876
5877    /// Returns the last recorded ID.
5878    pub fn last_id(&self) -> Result<Id, Error> {
5879        Ok(fs::read_to_string(self.data_dir.join(LAST))?.parse()?)
5880    }
5881
5882    /// Atomically names `id` as the newest recording: `last-run` always,
5883    /// and `last`, which a bare `hermit replay` replays, when the user
5884    /// `asked` for the recording (`hermit record`, `hermit run
5885    /// --record-networking`) rather than a run leaving its manifest; see
5886    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4271>.
5887    pub fn note_latest(&self, id: &Id, asked: bool) -> Result<(), Error> {
5888        let tmp = self.data_dir.join("tmp");
5889        fs::create_dir_all(&tmp)?;
5890        let names = if asked {
5891            &[LAST_RUN, LAST][..]
5892        } else {
5893            &[LAST_RUN][..]
5894        };
5895        for name in names {
5896            let mut file = tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in(&tmp)?;
5897            write!(file, "{}", id)?;
5898            file.persist(self.data_dir.join(name))?;
5899        }
5900        Ok(())
5901    }
5902}
5903
5904/// What a recording takes from the completed recording container's mount
5905/// namespace, which a caller without a Hermit container leaves empty.
5906#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
5907pub struct MountProvenance {
5908    /// The proven roots of Hermit's own mounts
5909    /// (`detcore::Config::mountinfo_root_rewrites`).
5910    pub root_rewrites: Vec<detcore_model::config::MountInfoRootRewrite>,
5911    /// The guest's container mount table
5912    /// (`detcore::Config::container_mount_table`), which the recording carries
5913    /// for its replay.
5914    pub container_mount_table: Option<detcore_model::container_mounts::ContainerMountTable>,
5915    /// The namespace's identity order, read with the table
5916    /// (`detcore::Config::mountinfo_mount_ids`). `None` asks the recorder to
5917    /// capture it. A table and an order from two reads need not agree: a host
5918    /// process that removes a host mount's directory detaches the copy of that
5919    /// mount from the container too, so a row the table shows can be gone
5920    /// from a later read.
5921    pub mount_ids: Option<Vec<u64>>,
5922}
5923
5924/// `NS_GET_MNTNS_ID`, `_IOR(NSIO, 5, __u64)` in Linux's uapi/linux/nsfs.h.
5925const NS_GET_MNTNS_ID: libc::c_ulong = (2 << 30) | (8 << 16) | (0xb7 << 8) | 5;
5926
5927/// The calling thread's mount namespace (`DetConfig::mountinfo_mount_namespace`):
5928/// the kernel's namespace ID from `ioctl(NS_GET_MNTNS_ID)` on
5929/// `/proc/thread-self/ns/mnt`, and the descriptor's device and inode numbers.
5930/// The calling thread's, not the thread group leader's: a library caller's
5931/// thread can have a mount namespace of its own, and every capture here
5932/// (`/proc/thread-self/mountinfo` and `fdinfo`) reads that same thread's. A
5933/// kernel without the ioctl (ENOTTY or EINVAL) yields no ID; any other failure
5934/// is an error.
5935pub fn current_mount_namespace() -> Result<detcore_model::config::MountNamespaceIdentity, Error> {
5936    use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
5937    use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
5938    let file = fs::File::open("/proc/thread-self/ns/mnt")
5939        .context("failed to open this thread's mount namespace")?;
5940    let metadata = file
5941        .metadata()
5942        .context("failed to read this process's mount namespace")?;
5943    let mut id: u64 = 0;
5944    // SAFETY: NS_GET_MNTNS_ID writes one u64 through the pointer, which
5945    // points at `id` for the duration of the call.
5946    let id =
5947        if unsafe { libc::ioctl(file.as_raw_fd(), NS_GET_MNTNS_ID, &mut id as *mut u64) } == 0 {
5948            Some(id)
5949        } else {
5950            let error = std::io::Error::last_os_error();
5951            match error.raw_os_error() {
5952                Some(libc::ENOTTY | libc::EINVAL) => None,
5953                _ => {
5954                    return Err(Error::new(error)
5955                        .context("failed to read this process's mount namespace ID"));
5956                }
5957            }
5958        };
5959    Ok(detcore_model::config::MountNamespaceIdentity {
5960        id,
5961        device: metadata.dev(),
5962        inode: metadata.ino(),
5963    })
5964}
5965
5966/// The calling thread's mount table (`/proc/thread-self/mountinfo`): the rows
5967/// of the namespace [`current_mount_namespace`] names.
5968pub fn thread_mountinfo() -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error> {
5969    fs::read("/proc/thread-self/mountinfo")
5970        .context("Failed to read this thread's mount table (/proc/thread-self/mountinfo)")
5971}
5972
5973/// The raw mount ID of the mount `path` reaches in the calling thread's
5974/// namespace, from the `fdinfo` of an `O_PATH` descriptor held on it; `None`
5975/// where it cannot be opened. O_PATH pins the object without read
5976/// permission.
5977fn thread_mount_id_of(path: &Path) -> Option<u64> {
5978    held_mount_id(&hold_path(path, false).ok()?)
5979}
5980
5981/// An `O_PATH` descriptor held on `path` (a directory, with `directory`),
5982/// resolved as `chdir` and `open` resolve it: following symbolic links, and
5983/// a relative path from the calling thread's working directory, whose name is
5984/// never asked for. Holding it pins the mount it reaches, and the lookup has
5985/// already triggered any automount on the way.
5986fn hold_path(path: &Path, directory: bool) -> nix::Result<std::os::fd::OwnedFd> {
5987    use nix::fcntl::OFlag;
5988    let flags = OFlag::O_PATH
5989        | OFlag::O_CLOEXEC
5990        | if directory {
5991            OFlag::O_DIRECTORY
5992        } else {
5993            OFlag::empty()
5994        };
5995    nix::fcntl::open(path, flags, nix::sys::stat::Mode::empty())
5996}
5997
5998/// The raw mount ID of the mount `held` reaches, from its
5999/// `/proc/thread-self/fdinfo`.
6000fn held_mount_id(held: &std::os::fd::OwnedFd) -> Option<u64> {
6001    let fdinfo = fs::read(format!("/proc/thread-self/fdinfo/{}", held.as_raw_fd())).ok()?;
6002    detcore_model::procfs::parse_fdinfo_mount_id(&fdinfo)
6003}
6004
6005/// Capture the calling thread's mount namespace's raw IDs in the exact
6006/// row/parent order used by Detcore's canonical mountinfo mapping.
6007pub fn capture_mountinfo_identity_order() -> Result<Vec<u64>, Error> {
6008    mountinfo_identity_order_from_raw(&thread_mountinfo()?)
6009}
6010
6011/// [`capture_mountinfo_identity_order`], keeping every row whose mount ID is
6012/// in `keep` (the rows a container mount table shows) whatever its name: a
6013/// mount Hermit installed is never dropped by the seed filter, so a table
6014/// showing it validates against the captured order.
6015pub fn capture_mountinfo_identity_order_keeping(
6016    keep: &std::collections::BTreeSet<u64>,
6017) -> Result<Vec<u64>, Error> {
6018    mountinfo_identity_order_keeping_from_raw(&thread_mountinfo()?, keep)
6019}
6020
6021/// Each of [`BASE_MOUNTPOINTS`](detcore_model::container_mounts::BASE_MOUNTPOINTS)
6022/// that the calling thread can open, as the kernel escapes it in `mountinfo`,
6023/// with the mount ID of a descriptor held on it: rule 2's proof of
6024/// `ContainerMountTable::select`. The base mountpoints hold no byte the kernel
6025/// escapes (space, tab, newline or backslash), so each is its own escaped form.
6026pub fn base_mountpoint_mount_ids() -> Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64)> {
6027    detcore_model::container_mounts::BASE_MOUNTPOINTS
6028        .iter()
6029        .filter_map(|mountpoint| {
6030            let id = thread_mount_id_of(Path::new(mountpoint))?;
6031            Some((mountpoint.as_bytes().to_vec(), id))
6032        })
6033        .collect()
6034}
6035
6036/// A container mount table and the raw identity order Detcore validates it
6037/// against ([`unplanned_container_mount_table`]).
6038pub type UnplannedMountTable = (
6039    detcore_model::container_mounts::ContainerMountTable,
6040    Vec<u64>,
6041);
6042
6043// TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4213): Review
6044// the container mount table of a run in a namespace Hermit did not make: the
6045// membership rule of K3a with the launch mounts in place of Hermit's
6046// installations.
6047/// The container mount table of a run whose guest runs in the calling
6048/// thread's own mount namespace, in which Hermit installed no mount
6049/// (`--no-namespace`, or a library caller that built no container, on KVM),
6050/// and the raw identity order Detcore validates it against, both from one
6051/// read of the namespace's rows. Shown are:
6052/// - the launch mounts: the mount holding `launch_cwd`, the guest's working
6053///   directory at launch, and the mount holding the host's `/tmp`, which the
6054///   guest shares, with their ancestors (rules 1 and 3 of
6055///   `ContainerMountTable::select`, as for Hermit's installations), so that
6056///   `df .` and `findmnt -T .` from a checkout find their row;
6057/// - the base mountpoints mounted here (rule 2).
6058///
6059/// Both are facts of the launch, fixed before the guest starts, as the base
6060/// mountpoints are. No other host mount is shown; a file on one reports its
6061/// nearest shown ancestor. A shown row's parent is its nearest shown
6062/// ancestor, as for every table.
6063///
6064/// `launch_cwd` may be relative (`.` for the inherited working directory):
6065/// it is resolved from the calling thread's working directory as the guest's
6066/// `chdir` will resolve it, without asking that directory for its name, so a
6067/// removed working directory does not stop a launch with an absolute
6068/// `--workdir`.
6069pub fn unplanned_container_mount_table(launch_cwd: &Path) -> Result<UnplannedMountTable, Error> {
6070    unplanned_container_mount_table_with(launch_cwd, thread_mountinfo)
6071}
6072
6073/// [`unplanned_container_mount_table`], reading the mount table with `read`.
6074/// The launch directories and the base mountpoints are resolved and held
6075/// first, then the table is read, then the mount IDs are taken from the held
6076/// descriptors: a mount that resolving a launch directory creates (an
6077/// automount on its path) is already in the rows read, and one that leaves
6078/// afterwards is still named by them. A launch mount the read does not list
6079/// is refused, never dropped.
6080fn unplanned_container_mount_table_with(
6081    launch_cwd: &Path,
6082    read: impl FnOnce() -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error>,
6083) -> Result<UnplannedMountTable, Error> {
6084    let working = hold_path(launch_cwd, true).with_context(|| {
6085        format!(
6086            "the guest's working directory {} cannot be opened for its mount table",
6087            launch_cwd.display()
6088        )
6089    })?;
6090    // The host /tmp, which the guest shares, if there is one.
6091    let tmp = hold_path(Path::new("/tmp"), true).ok();
6092    let base = detcore_model::container_mounts::BASE_MOUNTPOINTS
6093        .iter()
6094        .filter_map(|mountpoint| Some((*mountpoint, hold_path(Path::new(mountpoint), false).ok()?)))
6095        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
6096    let raw = read()?;
6097    let launch = std::iter::once(&working)
6098        .chain(tmp.as_ref())
6099        .map(|held| {
6100            held_mount_id(held)
6101                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("a launch directory's mount ID cannot be read"))
6102        })
6103        .collect::<Result<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>, Error>>()?;
6104    let base = base
6105        .iter()
6106        .filter_map(|(mountpoint, held)| {
6107            Some((mountpoint.as_bytes().to_vec(), held_mount_id(held)?))
6108        })
6109        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
6110    unplanned_container_mount_table_from(&raw, &launch, &base)
6111}
6112
6113fn unplanned_container_mount_table_from(
6114    raw: &[u8],
6115    launch: &std::collections::BTreeSet<u64>,
6116    base: &[(Vec<u8>, u64)],
6117) -> Result<UnplannedMountTable, Error> {
6118    use detcore_model::container_mounts::ContainerMountTable;
6119    let rows = detcore_model::container_mounts::parse_container_mounts(raw)
6120        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("this thread's mount table has a malformed row"))?;
6121    if let Some(missing) = launch
6122        .iter()
6123        .find(|id| !rows.iter().any(|row| row.raw_mount_id == **id))
6124    {
6125        anyhow::bail!(
6126            "the launch mount {missing} (holding the guest's working directory or /tmp) is not in \
6127             this thread's mount table, read after it was resolved; refusing a table that would \
6128             omit the mount the guest starts on"
6129        );
6130    }
6131    let never = rows
6132        .iter()
6133        .filter(|row| row.is_ephemeral_host_seed())
6134        .map(|row| row.raw_mount_id)
6135        .collect();
6136    let table = ContainerMountTable::select(&rows, launch, base, &never);
6137    let order = mountinfo_identity_order_keeping_from_raw(raw, &table.shown_mount_ids())?;
6138    Ok((table, order))
6139}
6140
6141/// Producer provenance follows the guest mount model: ephemeral host seed rows
6142/// (other processes' squashfuse mounts) are not namespace members and must not
6143/// enter the captured identity order. Detcore drops the same rows with the same
6144/// filter when it captures the guest's mountinfo.
6145fn mountinfo_identity_order_from_raw(raw: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u64>, Error> {
6146    mountinfo_identity_order_keeping_from_raw(raw, &std::collections::BTreeSet::new())
6147}
6148
6149/// The identity order of the mountinfo contents `raw` (seed rows dropped, as
6150/// `mountinfo_identity_order_from_raw` drops them), keeping a seed row whose
6151/// mount ID is in `keep`.
6152pub fn mountinfo_identity_order_keeping_from_raw(
6153    raw: &[u8],
6154    keep: &std::collections::BTreeSet<u64>,
6155) -> Result<Vec<u64>, Error> {
6156    let mut kept = Vec::with_capacity(raw.len());
6157    for line in raw.split_inclusive(|byte| *byte == b'\n') {
6158        let body = line.strip_suffix(b"\n").unwrap_or(line);
6159        let id = body
6160            .split(|byte| *byte == b' ')
6161            .next()
6162            .and_then(|field| std::str::from_utf8(field).ok()?.parse::<u64>().ok());
6163        if !detcore_model::procfs::is_ephemeral_host_seed_mount(body)
6164            || id.is_some_and(|id| keep.contains(&id))
6165        {
6166            kept.extend_from_slice(line);
6167        }
6168    }
6169    mountinfo_identity_order_from(&kept)
6170}
6171
6172fn mountinfo_identity_order_from(contents: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u64>, Error> {
6173    use std::collections::BTreeSet;
6174
6175    let rows = detcore_model::procfs::parse_mountinfo(contents)
6176        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("malformed mountinfo"))?;
6177    let mut visible = Vec::new();
6178    let mut parents = Vec::new();
6179    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
6180    for row in rows {
6181        seen.insert(row.raw_mount_id);
6182        visible.push(row.raw_mount_id);
6183        parents.push(row.raw_parent_id);
6184    }
6185    for parent in parents {
6186        if seen.insert(parent) {
6187            visible.push(parent);
6188        }
6189    }
6190    Ok(visible)
6191}

6193impl<'a> From<Option<&'a PathBuf>> for HermitData {
6194    fn from(data_dir: Option<&'a PathBuf>) -> Self {
6195        data_dir.map_or_else(Self::new, Self::with_dir)

6199/// Records to an existing directory. The caller must keep its backing resources
6200/// alive through any [`HermitCleanupUnconfirmed`] recovery. [`HermitData::record`]
6201/// owns its temporary recording directory inside the retained operation.
6202///
6203/// The ptrace session runs on a tracer thread, so the calling thread needs no
6204/// particular stack; see [`run`].
6205pub fn record_to(command: Command, dir: &Path) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
6206    let dir = dir.to_owned();
6207    let command = tracer_thread::SendCommand::new(command);
6208    ptrace_completion::run_on_tracer_thread(None, move |control| async move {
6209        let command = command.into_inner();
6210        record_to_async(
6211            command,
6212            &dir,
6213            MountProvenance::default(),
6214            None,
6215            None,
6216            None,
6217            detcore_model::cpu_profile::CpuProfile::default(),
6218            control,
6219        )
6220        .await
6221    })
6222}

6224/// Records with producer-owned mountinfo provenance. The directory-lifetime
6225/// obligation is the same as [`record_to`]. `local_networking` and
6226/// `proc_level` are stored in the recording's `metadata.json`, and a replay
6227/// uses that network and that `/proc` level.
6228///
6229/// The ptrace session runs on a tracer thread, so the calling thread needs no
6230/// particular stack; see [`run`].
6231pub fn record_to_with_mountinfo(
6232    command: Command,
6233    dir: &Path,
6234    mountinfo: MountProvenance,
6235    local_networking: bool,
6236    proc_level: detcore_model::config::ProcLevel,
6237    cpu_profile: detcore_model::cpu_profile::CpuProfile,
6238) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
6239    let dir = dir.to_owned();
6240    let command = tracer_thread::SendCommand::new(command);
6241    ptrace_completion::run_on_tracer_thread(None, move |control| async move {
6242        let command = command.into_inner();
6243        let mut mountinfo = mountinfo;
6244        let mount_ids = match mountinfo.mount_ids.take() {
6245            Some(mount_ids) => mount_ids,
6246            None => capture_mountinfo_identity_order_keeping(
6247                &mountinfo
6248                    .container_mount_table
6249                    .as_ref()
6250                    .map(detcore_model::container_mounts::ContainerMountTable::shown_mount_ids)
6251                    .unwrap_or_default(),
6252            )?,
6253        };
6254        record_to_async(
6255            command,
6256            &dir,
6257            mountinfo,
6258            Some(mount_ids),
6259            Some(local_networking),
6260            Some(proc_level),
6261            cpu_profile,
6262            control,
6263        )
6264        .await
6265    })
6266}

6268// Private plumbing: Record::spawn_with_mountinfo's parameters plus the
6269// ptrace completion control.
6270#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
6271async fn record_to_async(
6272    command: Command,
6273    dir: &Path,
6274    mountinfo: MountProvenance,
6275    mountinfo_mount_ids: Option<Vec<u64>>,
6276    local_networking: Option<bool>,
6277    proc_level: Option<detcore_model::config::ProcLevel>,
6278    cpu_profile: detcore_model::cpu_profile::CpuProfile,
6279    control: std::rc::Rc<ptrace_completion::Control>,
6280) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
6281    let report = SkidOvershootReport::begin(true);
6282    let result = async {
6283        Record::spawn_with_mountinfo(
6284            command,
6285            dir,
6286            mountinfo,
6287            mountinfo_mount_ids,
6288            local_networking,
6289            proc_level,
6290            cpu_profile,
6291        )
6292        .await?
6293        .wait(control)
6294        .await
6295    }
6296    .await;
6297    report.finish(result)
6298}

6361        )
6362        .await
6363    })
6364}
6365
6366// Private plumbing: Record::spawn_with_mountinfo's parameters plus the
6367// ptrace completion control.
6368#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
6369async fn record_with_output_async(
6370    mut command: Command,
6371    dir: &Path,
6372    mountinfo: MountProvenance,
6373    mountinfo_mount_ids: Option<Vec<u64>>,
6374    local_networking: Option<bool>,
6375    proc_level: Option<detcore_model::config::ProcLevel>,
6376    cpu_profile: detcore_model::cpu_profile::CpuProfile,
6377    control: std::rc::Rc<ptrace_completion::Control>,
6378) -> Result<Output, Error> {
6379    let report = SkidOvershootReport::begin(true);
6380    command.stdin(Stdio::null());
6381    command.stdout(Stdio::piped());
6382    command.stderr(Stdio::piped());
6383    let result = async {
6384        Record::spawn_with_mountinfo(
6385            command,
6386            dir,
6387            mountinfo,
6388            mountinfo_mount_ids,
6389            local_networking,
6390            proc_level,
6391            cpu_profile,
6392        )
6393        .await?
6394        .wait_with_output(control)
6395        .await
6396    }
6397    .await;
6398    report.finish(result)
6399}

6401/// Replays an existing recording. Materialization and chroot guards remain with
6402/// the original runtime through any cleanup checkpoint.
6403///
6404/// The ptrace session runs on a tracer thread, so the calling thread needs no
6405/// particular stack; see [`run`].
6406pub fn replay_from(dir: &Path) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
6407    replay_plain(dir, None, &[])
6408}
6409
6410/// Replays with a gdb server.
6411///
6412/// The ptrace session runs on a tracer thread, so the calling thread needs no
6413/// particular stack; see [`run`].
6414pub fn replay_with_gdbserver(dir: &Path, port: u16) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
6415    replay_plain(dir, Some(port), &[])
6416}
6417
6418/// Replays with a gdb server and mounts inside the replay chroot.
6419///
6420/// The ptrace session runs on a tracer thread, so the calling thread needs no
6421/// particular stack; see [`run`].
6422pub fn replay_with_gdbserver_and_mounts(
6423    dir: &Path,
6424    port: u16,
6425    mounts: &[Mount],
6426) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
6427    replay_plain(dir, Some(port), mounts)
6428}
6429
6430fn replay_plain(dir: &Path, port: Option<u16>, mounts: &[Mount]) -> Result<ExitStatus, Error> {
6431    let dir = dir.to_owned();
6432    let mounts = mounts.to_vec();
6433    ptrace_completion::run_on_tracer_thread(None, move |control| async move {
6434        let report = SkidOvershootReport::begin(true);
6435        let result = async {
6436            Replay::spawn(&dir, false, port, &mounts)
6437                .await?
6438                .wait(control)
6439                .await
6440        }
6441        .await;
6442        report.finish(result)
6443    })
6444}
6445
6446/// Replays with captured output.
6447///
6448/// The ptrace session runs on a tracer thread, so the calling thread needs no
6449/// particular stack; see [`run`].
6450pub fn replay_with_output(dir: &Path) -> Result<Output, Error> {
6451    replay_with_output_and_mounts(dir, &[])
6452}
6453
6454/// Replays with captured output and mounts inside the replay chroot.
6455///
6456/// The ptrace session runs on a tracer thread, so the calling thread needs no
6457/// particular stack; see [`run`].
6458pub fn replay_with_output_and_mounts(dir: &Path, mounts: &[Mount]) -> Result<Output, Error> {
6459    let dir = dir.to_owned();
6460    let mounts = mounts.to_vec();
6461    ptrace_completion::run_on_tracer_thread(None, move |control| async move {
6462        let report = SkidOvershootReport::begin(true);
6463        let result = async {
6464            Replay::spawn(&dir, true, None, &mounts)
6465                .await?
6466                .wait_with_output(control)
6467                .await
6468        }
6469        .await;
6470        report.finish(result)
6471    })
6472}

6474#[cfg(test)]

6478    static SKID_OVERSHOOT_TEST_LOCK: std::sync::Mutex<()> = std::sync::Mutex::new(());

6480    /// Runs `check_tracing_environment` against probes that report `denied`
6481    /// as unavailable and every other probe as available; returns the refusal,
6482    /// if any, and the probes in the order they ran.
6483    fn check_with_denied(
6484        namespaces: NamespaceUse,
6485        denied: &[CapabilityProbe],
6486    ) -> (Option<String>, Vec<CapabilityProbe>) {
6487        let mut ran = Vec::new();
6488        let result = check_tracing_environment(namespaces, |probe| {
6489            ran.push(probe);
6490            Ok(!denied.contains(&probe))
6491        });
6492        (result.err().map(|error| error.to_string()), ran)
6493    }
6494
6495    /// Where unprivileged user namespaces are denied, a run that creates them
6496    /// is refused at the namespace probe, and a `--no-namespace` run, which
6497    /// never calls unshare, is not: it still passes the ptrace and seccomp
6498    /// probes (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4515).
6499    #[test]
6500    fn denied_namespaces_refuse_only_a_run_that_creates_them() {
6501        let denied = [CapabilityProbe::Namespaces];
6502        let (refusal, ran) = check_with_denied(NamespaceUse::Creates, &denied);
6503        assert!(
6504            refusal
6505                .as_deref()
6506                .is_some_and(|refusal| refusal.contains("unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWPID)")),
6507            "{refusal:?}"
6508        );
6509        assert_eq!(ran, [CapabilityProbe::Namespaces]);
6510        let (refusal, ran) = check_with_denied(NamespaceUse::None, &denied);
6511        assert_eq!(refusal, None);
6512        assert_eq!(ran, [CapabilityProbe::Ptrace, CapabilityProbe::Seccomp]);
6513    }
6514
6515    /// A `--no-namespace` run is still refused where ptrace or seccomp is
6516    /// denied: skipping the namespace probe skips nothing else.
6517    #[test]
6518    fn a_run_without_namespaces_still_needs_ptrace_and_seccomp() {
6519        for denied in [CapabilityProbe::Ptrace, CapabilityProbe::Seccomp] {
6520            let (refusal, _) = check_with_denied(NamespaceUse::None, &[denied]);
6521            let expected = match denied {
6522                CapabilityProbe::Ptrace => "PTRACE_TRACEME",
6523                _ => "SECCOMP_SET_MODE_FILTER",
6524            };
6525            assert!(
6526                refusal
6527                    .as_deref()
6528                    .is_some_and(|refusal| refusal.contains(expected)),
6529                "{denied:?}: {refusal:?}"
6530            );
6531        }
6532        let (refusal, ran) = check_with_denied(NamespaceUse::Creates, &[]);
6533        assert_eq!(refusal, None);
6534        assert_eq!(
6535            ran,
6536            [
6537                CapabilityProbe::Namespaces,
6538                CapabilityProbe::Ptrace,
6539                CapabilityProbe::Seccomp
6540            ]
6541        );
6542    }

6568                    20 10 0:7 / /test rw - tmpfs tmpfs rw\n\
6569                    30 10 0:51 / /mnt/xarfuse/stable-release rw - fuse.squashfuse_ll squashfuse_ll rw\n";

6634    /// Provenance the backend keeps without reading the namespace again must
6635    /// be well formed by itself: these are the refusals a second, live capture
6636    /// used to supply (Codex post-facto review of dh-dt0n).
6637    #[test]
6638    fn kvm_mountinfo_config_refuses_malformed_captured_provenance() {
6639        let rewrite = |raw_mount_id| detcore_model::config::MountInfoRootRewrite {
6640            raw_mount_id,
6641            deterministic_root: b"/".to_vec(),
6642            raw_root_prefix: None,
6643            deterministic_root_prefix: None,
6644            raw_mountpoint_prefix: None,
6645            deterministic_mountpoint_prefix: None,
6646        };
6647        let valid = DetConfig {
6648            mountinfo_mount_ids: vec![10, 20, 1],
6649            mountinfo_mount_ids_captured: true,
6650            mountinfo_mount_namespace: Some(NAMESPACE),
6651            mount_id_assignment_order: vec![20],
6652            mountinfo_root_rewrites: vec![rewrite(20)],
6653            ..DetConfig::default()
6654        };
6655        prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config(
6656            &mut valid.clone(),
6657            || Ok(NAMESPACE),
6658            || panic!("captured provenance is not read again"),
6659        )
6660        .unwrap();
6661        let cases = [
6662            (
6663                "duplicate",
6664                DetConfig {
6665                    mountinfo_mount_ids: vec![10, 10],
6666                    ..valid.clone()
6667                },
6668                "malformed",
6669            ),
6670            (
6671                "empty",
6672                DetConfig {
6673                    mountinfo_mount_ids: vec![],
6674                    ..valid.clone()
6675                },
6676                "malformed",
6677            ),
6678            (
6679                "assigned twice",
6680                DetConfig {
6681                    mount_id_assignment_order: vec![20, 20],
6682                    ..valid.clone()
6683                },
6684                "malformed",
6685            ),
6686            (
6687                "zero assigned, unlisted",
6688                DetConfig {
6689                    mount_id_assignment_order: vec![0],
6690                    ..valid.clone()
6691                },
6692                "malformed",
6693            ),
6694            (
6695                "rewrite outside",
6696                DetConfig {
6697                    mountinfo_root_rewrites: vec![rewrite(30)],
6698                    ..valid.clone()
6699                },
6700                "root rewrite names mount 30",
6701            ),
6702        ];
6703        for (name, mut config, expected) in cases {
6704            let before = serde_json::to_value(&config).unwrap();
6705            let error = prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config(
6706                &mut config,
6707                || panic!("{name}: malformed provenance is refused before any read"),
6708                || panic!("{name}: captured provenance is not read again"),
6709            )
6710            .unwrap_err();
6711            assert!(error.to_string().contains(expected), "{name}: {error:#}");
6712            assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&config).unwrap(), before, "{name}");
6713        }
6714    }

6726    /// A host mount copied into the container can leave it between the
6727    /// producer's capture and the backend's start: Linux detaches the mounts on
6728    /// a dentry in every mount namespace when a host process removes that
6729    /// directory (`__detach_mounts`). The backend keeps the producer's order,
6730    /// which still names the row, and does not refuse; the order Detcore later
6731    /// validates guest views against is the producer's
6732    /// (minibeads dh-dt0n).
6733    #[test]
6734    fn kvm_mountinfo_config_keeps_a_snapshot_whose_host_row_left_the_namespace() {
6735        let producer = b"10 1 8:1 / / rw - ext4 /dev/root rw\n\
6736                         20 10 0:22 / /proc rw - proc proc rw\n\
6737                         30 10 0:50 / /data/a rw - tmpfs tmpfs rw\n";
6738        let now = b"10 1 8:1 / / rw - ext4 /dev/root rw\n\
6739                    20 10 0:22 / /proc rw - proc proc rw\n";
6740        let order = mountinfo_identity_order_from(producer).unwrap();
6741        let mut config = DetConfig {
6742            mountinfo_mount_ids: order.clone(),
6743            mountinfo_mount_ids_captured: true,
6744            mountinfo_mount_namespace: Some(NAMESPACE),
6745            ..DetConfig::default()
6746        };
6747        prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config(
6748            &mut config,
6749            || Ok(NAMESPACE),
6750            || mountinfo_identity_order_from(now),
6751        )
6752        .unwrap();
6753        assert_eq!(config.mountinfo_mount_ids, order);
6754        assert_eq!(config.mountinfo_mount_ids, [10, 20, 30, 1]);
6755        assert!(detcore_model::procfs::mount_ids_are_ordered_subset(
6756            &mountinfo_identity_order_from(now).unwrap(),
6757            &config.mountinfo_mount_ids
6758        ));
6759    }

6824        let error = prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config(

6933                mountinfo_mount_ids: listed,
6934                mount_id_assignment_order: assigned,
6935                mountinfo_mount_namespace: namespace,
6936                ..DetConfig::default()
6937            };
6938            let before = serde_json::to_value(&config).unwrap();
6939            let error = prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config(
6940                &mut config,
6941                || panic!("must not overwrite incomplete provenance"),
6942                || panic!("must not overwrite incomplete provenance"),
6943            )
6944            .unwrap_err();
6945            assert!(error.to_string().contains("no producer-captured namespace"));
6946            assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&config).unwrap(), before);

6950    /// The container mount table Detcore renders on KVM must name mounts of
6951    /// the namespace the backend captured
6952    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4213, K3a).
6953    #[test]
6954    fn kvm_mountinfo_config_refuses_a_mount_table_of_another_namespace() {
6955        let namespace = b"10 1 8:1 / / rw - ext4 /dev/root rw\n\
6956                          20 10 0:22 / /proc rw - proc proc rw\n\
6957                          40 10 0:23 / /elsewhere rw - tmpfs tmpfs rw\n";
6958        let rows = detcore_model::container_mounts::parse_container_mounts(namespace).unwrap();
6959        let table = |installed: &[u64]| {
6960            detcore_model::container_mounts::ContainerMountTable::select(
6961                &rows,
6962                &installed.iter().copied().collect(),
6963                &[],
6964                &std::collections::BTreeSet::new(),
6965            )
6966        };
6967        let config = |table| DetConfig {
6968            mountinfo_mount_ids: vec![10, 20, 1],
6969            mountinfo_mount_ids_captured: true,
6970            mountinfo_mount_namespace: Some(NAMESPACE),
6971            container_mount_table: Some(table),
6972            ..DetConfig::default()
6973        };
6974        let snapshot = || -> Result<Vec<u64>, Error> { panic!("the snapshot is kept") };
6975        let mut matching = config(table(&[20]));
6976        prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config(&mut matching, || Ok(NAMESPACE), snapshot).unwrap();
6977        let mut stale = config(table(&[40]));
6978        let error =
6979            prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config(&mut stale, || Ok(NAMESPACE), snapshot).unwrap_err();
6980        assert!(error.to_string().contains("names mount 40"), "{error:#}");
6981    }

6983    /// A run in a namespace Hermit made no mount in shows only the base
6984    /// mountpoints mounted at their very paths, maps a file on any other
6985    /// mount to its nearest shown ancestor, and validates against an order
6986    /// read from the same bytes (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4213).
6987    #[test]
6988    fn an_unplanned_table_shows_only_the_base_mountpoints() {
6989        let namespace = b"10 1 8:1 / / rw - ext4 /dev/root rw\n\
6990                          20 10 0:22 / /proc rw - proc proc rw\n\
6991                          30 10 0:23 / /dev rw - devtmpfs dev rw\n\
6992                          40 10 0:24 / /data/eden rw - fuse.edenfs eden rw\n\
6993                          41 30 0:25 / /dev/shm rw - tmpfs tmpfs rw\n\
6994                          50 10 0:26 / /run/user/1000 rw - tmpfs tmpfs rw\n";
6995        // /run is no mount here: its descriptor reaches the root mount.
6996        let base = [
6997            (b"/".to_vec(), 10),
6998            (b"/proc".to_vec(), 20),
6999            (b"/dev".to_vec(), 30),
7000            (b"/dev/shm".to_vec(), 41),
7001            (b"/run".to_vec(), 10),
7002        ];
7003        for mountpoint in detcore_model::container_mounts::BASE_MOUNTPOINTS {
7004            assert!(
7005                !mountpoint.bytes().any(|byte| b" \t\n\\".contains(&byte)),
7006                "{mountpoint} needs mountinfo escaping"
7007            );
7008        }
7009        let no_launch = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
7010        let (table, order) =
7011            unplanned_container_mount_table_from(namespace, &no_launch, &base).unwrap();
7012        assert_eq!(table.shown_mount_ids(), [10, 20, 30, 41].into());
7013        assert_eq!(table.shown_mount_id(40), 10);
7014        assert_eq!(table.shown_mount_id(50), 10);
7015        assert_eq!(order, [10, 20, 30, 40, 41, 50, 1]);
7016        let rendered = String::from_utf8(table.mountinfo()).unwrap();
7017        assert!(!rendered.contains("/data/eden") && !rendered.contains("/run/user"));
7018        // A launch from a checkout on /data/eden shows that mount too; a
7019        // file on the still hidden /run/user/1000 reports the root.
7020        let launch = [40].into();
7021        let (table, order) =
7022            unplanned_container_mount_table_from(namespace, &launch, &base).unwrap();
7023        assert_eq!(table.shown_mount_ids(), [10, 20, 30, 40, 41].into());
7024        assert_eq!(table.shown_mount_id(40), 40);
7025        assert_eq!(table.shown_mount_id(50), 10);
7026        assert_eq!(order, [10, 20, 30, 40, 41, 50, 1]);
7027    }

7029    /// Runs test `name` again under `unshare --user --map-root-user
7030    /// --mount`, where it may mount, and returns true in this process, which
7031    /// then has nothing more to check; returns false in that child, which runs
7032    /// the test's body. `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)` refuses a multithreaded
7033    /// process, so the test cannot enter one itself. Where user namespaces
7034    /// are unavailable the test is skipped, saying why.
7035    fn rerun_in_user_namespace(name: &str) -> bool {
7036        const CHILD: &str = "HERMIT_TEST_USER_NAMESPACE_CHILD";
7037        if std::env::var_os(CHILD).is_some() {
7038            return false;
7039        }
7040        let probe = std::process::Command::new("unshare")
7041            .args(["--user", "--map-root-user", "--mount", "true"])
7042            .output();
7043        if !probe.as_ref().is_ok_and(|probe| probe.status.success()) {
7044            eprintln!("SKIPPED {name}: user namespaces are unavailable here: {probe:?}");
7045            return true;
7046        }
7047        let output = std::process::Command::new("unshare")
7048            .args(["--user", "--map-root-user", "--mount", "--"])
7049            .arg(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
7050            .args(["--exact", name, "--nocapture", "--test-threads=1"])
7051            .env(CHILD, "1")
7052            .output()
7053            .expect("run the test under unshare");
7054        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
7055        assert!(
7056            output.status.success() && stdout.contains("1 passed"),
7057            "the child failed or ran no test:\n{stdout}\n{}",
7058            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
7059        );
7060        true
7061    }

7063    /// A library caller's thread with a mount namespace of its own captures
7064    /// its own namespace's rows, identity and mount IDs (all through
7065    /// `/proc/thread-self`), not the thread group leader's: otherwise the
7066    /// leader's rows and the thread's descriptor mount IDs never meet, and
7067    /// the table shows nothing, not even `/`. A thread may unshare its mount
7068    /// namespace only with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, which an unprivileged test gets in
7069    /// a user namespace of its own (`rerun_in_user_namespace`); there the test
7070    /// thread, not the leader, unshares the mount namespace.
7071    #[test]
7072    fn a_thread_with_its_own_mount_namespace_captures_its_own_view() {
7073        use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
7074        if rerun_in_user_namespace(
7075            "tests::a_thread_with_its_own_mount_namespace_captures_its_own_view",
7076        ) {
7077            return;
7078        }
7079        let checked = std::thread::spawn(|| {
7080            // SAFETY: unshare takes no pointer.
7081            assert_eq!(
7082                unsafe { libc::unshare(libc::CLONE_NEWNS) },
7083                0,
7084                "unshare(CLONE_NEWNS): {}",
7085                io::Error::last_os_error()
7086            );
7087            let own = current_mount_namespace().unwrap();
7088            let leader = fs::metadata("/proc/self/ns/mnt").unwrap();
7089            assert_ne!(
7090                own.inode,
7091                leader.ino(),
7092                "the thread kept the leader's namespace"
7093            );
7094            let (table, order) = unplanned_container_mount_table(Path::new(".")).unwrap();
7095            assert!(
7096                table
7097                    .mounts
7098                    .iter()
7099                    .any(|row| row.mountpoint.as_slice() == b"/"),
7100                "the thread's table shows no /: {table:?}"
7101            );
7102            let root = thread_mount_id_of(Path::new("/")).unwrap();
7103            assert!(table.shown_mount_ids().contains(&root));
7104            assert!(table.shown_mount_ids().iter().all(|id| order.contains(id)));
7105        })
7106        .join();
7107        assert!(checked.is_ok(), "the thread's checks failed");
7108    }
7109
7110    /// The launch directory is resolved and held before the mount table is
7111    /// read: a mount made on it between the two (here a tmpfs over it, in a
7112    /// user and mount namespace of the test's own) is not the launch mount,
7113    /// because the held directory is below it; the mount the directory was
7114    /// on is, and it is in the rows read. Had the directory been resolved
7115    /// after the read, it would have reached the new tmpfs. The same order
7116    /// puts a mount that resolving the directory triggers (an automount on
7117    /// its path) in the rows read.
7118    #[test]
7119    fn launch_directories_are_held_before_the_mount_table_is_read() {
7120        if rerun_in_user_namespace(
7121            "tests::launch_directories_are_held_before_the_mount_table_is_read",
7122        ) {
7123            return;
7124        }
7125        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
7126        let launch = directory.path().join("launch");
7127        fs::create_dir(&launch).unwrap();
7128        let before = thread_mount_id_of(&launch).unwrap();
7129        let target = launch.clone();
7130        let (table, _) = unplanned_container_mount_table_with(&launch, move || {
7131            let status = std::process::Command::new("mount")
7132                .args(["-t", "tmpfs", "none"])
7133                .arg(&target)
7134                .status()
7135                .expect("run mount");
7136            assert!(status.success(), "mount a tmpfs over the launch directory");
7137            thread_mountinfo()
7138        })
7139        .unwrap();
7140        let over = thread_mount_id_of(&launch).unwrap();
7141        assert_ne!(over, before, "the tmpfs did not cover the launch directory");
7142        assert!(table.shown_mount_ids().contains(&before));
7143        assert!(!table.shown_mount_ids().contains(&over));
7144        let _ = std::process::Command::new("umount").arg(&launch).status();
7145    }

7158    #[test]
7159    fn skid_overshoot_report_covers_success_error_and_disabled_backends() {
7160        let _lock = SKID_OVERSHOOT_TEST_LOCK.lock().unwrap();
7161        let _ = reverie::take_skid_overshoot_count();
7162
7163        reverie::record_skid_overshoot();
7164        let empty_run = SkidOvershootReport::begin(true);
7165        assert_eq!(
7166            reverie::take_skid_overshoot_count(),
7167            0,
7168            "begin must clear evidence from a previous invocation"
7169        );
7170        empty_run.finish(Ok::<_, Error>(())).unwrap();
7171
7172        let success = SkidOvershootReport::begin(true);
7173        reverie::record_skid_overshoot();
7174        reverie::record_skid_overshoot();
7175        let error = success.finish(Ok::<_, Error>(7)).unwrap_err();
7176        assert_eq!(
7177            error
7178                .downcast_ref::<SkidOvershootError>()
7179                .expect("skid refusal must remain typed")
7180                .count(),
7181            2
7182        );
7183        assert!(
7184            error
7185                .to_string()
7186                .contains("observed 2 HERMIT_SKID_OVERSHOOT report(s)"),
7187            "{error:#}"
7188        );
7189        assert!(
7190            error
7191                .to_string()
7192                .contains("deterministic execution was not established"),
7193            "{error:#}"
7194        );
7195        assert_eq!(reverie::take_skid_overshoot_count(), 0);
7196
7197        let error = SkidOvershootReport::begin(true);
7198        reverie::record_skid_overshoot();
7199        let error = error
7200            .finish(Err::<(), _>(anyhow!("guest failed")))
7201            .unwrap_err();
7202        assert!(error.downcast_ref::<SkidOvershootError>().is_some());
7203        let error = format!("{error:#}");
7204        assert!(error.contains("guest failed"), "{error}");
7205        assert!(
7206            error.contains("observed 1 HERMIT_SKID_OVERSHOOT report(s)"),
7207            "{error}"
7208        );
7209        assert_eq!(reverie::take_skid_overshoot_count(), 0);
7210
7211        reverie::record_skid_overshoot();
7212        let disabled = SkidOvershootReport::begin(false);
7213        disabled.finish(Ok::<_, Error>(())).unwrap();
7214        assert_eq!(
7215            reverie::take_skid_overshoot_count(),
7216            1,
7217            "a backend that cannot produce ptrace PMU overshoots must not consume another run's evidence"
7218        );
7219    }

7235    fn write_guest_program(directory: &Path, name: &str, bytes: &[u8], mode: u32) -> PathBuf {
7236        let path = directory.join(name);
7237        fs::write(&path, bytes).unwrap();
7238        fs::set_permissions(&path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(mode)).unwrap();
7239        // The kernel may clear a set-group-ID bit that this user cannot set;
7240        // a test that silently lost its bit would test nothing.
7241        assert_eq!(
7242            fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().permissions().mode() & 0o7777,
7243            mode,
7244            "{}",
7245            path.display()
7246        );
7247        path
7248    }

7316    /// A failure recorded during an in-guest run fails the settle step and
7317    /// latches a determinism loss, so verification refuses the run (Codex
7318    /// implementation review, HIGH 3 and 4).
7319    #[tokio::test]
7320    #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
7321    async fn a_recorded_in_guest_failure_fails_the_run_and_latches_a_loss() {
7322        use std::os::fd::FromRawFd;
7323
7324        use reverie::GlobalTool;
7325        use reverie_rpc_transport::ConnectionAdmission;
7326
7327        let config = DetConfig::default().with_backend(|backend| {
7328            backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously = true;
7329        });
7330        let global_state = detcore::GlobalState::init_global_state(&config).await;
7331        let exits = in_guest_exits::InGuestExitAdmission::default();
7332        // Admitting before any reporter is attached is refused and recorded.
7333        let fd = unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_pidfd_open, std::process::id() as i32, 0) };
7334        assert!(fd >= 0);
7335        let pidfd = unsafe { std::os::fd::OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(fd as i32) };
7336        assert!(exits.admit(pidfd).is_err());
7337        let error = settle_in_guest_exits(&exits, &global_state)
7338            .await
7339            .expect_err("a recorded failure must fail the run");
7340        assert!(
7341            error
7342                .to_string()
7343                .starts_with("in-guest LiteInst refused a guest connection:"),
7344            "{error}"
7345        );
7346        assert!(detcore::detlog::determinism_loss().is_some());
7347    }

7384    /// in-guest-trap sets `REVERIE_LITEINST_SITE_PATCHING=0` on the guest
7385    /// command when the guest environment leaves it unset or already `0`, and
7386    /// refuses, before anything starts, an environment that sets any other
7387    /// value; the refusal names the value and both ways out. liteinst neither
7388    /// refuses nor changes the variable.
7389    #[test]
7390    #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
7391    fn in_guest_trap_refuses_a_guest_environment_that_turns_site_patching_on() {
7392        use std::ffi::OsStr;
7393
7394        let name = reverie_liteinst::SITE_PATCHING_ENV;
7395        let mut unset = Command::new("/bin/true");
7396        unset.env_remove(name);
7397        assert_eq!(
7398            in_guest_trap_site_patching_conflict(&unset, Backend::InGuestTrap),
7399            None
7400        );
7401        force_in_guest_site_patching(&mut unset, Backend::InGuestTrap);
7402        assert_eq!(unset.get_env(name).as_deref(), Some(OsStr::new("0")));
7403
7404        let mut zero = Command::new("/bin/true");
7405        zero.env(name, "0");
7406        assert_eq!(
7407            in_guest_trap_site_patching_conflict(&zero, Backend::InGuestTrap),
7408            None
7409        );
7410
7411        for value in ["1", "", "yes", " 0"] {
7412            let mut command = Command::new("/bin/true");
7413            command.env(name, value);
7414            let conflict = in_guest_trap_site_patching_conflict(&command, Backend::InGuestTrap)
7415                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{value:?} was accepted"));
7416            assert!(conflict.contains(&format!("{name}={value},")), "{conflict}");
7417            assert!(conflict.contains("--backend=liteinst"), "{conflict}");
7418            assert!(conflict.contains("drop the variable"), "{conflict}");
7419            // The whole refusal path stops on it first, before the program,
7420            // kernel or timeslice checks, and leaves the value untouched.
7421            let error = refuse_in_guest_liteinst_run(
7422                &mut command,
7423                &DetConfig::default(),
7424                Backend::InGuestTrap,
7425            )
7426            .unwrap_err();
7427            let refusal = error
7428                .downcast_ref::<LiteinstInGuestRefusal>()
7429                .expect("a typed in-guest refusal, which the CLI reports as exit 122");
7430            assert!(
7431                refusal.to_string().starts_with(
7432                    "--backend=in-guest-trap (in-guest LiteInst, site patching off) refuses \
7433                     this run: the guest environment sets"
7434                ),
7435                "{refusal}"
7436            );
7437            assert_eq!(command.get_env(name).as_deref(), Some(OsStr::new(value)));
7438
7439            // liteinst takes the variable from the guest environment as it is.
7440            let mut liteinst = Command::new("/bin/true");
7441            liteinst.env(name, value);
7442            assert_eq!(
7443                in_guest_trap_site_patching_conflict(&liteinst, Backend::Liteinst),
7444                None
7445            );
7446            force_in_guest_site_patching(&mut liteinst, Backend::Liteinst);
7447            assert_eq!(liteinst.get_env(name).as_deref(), Some(OsStr::new(value)));
7448        }
7449    }

7451    /// The coordinator's postcondition for an in-guest-trap run: a record
7452    /// with no patched and no candidate site passes; a patched site, a
7453    /// candidate, an unmeasured count or a missing record is refused, with a
7454    /// typed in-guest refusal and a determinism loss. Other backends are not
7455    /// held to it.
7456    #[test]
7457    #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
7458    fn an_in_guest_trap_run_that_patched_a_site_is_refused_after_it_ends() {
7459        let record = |candidates: Option<u64>, patched: Option<u64>| {
7460            reverie::DispatchStats::new(
7461                "in-guest-trap",
7462                reverie::DispatchCounters::ZERO,
7463                reverie::SiteCounters {
7464                    candidates,
7465                    patched,
7466                    fell_back: Some(0),
7467                },
7468            )
7469        };
7470        let clean = record(Some(0), Some(0));
7471        assert_eq!(
7472            in_guest_trap_patching_evidence(Backend::InGuestTrap, Some(&clean), 1),
7473            None
7474        );
7475        for (candidates, patched, shown) in [
7476            (Some(3), Some(3), "3 patched and 3 candidate"),
7477            (Some(1), Some(0), "0 patched and 1 candidate"),
7478            (Some(0), None, "unmeasured patched and 0 candidate"),
7479        ] {
7480            let reason = in_guest_trap_patching_evidence(
7481                Backend::InGuestTrap,
7482                Some(&record(candidates, patched)),
7483                1,
7484            )
7485            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{candidates:?} {patched:?} was accepted"));
7486            assert!(reason.contains(shown), "{reason}");
7487        }
7488        assert!(
7489            in_guest_trap_patching_evidence(Backend::InGuestTrap, None, 1)
7490                .is_some_and(|reason| reason.contains("no LiteInst dispatch record"))
7491        );
7492        // An empty record from guests that collected nothing is not zero.
7493        assert!(
7494            in_guest_trap_patching_evidence(Backend::InGuestTrap, Some(&clean), 0)
7495                .is_some_and(|reason| reason.contains("no guest process reported"))
7496        );
7497        let patched = record(Some(3), Some(3));
7498        assert_eq!(
7499            in_guest_trap_patching_evidence(Backend::Liteinst, Some(&patched), 1),
7500            None
7501        );
7502        assert_eq!(
7503            in_guest_trap_patching_evidence(Backend::Liteinst, None, 0),
7504            None
7505        );
7506
7507        refuse_in_guest_trap_patching(Backend::InGuestTrap, None).unwrap();
7508        let error = refuse_in_guest_trap_patching(
7509            Backend::InGuestTrap,
7510            in_guest_trap_patching_evidence(Backend::InGuestTrap, Some(&patched), 1),
7511        )
7512        .unwrap_err();
7513        assert!(
7514            error.downcast_ref::<LiteinstInGuestRefusal>().is_some(),
7515            "{error:#}"
7516        );
7517        assert!(
7518            error
7519                .to_string()
7520                .starts_with("--backend=in-guest-trap (in-guest LiteInst, site patching off)"),
7521            "{error:#}"
7522        );
7523        assert!(
7524            detcore::detlog::determinism_loss().is_some_and(|loss| loss.contains("3 patched")),
7525            "the refusal must record a determinism loss"
7526        );
7527    }

7545    /// A configuration that already carries a reserved-signal set (it is a
7546    /// public, serialized field) never keeps it through Hermit's preparation:
7547    /// every backend's preparation, the loader route's
7548    /// (`prepare_in_guest_loader_route_config`, which `hermit run`'s
7549    /// exec-stop, native-exec and mapped-first-admission launchers use) and
7550    /// the native-exec verify route's leave it empty. Only the default
7551    /// in-guest route sets it afterwards, from the backend and the
7552    /// subscription alone, never from the input.
7553    #[test]
7554    fn a_poisoned_reserved_signal_set_never_survives_preparation() {
7555        let poisoned = DetConfig {
7556            in_guest_reserved_signals: u64::MAX,

7558        };
