7560            let prepared = prepare_backend_config(poisoned.clone(), backend);
7561            assert_eq!(prepared.in_guest_reserved_signals, 0, "{backend:?}");
7562            let expected = if backend.is_in_guest_liteinst() {
7563                in_guest_reserved_signals(
7564                    &prepare_backend_config(DetConfig::default(), backend),
7565                    backend,
7566                )
7567            } else {
7568                0
7569            };

7571                in_guest_reserved_signals(&prepared, backend),
7572                expected,

7577        assert_eq!(loader.in_guest_reserved_signals, 0);
7578        assert!(loader.in_guest_site_patching_off);
7579        assert_eq!(loader.backend, backend_capabilities(Backend::InGuestTrap));

7612    /// A configuration that every condition of the in-guest delivery gate
7613    /// holds for, on `backend`, as the default route's launch leaves it
7614    /// before it sets the gate: prepared, with site patching off.
7615    fn gate_ready(backend: Backend) -> DetConfig {
7616        let mut config = prepare_backend_config(
7617            DetConfig {
7618                sequentialize_threads: true,
7619                max_timeslice: None,
7620                ..DetConfig::default()
7621            },
7622            backend,
7623        );
7624        config.in_guest_site_patching_off = true;
7625        config

7628    /// A configuration that already turns the in-guest delivery gate on (a
7629    /// public, serialized field) never keeps it through Hermit's
7630    /// preparation: every backend's preparation and the loader route's (the
7631    /// exec-stop, native-exec and mapped-first-admission launchers, and the
7632    /// native-exec verify route) turn it off, also where every other
7633    /// condition holds (A5 step 3c.1, D35, D43, D52). Only the default
7634    /// route's launch sets it afterwards. Mutation it catches: the reset in
7635    /// `prepare_backend_config` removed.
7636    #[test]
7637    fn a_poisoned_signal_delivery_gate_never_survives_preparation() {
7638        let poisoned = DetConfig {
7639            in_guest_signal_delivery: true,
7640            sequentialize_threads: true,
7641            max_timeslice: None,
7642            in_guest_site_patching_off: true,
7643            ..DetConfig::default()
7644        };
7645        for backend in Backend::ALL {
7646            let prepared = prepare_backend_config(poisoned.clone(), backend);
7647            assert!(!prepared.in_guest_signal_delivery, "{backend:?}");
7648        }
7649        let loader = prepare_in_guest_loader_route_config(poisoned);
7650        assert!(!loader.in_guest_signal_delivery);
7651        assert!(loader.in_guest_site_patching_off);
7652        assert_eq!(loader.backend, backend_capabilities(Backend::InGuestTrap));

7655    /// D35's gate holds only for an in-guest backend with site patching off,
7656    /// sequentialized threads, none of the configurations in which Detcore
7657    /// cannot keep the two-phase protocol (D33: each one alone turns the gate
7658    /// off), and a launcher that owns the guest's PID namespace (D51).
7659    #[test]
7660    fn the_signal_delivery_gate_needs_every_condition() {
7661        let owned = true;
7662        for backend in Backend::ALL {
7663            let ready = gate_ready(backend);
7664            assert_eq!(
7665                in_guest_signal_delivery_gate(&ready, backend, owned),
7666                backend.is_in_guest_liteinst(),
7667                "{backend:?}"
7668            );
7669        }
7670        for backend in [Backend::Liteinst, Backend::InGuestTrap] {
7671            let ready = gate_ready(backend);
7672            assert!(detcore::two_phase_refusal(&ready).is_none(), "{backend:?}");
7673            let off = |change: &dyn Fn(&mut DetConfig)| {
7674                let mut config = ready.clone();
7675                change(&mut config);
7676                !in_guest_signal_delivery_gate(&config, backend, owned)
7677            };
7678            assert!(
7679                off(&|c| c.in_guest_site_patching_off = false),
7680                "{backend:?}"
7681            );
7682            assert!(off(&|c| c.sequentialize_threads = false), "{backend:?}");
7683            // D33's flags, each refused by `two_phase_refusal`.
7684            assert!(
7685                off(&|c| c.target_timeslice = std::num::NonZeroU64::new(1_000)),
7686                "{backend:?}"
7687            );
7688            assert!(
7689                off(&|c| c.max_timeslice = std::num::NonZeroU64::new(1_000)),
7690                "{backend:?}"
7691            );
7692            assert!(off(&|c| c.record_preemptions = true), "{backend:?}");
7693            assert!(
7694                off(&|c| c.replay_schedule_from = Some(PathBuf::from("schedule.json"))),
7695                "{backend:?}"
7696            );
7697            let mut pipe = ready.clone();
7698            pipe.pipe_wake_latency = Some(1_000);
7699            assert!(pipe.pipe_wake_latency_in_effect().is_some());
7700            assert!(
7701                !in_guest_signal_delivery_gate(&pipe, backend, owned),
7702                "{backend:?}"
7703            );
7704            // D51: no PID namespace the launcher owns.
7705            assert!(
7706                !in_guest_signal_delivery_gate(&ready, backend, false),
7707                "{backend:?}"
7708            );
7709        }
7710    }

7712    /// `scheduler_owns_guest_pid_namespace` in a forked process, plain or
7713    /// the first process of a new user and PID namespace, as its exit status
7714    /// (1 owned, 0 not, 2 when a step failed).
7715    fn ownership_in_child(new_pid_namespace: bool) -> i32 {
7716        let observe = || i32::from(scheduler_owns_guest_pid_namespace());
7717        // SAFETY: plain process calls; each forked process calls only getpid,
7718        // unshare, fork, waitpid and _exit before it exits.
7719        unsafe {
7720            let launcher = libc::fork();
7721            assert!(launcher >= 0, "fork failed");
7722            if launcher == 0 {
7723                if !new_pid_namespace {
7724                    libc::_exit(observe());
7725                }
7726                if libc::unshare(libc::CLONE_NEWUSER | libc::CLONE_NEWPID) != 0 {
7727                    libc::_exit(2);
7728                }
7729                let init = libc::fork();
7730                if init == 0 {
7731                    libc::_exit(observe());
7732                }
7733                let mut status = 0;
7734                if init < 0
7735                    || libc::waitpid(init, &mut status, 0) != init
7736                    || !libc::WIFEXITED(status)
7737                {
7738                    libc::_exit(2);
7739                }
7740                libc::_exit(libc::WEXITSTATUS(status));
7741            }
7742            let mut status = 0;
7743            assert_eq!(libc::waitpid(launcher, &mut status, 0), launcher);
7744            assert!(libc::WIFEXITED(status), "wait status {status:#x}");
7745            libc::WEXITSTATUS(status)
7746        }
7747    }
7748
7749    /// D52: ownership of the guests' PID namespace is derived from the
7750    /// process, not supplied. The first process of a new user and PID
7751    /// namespace (PID 1 there, as `hermit run`'s container init is) owns it;
7752    /// a plain child, as under `--no-namespace`, does not, and neither does
7753    /// this test process. Mutation it catches: ownership forced true.
7754    #[test]
7755    fn only_a_pid_namespace_init_owns_the_guests_namespace() {
7756        assert!(!scheduler_owns_guest_pid_namespace());
7757        assert_eq!(
7758            ownership_in_child(false),
7759            0,
7760            "a plain child owns no namespace"
7761        );
7762        assert_eq!(
7763            ownership_in_child(true),
7764            1,
7765            "the init of a new PID namespace owns it (2: no user and PID namespace)"
7766        );
7767    }

7775    fn no_launch_outside_a_new_pid_namespace_and_no_3c1a_launch_turns_the_gate_on() {

7796    /// D25: the guest's check logs the limit it found, unchanged when
7797    /// already unlimited and raised otherwise, and a limit it could not raise
7798    /// refuses the run, naming both values and the errno.
7799    #[test]
7800    #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
7801    fn an_in_guest_launch_logs_the_cpu_limit_it_found_and_refuses_one_it_cannot_raise() {
7802        let limit = |rlim_cur, rlim_max| libc::rlimit { rlim_cur, rlim_max };
7803        let unchanged = rlimit_cpu_report_line(limit(libc::RLIM_INFINITY, libc::RLIM_INFINITY));
7804        assert!(
7805            unchanged.contains(
7806                "was soft unlimited hard unlimited, the value Detcore reports; the guest starts \
7807                 with it unchanged"
7808            ),
7809            "{unchanged}"
7810        );
7811        let raised = rlimit_cpu_report_line(limit(1, libc::RLIM_INFINITY));
7812        assert!(
7813            raised.contains(
7814                "was soft 1s hard unlimited; Hermit sets it to soft unlimited hard unlimited"
7815            ),
7816            "{raised}"
7817        );
7818        let refused = rlimit_cpu_refusal(limit(3600, 7200), nix::errno::Errno::EPERM);
7819        assert!(
7820            refused.starts_with(
7821                "the guest would inherit a finite physical RLIMIT_CPU (soft 3600s, hard 7200s), \
7822                 and Hermit cannot raise it (EPERM: "
7823            ),
7824            "{refused}"
7825        );
7826        assert!(refused.contains("D25"), "{refused}");
7827    }

7829    /// D25: what the guest's own check reports through its pipe becomes the
7830    /// refusal naming the descriptor and why (an unreadable one, or a table
7831    /// that cannot be listed, with its errno; an unraisable `RLIMIT_CPU` with
7832    /// its values), or, for a check that passed, the limit to log; an empty
7833    /// pipe (the check never ran) names nothing.
7834    #[test]
7835    #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
7836    fn the_launch_audit_reports_what_the_guest_check_found() {
7837        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
7838        let mut command = Command::new("/bin/true");
7839        let audit = LaunchAudit::install(&mut command).unwrap();
7840        let pipe = &audit.pipe;
7841        assert_eq!(pipe.read_report(), None);
7842        let write = |report: LaunchReport| {
7843            let bytes = report.encode();
7844            // SAFETY: a write of a local array.
7845            let written =
7846                unsafe { libc::write(pipe._write.as_raw_fd(), bytes.as_ptr().cast(), bytes.len()) };
7847            assert_eq!(written, bytes.len() as isize);
7848        };
7849        let report = |kind, bits, errno: i32, fd, rlimit| LaunchReport {
7850            kind,
7851            bits,
7852            errno: errno as u8,
7853            fd,
7854            rlimit,
7855        };
7856        for (sent, what) in [
7857            (
7858                report(
7859                    audit_bits::PRODUCER,
7860                    audit_bits::O_ASYNC | audit_bits::OWNER,
7861                    0,
7862                    0,
7863                    (0, 0),
7864                ),
7865                "the guest would inherit descriptor 0, which is already a signal producer: it has \
7866                 O_ASYNC and an owner",
7867            ),
7868            (
7869                report(
7870                    audit_bits::PRODUCER,
7871                    audit_bits::SOCKET | audit_bits::OWNER,
7872                    0,
7873                    1,
7874                    (0, 0),
7875                ),
7876                "descriptor 1, which is already a signal producer: it is a socket with an owner",
7877            ),
7878            (
7879                report(audit_bits::PRODUCER, audit_bits::LEASE, 0, 300, (0, 0)),
7880                "descriptor 300, which is already a signal producer: it holds a lease",
7881            ),
7882            (
7883                report(audit_bits::UNREADABLE, 0, libc::EACCES, 7, (0, 0)),
7884                "descriptor 7, whose signal owner and flags cannot be read (EACCES",
7885            ),
7886            (
7887                report(audit_bits::UNLISTED, 0, libc::EMFILE, -1, (0, 0)),
7888                "descriptor table could not be listed from /proc/self/fd (EMFILE",
7889            ),
7890            (
7891                report(audit_bits::RLIMIT_CPU, 0, libc::EPERM, -1, (3600, 3600)),
7892                "finite physical RLIMIT_CPU (soft 3600s, hard 3600s), and Hermit cannot raise it \
7893                 (EPERM",
7894            ),
7895        ] {
7896            write(sent);
7897            let received = pipe.read_report().unwrap();
7898            assert_eq!(received, sent);
7899            let reason = received.refusal().unwrap();
7900            assert!(reason.contains(what), "{reason}");
7901        }
7902        let passed = report(audit_bits::PASSED, 0, 0, -1, (1, libc::RLIM_INFINITY));
7903        write(passed);
7904        let received = pipe.read_report().unwrap();
7905        assert_eq!(received.refusal(), None);
7906        assert_eq!(
7907            rlimit_cpu_report_line(received.limit()),
7908            rlimit_cpu_report_line(libc::rlimit {
7909                rlim_cur: 1,
7910                rlim_max: libc::RLIM_INFINITY
7911            })
7912        );
7913        assert_eq!(pipe.read_report(), None);
7914    }
7915
7916    /// D25: the guest's check reads its whole descriptor table and skips
7917    /// close-on-exec descriptors and its own pipe: in this process, a pipe
7918    /// with O_ASYNC and an owner is reported only once its close-on-exec is
7919    /// cleared, by number and state, and the table scan reports exactly it.
7920    #[test]
7921    #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
7922    fn the_inherited_descriptor_scan_finds_a_producer_without_close_on_exec() {
7923        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
7924        let (read, write) = nix::unistd::pipe2(nix::fcntl::OFlag::O_CLOEXEC).unwrap();
7925        drop(write);
7926        let fd = read.as_raw_fd();
7927        // SAFETY: plain fcntl calls on a descriptor this test owns; no SIGIO
7928        // can be sent for a pipe with no writer.
7929        unsafe {
7930            assert_eq!(libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_SETOWN, libc::getpid()), 0);
7931            let flags = libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_GETFL);
7932            assert_eq!(libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_SETFL, flags | libc::O_ASYNC), 0);
7933        }
7934        assert_eq!(check_inherited_descriptor(fd, -1), None);
7935        // SAFETY: as above.
7936        unsafe { assert_eq!(libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_SETFD, 0), 0) };
7937        let expected = LaunchReport {
7938            kind: audit_bits::PRODUCER,
7939            bits: audit_bits::O_ASYNC | audit_bits::OWNER,
7940            errno: 0,
7941            fd,
7942            rlimit: (0, 0),
7943        };
7944        assert_eq!(check_inherited_descriptor(fd, -1), Some(expected));
7945        assert_eq!(
7946            check_inherited_descriptor(fd, fd),
7947            None,
7948            "the audit's own pipe"
7949        );
7950        // No other descriptor of this test process is a producer, so the
7951        // table scan reports exactly this one.
7952        assert_eq!(audit_inherited_descriptors(-1), Some(expected));
7953        // SAFETY: as above.
7954        unsafe { assert_eq!(libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_SETFD, libc::FD_CLOEXEC), 0) };
7955    }
7956
7957    /// D25: an inherited descriptor that is already a producer (O_ASYNC with
7958    /// an owner, a socket with an owner, a lease) refuses the run, naming the
7959    /// descriptor, and so does one with only an owner (a directory
7960    /// notification, which cannot be read back, would signal it); one with
7961    /// only O_ASYNC, or an unowned socket, does not.
7962    #[test]
7963    #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
7964    fn an_inherited_signal_producer_is_refused_by_descriptor() {
7965        use detcore::host_timed_producers::ProducerState;
7966        let state = |o_async, owner, socket| ProducerState {
7967            o_async,
7968            owner,
7969            socket,
7970        };
7971        for (producer, lease, what) in [
7972            (state(true, true, false), false, "O_ASYNC and an owner"),
7973            (state(false, true, true), false, "a socket with an owner"),
7974            (state(false, false, false), true, "holds a lease"),
7975            (
7976                state(false, true, false),
7977                false,
7978                "it has an owner, which a directory",
7979            ),
7980        ] {
7981            let reason = inherited_producer_refusal(7, producer, lease).unwrap();
7982            assert!(
7983                reason.starts_with("the guest would inherit descriptor 7, "),
7984                "{reason}"
7985            );
7986            assert!(reason.contains(what), "{reason}");
7987        }
7988        for state in [
7989            state(true, false, false),
7990            state(false, false, true),
7991            state(true, false, true),
7992        ] {
7993            assert_eq!(
7994                inherited_producer_refusal(7, state, false),
7995                None,
7996                "{state:?}"
7997            );
7998        }
7999    }

8001    /// Hermit's default in-guest route reserves SIGSYS always, SIGSEGV while
8002    /// Detcore's subscription traps an instruction, and SIGTRAP only while the
8003    /// guard router can be installed: with site patching on
8004    /// (`in_guest_site_patching_off` false), never with it off, on either
8005    /// in-guest backend (A5 step 3c slice 0c). Every other backend gets an
8006    /// empty set and no router whatever the setting, and so does the in-guest
8007    /// loader route, whose configuration is `prepare_backend_config`'s with no
8008    /// reserved set (A5 step 3c, design section 16.30).
8009    #[test]
8010    fn in_guest_reserved_signals_follow_the_backend_the_subscription_and_site_patching() {
8011        let bit = |signal: libc::c_int| 1_u64 << (signal - 1);
8012        for backend in Backend::ALL {
8013            for patching_off in [false, true] {
8014                let mut config = prepare_backend_config(DetConfig::default(), backend);
8015                assert_eq!(config.in_guest_reserved_signals, 0, "{backend:?}");
8016                config.in_guest_site_patching_off = patching_off;
8017                let router = in_guest_guard_router_installed(&config, backend);
8018                let reserved = in_guest_reserved_signals(&config, backend);
8019                let label = format!("{backend:?} patching_off={patching_off}");
8020                if !backend.is_in_guest_liteinst() {
8021                    assert!(!router, "{label}");
8022                    assert_eq!(reserved, 0, "{label}");
8023                    continue;
8024                }
8025                assert_eq!(router, !patching_off, "{label}");
8026                let trap = if patching_off { 0 } else { bit(libc::SIGTRAP) };
8027                // Without --passthru-opt Detcore always subscribes RDTSC.
8028                assert!(<Detcore as reverie::Tool>::subscriptions(&config).has_rdtsc());
8029                assert_eq!(
8030                    reserved,
8031                    bit(libc::SIGSYS) | bit(libc::SIGSEGV) | trap,
8032                    "{label}"
8033                );
8034
8035                // --passthru-opt with time and CPUID virtualization off traps
8036                // no instruction, so the runtime installs no SIGSEGV handler.
8037                let mut unsubscribed = config.clone();
8038                unsubscribed.passthru_opt = true;
8039                unsubscribed.virtualize_time = false;
8040                unsubscribed.virtualize_cpuid = false;
8041                let subscription = <Detcore as reverie::Tool>::subscriptions(&unsubscribed);
8042                assert!(!subscription.has_rdtsc() && !subscription.has_cpuid());
8043                assert_eq!(
8044                    in_guest_reserved_signals(&unsubscribed, backend),
8045                    bit(libc::SIGSYS) | trap,
8046                    "{label}"
8047                );
8048                for (time, cpuid) in [(true, false), (false, true)] {
8049                    let mut subscribed = unsubscribed.clone();
8050                    subscribed.virtualize_time = time;
8051                    subscribed.virtualize_cpuid = cpuid;
8052                    assert_eq!(
8053                        in_guest_reserved_signals(&subscribed, backend),
8054                        bit(libc::SIGSYS) | bit(libc::SIGSEGV) | trap,
8055                        "{label} time={time} cpuid={cpuid}"
8056                    );
8057                }
8058            }
8059        }
8060    }

8062    /// The default in-guest route sets every Tool image's site-patching check
8063    /// from the backend and only then the reserved set, so SIGTRAP is
8064    /// reserved on `liteinst` (patching on, router installed) and not on
8065    /// `in-guest-trap` (patching off, no router): a SIGTRAP another process
8066    /// sends to an in-guest-trap guest is delivered as on Linux, while SIGSYS
8067    /// and SIGSEGV stay reserved on both (A5 step 3c slice 0c).
8068    #[test]
8069    #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
8070    fn the_default_route_reserves_sigtrap_only_with_site_patching_on() {
8071        let bit = |signal: libc::c_int| 1_u64 << (signal - 1);
8072        for backend in Backend::ALL {
8073            let mut config = prepare_backend_config(DetConfig::default(), backend);
8074            config.in_guest_site_patching_off = in_guest_site_patching_off(backend);
8075            let reserved = in_guest_reserved_signals(&config, backend);
8076            let expected = match backend {
8077                Backend::Liteinst => bit(libc::SIGSYS) | bit(libc::SIGSEGV) | bit(libc::SIGTRAP),
8078                Backend::InGuestTrap => bit(libc::SIGSYS) | bit(libc::SIGSEGV),
8079                _ => 0,
8080            };
8081            assert_eq!(reserved, expected, "{backend:?}");
8082            assert_eq!(
8083                in_guest_guard_router_installed(&config, backend),
8084                backend == Backend::Liteinst,
8085                "{backend:?}"
8086            );
8087        }
8088    }

8139    #[test]
8140    #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
8141    fn in_guest_liteinst_checks_scripts_through_their_interpreter() {
8142        use interp::startup_fixtures::*;
8143
8144        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
8145        let dynamic = write_guest_program(
8146            directory.path(),
8147            "dynamic",
8148            &dynamic_executable(false),
8149            0o755,
8150        );
8151        let static_elf = write_guest_program(
8152            directory.path(),
8153            "static",
8154            &elf(EM_X86_64, &[(PT_LOAD, b"code")]),
8155            0o755,
8156        );
8157
8158        let script = write_guest_program(
8159            directory.path(),
8160            "to-static",
8161            &shebang_to(&static_elf),
8162            0o755,
8163        );
8164        let gap = in_guest_liteinst_program_gap(&mut Command::new(&script))
8165            .unwrap()
8166            .expect("a script run by a static interpreter was not refused");
8167        assert!(
8168            gap.contains(&static_elf.display().to_string()) && gap.contains("statically linked"),
8169            "{gap}"
8170        );
8171
8172        // A relative interpreter resolves against the guest's working directory.
8173        let relative = write_guest_program(directory.path(), "relative", b"#!static\n", 0o755);
8174        let gap =
8175            in_guest_liteinst_program_gap(Command::new(&relative).current_dir(directory.path()))
8176                .unwrap()
8177                .expect("a relative static interpreter was not refused");
8178        assert!(gap.contains("statically linked"), "{gap}");
8179
8180        // The kernel keeps a carriage return in the interpreter path, so a
8181        // script with CRLF line endings runs `interp\r`, not `interp`.
8182        write_guest_program(
8183            directory.path(),
8184            "interp",
8185            &dynamic_executable(false),
8186            0o755,
8187        );
8188        let interp_cr = write_guest_program(
8189            directory.path(),
8190            "interp\r",
8191            &elf(EM_X86_64, &[(PT_LOAD, b"code")]),
8192            0o755,
8193        );
8194        let mut crlf = b"#!".to_vec();
8195        crlf.extend_from_slice(directory.path().join("interp").as_os_str().as_bytes());
8196        crlf.extend_from_slice(b"\r\necho script\r\n");
8197        let crlf = write_guest_program(directory.path(), "crlf", &crlf, 0o755);
8198        let gap = in_guest_liteinst_program_gap(&mut Command::new(&crlf))
8199            .unwrap()
8200            .expect("a CRLF script run by a static interp\\r was not refused");
8201        assert!(
8202            gap.contains(&interp_cr.display().to_string()) && gap.contains("statically linked"),
8203            "{gap}"
8204        );
8205
8206        // A #! line the kernel's script handler declines runs no interpreter:
8207        // the kernel fails the execve or tries another handler, so it is
8208        // refused.
8209        let mut truncated = b"#!/".to_vec();
8210        truncated.resize(256, b'a');
8211        for (name, bytes) in [
8212            ("empty", b"#! \t\nbody\n".to_vec()),
8213            ("truncated", truncated),
8214        ] {
8215            let program = write_guest_program(directory.path(), name, &bytes, 0o755);
8216            let gap = in_guest_liteinst_program_gap(&mut Command::new(&program))
8217                .unwrap()
8218                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{name} was not refused"));
8219            assert!(
8220                gap.contains("the kernel's script handler declines it"),
8221                "{name}: {gap}"
8222            );
8223        }
8224
8225        // Four nested scripts are followed to the ELF image; a fifth is refused.
8226        let mut target = dynamic;
8227        for level in 1..=5 {
8228            target = write_guest_program(
8229                directory.path(),
8230                &format!("level-{level}"),
8231                &shebang_to(&target),
8232                0o755,
8233            );
8234            let gap = in_guest_liteinst_program_gap(&mut Command::new(&target)).unwrap();
8235            if level <= MAX_INTERPRETER_DEPTH {
8236                assert_eq!(gap, None, "level {level}");
8237            } else {
8238                let gap = gap.expect("five nested scripts were not refused");
8239                assert!(gap.contains("nest more than 4 deep"), "{gap}");
8240            }
8241        }
8242    }

8244    #[test]
8245    #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
8246    fn in_guest_liteinst_refuses_a_fifo_without_blocking() {
8247        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
8248        let fifo = directory.path().join("fifo");
8249        let fifo_c = std::ffi::CString::new(fifo.as_os_str().as_bytes()).unwrap();
8250        assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::mkfifo(fifo_c.as_ptr(), 0o700) }, 0);
8251        let script = write_guest_program(directory.path(), "to-fifo", &shebang_to(&fifo), 0o755);
8252        // A socket cannot be opened at all (ENXIO), and opening a device can
8253        // act on it; both must be refused, not reported as unreadable.
8254        let socket = directory.path().join("socket");
8255        let _listener = std::os::unix::net::UnixListener::bind(&socket).unwrap();
8256        let to_socket =
8257            write_guest_program(directory.path(), "to-socket", &shebang_to(&socket), 0o755);
8258        let device = PathBuf::from("/dev/null");
8259        let to_device =
8260            write_guest_program(directory.path(), "to-device", &shebang_to(&device), 0o755);
8261        // `./fifo` reaches the check through find_program's working-directory
8262        // branch, which does not require a regular file; the scripts reach the
8263        // FIFO, the socket and the device as their interpreters. Nothing opens
8264        // the FIFO for writing, so a blocking open or read would never return:
8265        // each check runs on its own thread and must answer within 10 s.
8266        let cases = [
8267            (
8268                "program",
8269                PathBuf::from("./fifo"),
8270                Some(directory.path().to_owned()),
8271                fs::canonicalize(&fifo).unwrap(),
8272            ),
8273            ("interpreter", script, None, fifo.clone()),
8274            ("socket interpreter", to_socket, None, socket.clone()),
8275            ("device interpreter", to_device, None, device),
8276        ];
8277        for (name, program, current_dir, shown) in cases {
8278            let (sender, receiver) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
8279            std::thread::spawn(move || {
8280                let mut command = Command::new(&program);
8281                if let Some(directory) = current_dir {
8282                    command.current_dir(directory);
8283                }
8284                let gap = in_guest_liteinst_program_gap(&mut command)
8285                    .map_err(|error| format!("{error:#}"));
8286                let _ = sender.send(gap);
8287            });
8288            let gap = receiver
8289                .recv_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10))
8290                .unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("{name}: the check blocked on the FIFO"))
8291                .unwrap()
8292                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{name}: the FIFO was not refused"));
8293            assert!(
8294                gap.contains(&format!("{} is not a regular file", shown.display())),
8295                "{name}: {gap}"
8296            );
8297        }
8298    }

8300    #[test]
8301    #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
8302    fn in_guest_liteinst_pins_the_program_the_launch_resolves() {
8303        use interp::startup_fixtures::*;
8304
8305        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
8306        // A name that no host PATH directory holds.
8307        let name = "hermit-3520-static";
8308        let static_elf = write_guest_program(
8309            directory.path(),
8310            name,
8311            &elf(EM_X86_64, &[(PT_LOAD, b"code")]),
8312            0o755,
8313        );
8314        let search = format!("/nonexistent-directory:{}", directory.path().display());
8315        // The launch resolves the program with `find_program` on the command it
8316        // is given. Builds the command twice: once for the launch's own
8317        // resolution, once for the check, which must agree with it.
8318        let check = |build: &dyn Fn() -> Command| {
8319            let launch = build().find_program();
8320            let mut command = build();
8321            let arg0 = command.get_arg0().to_owned();
8322            let gap = in_guest_liteinst_program_gap(&mut command);
8323            match launch {
8324                Ok(program) => {
8325                    let gap = gap.unwrap().expect("the static image was not refused");
8326                    assert!(gap.contains("is statically linked"), "{gap}");
8327                    assert_eq!(Path::new(command.get_program()), program);
8328                    assert_eq!(command.get_arg0(), arg0);
8329                    // Pinned: the launch's own resolution returns it unchanged.
8330                    assert_eq!(command.find_program().unwrap(), program);
8331                    assert_eq!(
8332                        fs::canonicalize(&program).unwrap(),
8333                        fs::canonicalize(&static_elf).unwrap()
8334                    );
8335                    true
8336                }
8337                Err(_) => {
8338                    let error = gap.expect_err("the check found what the launch cannot");
8339                    assert!(
8340                        format!("{error:#}").contains("cannot find guest program"),
8341                        "{error:#}"
8342                    );
8343                    false
8344                }
8345            }
8346        };
8347
8348        // A path with a slash resolves against the guest's working directory.
8349        assert!(check(&|| {
8350            let mut command = Command::new(format!("./{name}"));
8351            command.current_dir(directory.path());
8352            command
8353        }));
8354        // A bare name is searched for in the command's PATH once the base
8355        // environment is cleared, skipping entries without such a file.
8356        assert!(check(&|| {
8357            let mut command = Command::new(name);
8358            command.env_clear().env("PATH", &search);
8359            command
8360        }));
8361        // Without a cleared environment the launch searches Hermit's own PATH,
8362        // not the command's, so the static image is not found by either.
8363        assert!(!check(&|| {
8364            let mut command = Command::new(name);
8365            command.env("PATH", &search);
8366            command
8367        }));
8368        // A cleared environment without PATH (`--base-env=empty`) searches
8369        // Hermit's working directory, not the guest's and not /bin:/usr/bin.
8370        assert!(!check(&|| {
8371            let mut command = Command::new(name);
8372            command.env_clear().current_dir(directory.path());
8373            command
8374        }));
8375        // Not executable, or missing: the launch cannot run it, and neither
8376        // resolution finds it.
8377        fs::set_permissions(&static_elf, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o644)).unwrap();
8378        assert!(!check(&|| {
8379            let mut command = Command::new(name);
8380            command.env_clear().env("PATH", &search);
8381            command
8382        }));
8383        assert!(!check(&|| Command::new(&static_elf)));
8384        assert!(!check(&|| Command::new("hermit-no-such-program-3520")));
8385    }

8431    /// ⚠️ THE REGRESSION agent(hermit-007)'s CODEX LANE CAUGHT, PINNED FOR THE
8432    /// SIGNAL BAND. This test fails if the signal half stops being covered; it
8433    /// does NOT prove the predicate can never drift again, because the
8434    /// `122..=127` half is still a hard-coded literal that a future reserved
8435    /// value would fall outside exactly as 130 did.
8436    /// `liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown` hard-coded
8437    /// `Exited(122..=127)`. When the reserved set grew to include the signal
8438    /// band, `Exited(130)` fell outside it and is not `Signaled(_, _)` -- it is a
8439    /// status hermit CHOSE -- so LiteInst skipped the forced shutdown and
8440    /// `clean_up` could wait forever on `handle.await`. A reachable hang,
8441    /// introduced by widening the reserved set in one place and not the other.
8442    ///
8443    /// The 130 and 143 rows are the ones with teeth: revert the predicate to the
8444    /// bare range and they fail.
8445    #[test]
8446    #[cfg(feature = "liteinst")]
8447    fn liteinst_forced_shutdown_covers_every_status_hermit_reserves() {
8448        // The signal band. Not `Signaled`: hermit CHOSE these codes, because a
8449        // namespace init cannot produce a genuine signalled wait status.
8450        assert!(
8451            liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Exited(130)),
8452            "128+SIGINT"
8453        );
8454        assert!(
8455            liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Exited(143)),
8456            "128+SIGTERM"
8457        );
8458        assert!(
8459            liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Exited(129)),
8460            "128+SIGHUP"
8461        );
8462
8463        // The pre-existing reserved band, unchanged.
8464        assert!(liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Exited(122)));
8465        assert!(liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Exited(125)));
8466        assert!(liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Exited(127)));
8467
8468        // A real signal death still forces shutdown.
8469        assert!(liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Signaled(
8470            nix::sys::signal::Signal::SIGKILL,
8471            false
8472        )));
8473
8474        // ⚠️ CONTROLS, so a predicate that simply returned `true` would fail
8475        // this test rather than pass it. An ordinary guest exit must NOT force a
8476        // shutdown; 128 is excluded because there is no signal 0, and 200 is
8477        // above SIGRTMAX so it is a guest's own number.
8478        assert!(!liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Exited(0)));
8479        assert!(!liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Exited(1)));
8480        assert!(!liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Exited(121)));
8481        assert!(!liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Exited(128)));
8482        assert!(!liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Exited(200)));
8483        // ⚠️ THE BAND EDGES, WHICH THIS TEST STOPPED SHORT OF. It went up to 143
8484        // and then jumped to 200, so `MAX_SIGNO` could shrink from 64 to 15 with
8485        // every row still green -- proved vacuous by agent(hermit-005)'s codex
8486        // lane. 192 is `128 + SIGRTMAX`, the last status in the band; 193 is the
8487        // first outside it. Testing a range in the middle pins nothing at either end.
8488        assert!(
8489            liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Exited(192)),
8490            "128 + SIGRTMAX is still a signal death and must force shutdown"
8491        );
8492        assert!(
8493            !liteinst_requires_forced_shutdown(ExitStatus::Exited(193)),
8494            "above SIGRTMAX the status is the guest's own and must NOT force shutdown"
8495        );
8496    }

8498    /// ⚠️ The bare `NotFound` here was read as a git-worktree bug and cost real
8499    /// investigation time. The message must name the mount namespace, because
8500    /// the directory it is complaining about usually exists on the host.
8501    #[test]
8502    fn a_cwd_under_tmp_is_explained_by_the_container_tmpfs_not_by_a_missing_directory() {
8503        let error = std::io::Error::from(std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound);
8504        let rendered = format!(
8505            "{}",
8506            super::kvm_cwd_resolution_error(std::path::Path::new("/tmp/agent-checkout"), &error)
8507        );
8508        assert!(
8509            rendered.contains("private, empty tmpfs"),
8510            "must name the mechanism: {rendered}"
8511        );
8512        assert!(
8513            rendered.contains("--workdir"),
8514            "must name a way out: {rendered}"
8515        );
8516        assert!(
8517            rendered.contains("/tmp/agent-checkout"),
8518            "must still name the path asked for: {rendered}"
8519        );
8520    }

8522    /// The explanation must NOT be attached to failures it does not explain --
8523    /// an error that volunteers the wrong cause is what produced the original
8524    /// misdiagnosis, in the other direction.
8525    #[test]
8526    fn the_tmpfs_explanation_is_withheld_where_it_does_not_apply() {
8527        let not_found = std::io::Error::from(std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound);
8528        // ⚠️ A CONSTANT ABSOLUTE PATH, NOT ONE READ FROM THE ENVIRONMENT. The only
8529        // property this arm needs is "outside /tmp", and a literal that is outside
8530        // /tmp by construction supplies it without asking the runner anything.
8531        //
8532        // The earlier form wrote a developer-specific home path, which made
8533        // `scripts/check-portable-paths.sh` red on main -- correctly: that gate
8534        // rejects such a path anywhere in a tracked build or run file, tests and
8535        // COMMENTS included, so spelling one out even to explain this would trip
8536        // it. Replacing it by reading $HOME then made the test depend on the
8537        // runner instead: measured by `agent(codex-rev-2641)`, HOME unset, empty,
8538        // relative and /tmp-rooted gave three different fixtures and one failure.
8539        // A unit test that consults the environment is answering a question about
8540        // the environment.
8541        //
8542        // ⚠️ AND NO GUARD IS NEEDED HERE, WHICH IS THE POINT OF USING A CONSTANT.
8543        // The $HOME form carried `assert!(!outside_path.starts_with("/tmp"))` to
8544        // stop a /tmp-rooted HOME making this vacuous. That assertion could never
8545        // fire: the `!outside.contains("tmpfs")` check below sits ABOVE it in
8546        // source order and panics first in exactly that case. It was decorative,
8547        // and an assertion over a compile-time constant would be too, so there is
8548        // none. The fixture cannot drift into /tmp because nothing computes it.
8549        let outside_path = std::path::Path::new("/nonexistent-home/wt");
8550        let outside = format!(
8551            "{}",
8552            super::kvm_cwd_resolution_error(outside_path, &not_found)
8553        );
8554        assert!(!outside.contains("tmpfs"), "not a /tmp path: {outside}");
8555
8556        // `/tmp` itself resolves in the guest -- the mount POINT exists -- so a
8557        // failure there is something else and must not be mislabelled.
8558        let tmp_itself = format!(
8559            "{}",
8560            super::kvm_cwd_resolution_error(std::path::Path::new("/tmp"), &not_found)
8561        );
8562        assert!(!tmp_itself.contains("tmpfs"), "/tmp itself: {tmp_itself}");
8563
8564        // A different errno under /tmp is a different fault (permissions, say).
8565        let denied = std::io::Error::from(std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied);
8566        let other = format!(
8567            "{}",
8568            super::kvm_cwd_resolution_error(std::path::Path::new("/tmp/x"), &denied)
8569        );
8570        assert!(!other.contains("tmpfs"), "not NotFound: {other}");
8571    }

8573    /// A build-flag message must not assert a machine condition it never tested.
8574    ///
8575    /// ⚠️ THIS IS THE FOURTH DIAGNOSTIC TONIGHT THAT NAMED AN UNESTABLISHED CAUSE,
8576    /// after the sigpipe checker, the manifest gate and the LiteInst pidfd error.
8577    /// "DBT support was not included in this build" reads as "this machine cannot
8578    /// run DBT", and cost four or five unnecessary abstentions across the fleet --
8579    /// agents declined to make DBT claims on a box where DynamoRIO is installed
8580    /// and `--features dbt` builds and runs. The absence is a build flag, and the
8581    /// message must say which flag and admit what it did not check.
8582    #[test]
8583    fn an_unbuilt_backend_names_the_flag_and_claims_nothing_about_the_machine() {
8584        let feature_disabled_backends: &[(Backend, &str)] = &[
8585            #[cfg(not(feature = "dbt"))]
8586            (Backend::Dbt, "dbt"),
8587            #[cfg(not(feature = "sabre"))]
8588            (Backend::Sabre, "sabre"),
8589            #[cfg(not(feature = "e9patch"))]
8590            (Backend::E9patch, "e9patch"),
8591            #[cfg(not(feature = "liteinst"))]
8592            (Backend::Liteinst, "liteinst"),
8593            // in-guest-trap is the same runtime behind the same feature.
8594            #[cfg(not(feature = "liteinst"))]
8595            (Backend::InGuestTrap, "liteinst"),
8596        ];
8597
8598        for &(backend, feature) in feature_disabled_backends {
8599            let reason = backend
8600                .unavailable_reason()
8601                .expect("a feature-disabled backend must report why it is unavailable");
8602            assert!(
8603                reason.contains(feature),
8604                "{backend:?}: a build-flag message must name the flag to rebuild with, got: {reason}"
8605            );
8606            assert!(
8607                reason.contains("has not been checked"),
8608                "{backend:?}: a build-flag message must not imply the machine was tested, got: {reason}"
8609            );
8610        }
8611    }

8827    /// Regression test for the `hermit run --verify` empty-stdin bug: a pipe
8828    /// (non-seekable) fed to hermit must be buffered and replayed *identically*
8829    /// to every run of `--verify`. Before the fix the output-capturing backend
8830    /// used `Stdio::null()`, so piped input was silently dropped and both runs
8831    /// saw empty input (a false "deterministic" pass, e.g. `gcc -x c -`
8832    /// compiling nothing). This asserts the reserved snapshot replays the exact
8833    /// bytes twice.
8834    #[test]
8835    fn output_stdin_snapshot_replays_pipe_to_repeated_runs() {
8836        use std::io::Read;
8837        use std::io::Write;
8838        use std::os::fd::FromRawFd;
8839
8840        // A pipe is non-seekable, exercising the buffer-into-tempfile path that
8841        // matches the real `echo prog | hermit run --verify` scenario.
8842        let mut fds = [0i32; 2];
8843        assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::pipe(fds.as_mut_ptr()) }, 0);
8844        // SAFETY: pipe(2) just returned two fresh owned descriptors.
8845        let read_end = unsafe { fs::File::from_raw_fd(fds[0]) };
8846        let mut write_end = unsafe { fs::File::from_raw_fd(fds[1]) };
8847
8848        let payload = b"int main(){return 0;}\n";
8849        write_end.write_all(payload).unwrap();
8850        // Close the write end so draining the pipe hits EOF.
8851        drop(write_end);
8852
8853        reserve_output_stdin_snapshot(Some(read_end)).unwrap();
8854
8855        // Two successive runs (as `--verify` performs) must each read the full
8856        // payload from the start.
8857        for run in 0..2 {
8858            let mut file = output_backend_stdin_file()
8859                .unwrap()
8860                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("run {run}: expected a replayable stdin snapshot"));
8861            let mut got = Vec::new();
8862            file.read_to_end(&mut got).unwrap();
8863            assert_eq!(got, payload, "run {run} stdin replay mismatch");
8864        }
8865
8866        let mut file = output_backend_stdin_file().unwrap().unwrap();
8867        let error = file
8868            .write_all(b"guest-must-not-change-the-snapshot")
8869            .expect_err("the replayed stdin must be read-only");
8870        assert_eq!(error.raw_os_error(), Some(libc::EBADF));
8871    }

8885    /// A SaBRe guest that never reaches the coordinator ran with no Detcore in
8886    /// the loop at all. The diagnosis must say so in those terms -- a
8887    /// zero-syscall SaBRe run is not a weak result, it is *no* result -- and it
8888    /// must name the statically linked ELF case, which is the shape that
8889    /// reaches this path in practice because a static client has no dynamic
8890    /// loader through which SaBRe could regain control.
8891    #[test]
8892    #[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
8893    fn uninstrumented_sabre_guest_is_reported_as_no_determinization() {
8894        let message = sabre_uninstrumented_guest_message(&ExitStatus::Exited(0));
8895        assert!(
8896            message.contains("no determinization at all"),
8897            "must not present an uninstrumented run as a weaker guarantee: {message}"
8898        );
8899        assert!(
8900            message.contains("Detcore coordinator"),
8901            "must name the authority that was never reached: {message}"
8902        );
8903        assert!(
8904            message.contains("statically linked ELF"),
8905            "must name the dominant cause so the reader can act: {message}"
8906        );
8907        // The exit status is carried because a successful-looking status is
8908        // exactly what makes this failure mode dangerous.
8909        assert!(
8910            message.contains("Exited(0)"),
8911            "must carry the observed status: {message}"
8912        );
8913        assert!(
8914            sabre_uninstrumented_guest_message(&ExitStatus::Exited(139)).contains("Exited(139)"),
8915            "must carry a failing status too"
8916        );
8917    }

8919    /// The old two-way banner treated both `guest_rpc_observed=false` and an
8920    /// engaged zero-fallback run as `sabre-exercised`. Assert the three states
8921    /// together so no pair can collapse back onto one value.
8922    #[test]
8923    #[cfg(feature = "sabre")]
8924    fn sabre_reach_states_are_pairwise_distinct() {
8925        let no_detcore = sabre_reach_state(false, 0);
8926        let degraded = sabre_reach_state(true, 1);
8927        let exercised = sabre_reach_state(true, 0);
8928
8929        assert_eq!(no_detcore, "no-detcore-reached");
8930        assert_eq!(degraded, "degraded-ptrace-fallback");
8931        assert_eq!(exercised, "sabre-exercised");
8932        assert_ne!(no_detcore, degraded);
8933        assert_ne!(no_detcore, exercised);
8934        assert_ne!(degraded, exercised);
8935        assert_eq!(
8936            sabre_reach_state(false, 9),
8937            "no-detcore-reached",
8938            "absence of a guest RPC must dominate any fallback count"
8939        );
8940    }

9010    #[test]
9011    fn sabre_backend_configures_process_local_capabilities() {
9012        let config = super::DetConfig::default();
9013        let sabre = prepare_backend_config(config.clone(), Backend::Sabre).backend;
9014        assert!(sabre.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table);
9015        assert!(sabre.rediscovers_descriptors_after_exec);
9016        assert!(sabre.internal_pipe_turns_are_host_timed);
9017        assert!(sabre.loopback_pollers_yield_to_peers);
9018        assert!(sabre.guest_clock_reads_bypass_backend);
9019        assert!(sabre.virtualizes_syscall_clobbers);
9020        assert!(sabre.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation);
9021        assert!(sabre.reports_physical_process_exits);
9022        assert!(sabre.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls);
9023        assert!(sabre.tracks_process_children);
9024        assert!(!sabre.runs_exit_robust_list);
9025        assert!(!sabre.requires_thread_directed_process_signals);
9026        assert!(!sabre.defers_vfork_child_registration);
9027        let ptrace = prepare_backend_config(config, Backend::Ptrace).backend;
9028        assert!(!ptrace.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table);
9029        assert!(!ptrace.rediscovers_descriptors_after_exec);
9030        assert!(!ptrace.internal_pipe_turns_are_host_timed);
9031        assert!(!ptrace.loopback_pollers_yield_to_peers);
9032        assert!(!ptrace.guest_clock_reads_bypass_backend);
9033        assert!(!ptrace.virtualizes_syscall_clobbers);
9034        assert!(!ptrace.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation);
9035        assert!(!ptrace.reports_physical_process_exits);
9036        assert!(!ptrace.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls);

9039        assert!(!ptrace.requires_thread_directed_process_signals);
9040        assert!(!ptrace.defers_vfork_child_registration);
9041    }

9073    #[test]
9074    fn kvm_backend_config_marks_concurrent_process_children() {
9075        let defaults = super::DetConfig::default();
9076        assert!(!defaults.sequentialize_threads);
9077        let nonsequential = prepare_backend_config(defaults, Backend::Kvm);
9078        assert!(nonsequential.backend.provides_process_signal_control);
9079        assert!(nonsequential.backend.emulates_child_waits);
9080        assert!(!may_observe_signal_dequeues(&nonsequential));
9081        assert!(!requires_signal_control(&nonsequential));
9082
9083        let config = super::DetConfig {
9084            sequentialize_threads: true,
9085            ..super::DetConfig::default()
9086        };
9087        let kvm = prepare_backend_config(config, Backend::Kvm);
9088        assert!(may_observe_signal_dequeues(&kvm));
9089        assert!(requires_signal_control(&kvm));
9090        assert!(kvm.backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation);
9091        assert!(kvm.backend.tracks_process_children);
9092        assert!(!kvm.backend.runs_exit_robust_list);
9093        assert!(!kvm.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals);
9094        assert!(kvm.backend.defers_vfork_child_registration);
9095
9096        // A controlled run needs both the backend's process-signal control and
9097        // sequentialized threads; neither alone admits one.
9098        for backend in [
9099            Backend::Ptrace,
9100            Backend::Dbt,
9101            Backend::Sabre,
9102            Backend::Liteinst,
9103            Backend::InGuestTrap,
9104            Backend::E9patch,
9105        ] {
9106            let config = super::DetConfig {
9107                sequentialize_threads: true,
9108                ..super::DetConfig::default()
9109            };
9110            let prepared = prepare_backend_config(config, backend);
9111            assert!(!may_observe_signal_dequeues(&prepared), "{backend:?}");
9112            assert!(!requires_signal_control(&prepared), "{backend:?}");
9113        }
9114    }

9116    /// Whether Detcore asks the backend to install process signal control for
9117    /// `config`: the bound Reverie checks before it offers the control.
9118    fn may_observe_signal_dequeues(config: &DetConfig) -> bool {
9119        <super::Detcore as reverie::Tool>::may_observe_signal_dequeues(config)
9120    }
9121
9122    /// Whether Reverie must refuse `config` on a runner that offers no
9123    /// process signal control, as Detcore's installation did before.
9124    fn requires_signal_control(config: &DetConfig) -> bool {
9125        <super::Detcore as reverie::Tool>::requires_signal_control(config)
9126    }
9127
9128    /// The values the hand-written assignments in `prepare_backend_config` and
9129    /// `run_kvm` gave each backend before Detcore read
9130    /// [`reverie::BackendCapabilities`], transcribed field by field. A backend
9131    /// identity check became the capability it selected:
9132    /// `discover_live_file_metadata` split into the first four fields, the old
9133    /// `backend_reports_physical_process_exits` became two, and
9134    /// `backend_is_kvm` became five, of which the last two remain here:
9135    /// `refuses_nonleader_exec_with_enosys` became the backend's typed exec
9136    /// refusal (Reverie d78f770f), `failed_gettimeofday_may_store_host_time`
9137    /// the guest's storable-memory report (Reverie 8bfb450e) and
9138    /// `user_address_limit` the guest's user address limit query (Reverie
9139    /// 6f75cc4c). Four fields are newer than that transcription:
9140    /// `process_exits_complete_asynchronously` (Reverie 056c8cac), true only
9141    /// for in-guest LiteInst, whose process exits complete some time after the
9142    /// tool grants them, `supports_madv_dontneed` (Reverie 8d8697aa), true for
9143    /// every backend, and `reports_child_exit_publication` (Reverie 9cb6f7b7),
9144    /// true for ptrace and e9patch, whose tracer reports when the kernel
9145    /// publishes a process's exit to its parent, and
9146    /// `virtualizes_guest_sigalrm` (Reverie 7142ff8c), true only for in-guest
9147    /// LiteInst, whose runtime keeps a guest SIGALRM handler virtual (signal
9148    /// phase 1). `in-guest-trap` is in-guest LiteInst with site patching off,
9149    /// which changes how a syscall reaches the Tool and nothing the Tool host
9150    /// can do, so it has exactly in-guest LiteInst's row.
9151    /// DBT now also shares the guest descriptor table and rediscovers it after
9152    /// exec (Reverie 15374907); its host-timed-turn and poller-yield
9153    /// capabilities remain false. `reports_sigreturns` (A5 step 2) is true
9154    /// for ptrace, and so for e9patch preprocessing, whose guest Hermit runs
9155    /// on ptrace. `reports_kernel_child_exit_signals` is true for ptrace,
9156    /// e9patch and SaBRe, whose signal callbacks see the kernel's child-exit
9157    /// SIGCHLD with its siginfo and can suppress or rewrite it.
9158    /// `virtualizes_syscall_clobbers` is true for KVM too since Reverie's
9159    /// per-call slice 6: its Tool register snapshot at a syscall has RCX ==
9160    /// RIP and R11 == RFLAGS, and it offers no register write, so Detcore's
9161    /// canonicalization could change nothing there.
9162    fn golden_backend_capabilities(backend: Backend) -> serde_json::Value {
9163        let sabre = backend == Backend::Sabre;
9164        let kvm = backend == Backend::Kvm;
9165        let dbt = backend == Backend::Dbt;
9166        // LiteInst runs only through its in-guest runtime.
9167        let in_guest_liteinst = matches!(backend, Backend::Liteinst | Backend::InGuestTrap);
9168        serde_json::json!({
9169            "tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table": sabre || dbt,
9170            "rediscovers_descriptors_after_exec": sabre || dbt,
9171            "internal_pipe_turns_are_host_timed": sabre,
9172            "loopback_pollers_yield_to_peers": sabre,
9173            "guest_clock_reads_bypass_backend": sabre,
9174            "virtualizes_syscall_clobbers": sabre || kvm,
9175            "needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation": in_guest_liteinst || sabre || dbt || kvm,
9176            "reports_physical_process_exits": sabre,
9177            "process_exits_complete_asynchronously": in_guest_liteinst,
9178            "virtualizes_guest_sigalrm": in_guest_liteinst,
9179            "signal_interrupts_external_syscalls": sabre,
9180            "tracks_process_children": !dbt,
9181            "runs_exit_robust_list": matches!(backend, Backend::Ptrace | Backend::E9patch),
9182            "requires_thread_directed_process_signals": dbt,
9183            "supports_parked_write_signal_interruption":
9184                matches!(backend, Backend::Ptrace | Backend::E9patch | Backend::Kvm),
9185            "defers_vfork_child_registration": kvm,
9186            "supports_madvise": !kvm,
9187            "supports_madv_dontneed": true,
9188            "reports_child_exit_publication":
9189                matches!(backend, Backend::Ptrace | Backend::E9patch),
9190            "reports_kernel_child_exit_signals":
9191                matches!(backend, Backend::Ptrace | Backend::E9patch | Backend::Sabre),
9192            "provides_process_signal_control": kvm,
9193            "emulates_child_waits": kvm,
9194            // A Config field Hermit set from the backend's name before it was
9195            // a stated capability. e9patch runs on ptrace and has its value.
9196            "supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption":
9197                matches!(backend, Backend::Ptrace | Backend::E9patch),
9198            // Readings of the field above until A5 step 3c.0 split them out,
9199            // with its value on every backend.
9200            "kernel_signal_state_is_guests": matches!(backend, Backend::Ptrace | Backend::E9patch),
9201            "kernel_signal_targets_are_predictable":
9202                matches!(backend, Backend::Ptrace | Backend::E9patch),
9203            "host_task_reads_reach_guest_threads":
9204                matches!(backend, Backend::Ptrace | Backend::E9patch),
9205            "host_timed_signals_are_physical":
9206                matches!(backend, Backend::Ptrace | Backend::E9patch),
9207            "delivers_preemption_timer_events":
9208                matches!(backend, Backend::Ptrace | Backend::E9patch),
9209            "runs_guest_code_between_injections": sabre || in_guest_liteinst,
9210            "promotes_open_files_before_native_lifecycle": dbt || in_guest_liteinst,
9211            // Hermit runs e9patch preprocessing as a ptrace run (empty
9212            // trampolines keep the original syscall instruction), whose
9213            // rt_sigreturns reach the seccomp stop that reports them.
9214            "reports_sigreturns": matches!(backend, Backend::Ptrace | Backend::E9patch),
9215        })
9216    }

9272                super::backend_capabilities(Backend::Dbt),

9278                super::backend_capabilities(Backend::Dbt),

9284    /// `Config` with its three environment-backed fields (`HERMIT_EPOCH`,
9285    /// `HERMIT_PRNG`, `HERMIT_SCHED_SEED`) pinned, so the encoding does not
9286    /// depend on the test process's environment.
9287    fn env_free_detconfig(epoch: &str, seed: &str) -> DetConfig {
9288        use clap::Parser;
9289        let mut config = DetConfig::parse_from(["hermit", epoch, seed, "--sched-seed=0"]);
9290        config.sched_seed = None;
9291        config
9292    }
9293
9294    /// Non-default values in fields that serialize as strings, floats,
9295    /// options and nested arrays. The path contains legacy key names, so an
9296    /// encoder that edited text would put a key inside a string value.
9297    fn rich_detconfig() -> DetConfig {
9298        let mut config = env_free_detconfig("--epoch=2000-12-31T23:59:59Z", "--seed=7");
9299        config.rng_seed = Some(13);
9300        config.sched_seed = Some(11);
9301        config.clock_multiplier = Some(1.5);
9302        config.chaos = true;
9303        config.record_preemptions_to = Some(std::path::PathBuf::from(
9304            "/tmp/a,\"detect_host_clock_futex_timeouts\":true,\"backend_tracks_process_children\":{",
9305        ));
9306        config.mountinfo_root_rewrites = vec![detcore_model::config::MountInfoRootRewrite {
9307            raw_mount_id: 41,
9308            deterministic_root: b"/".to_vec(),
9309            raw_root_prefix: Some(b"/tmp/x".to_vec()),
9310            deterministic_root_prefix: Some(b"/tmp".to_vec()),
9311            raw_mountpoint_prefix: None,
9312            deterministic_mountpoint_prefix: None,
9313        }];
9314        config.stacktrace_event = vec![(3, Some(std::path::PathBuf::from("/s")))];
9315        config
9316    }
9317
9318    /// `HERMIT_DBT_DETCONFIG` is in the guest's environment, so a guest can
9319    /// read it with `getenv` or `/proc/self/environ`. These fixtures are the
9320    /// output of `serde_json::to_string` on the same configs, captured from a
9321    /// build of the commit before Detcore read [`reverie::BackendCapabilities`],
9322    /// when `Config` still had one boolean field per backend switch. They are
9323    /// the variable's bytes before `dbt_detconfig_json` re-inserts the three
9324    /// deleted switches' keys; `dbt_detconfig_matches_806cf2fa_bytes` pins the
9325    /// complete variable. Every DBT run sequentializes threads, so the DBT
9326    /// cases do too. The fixtures carry one deliberate later change, the
9327    /// `fdinfo_unlisted_mount_ids` -> `mount_id_assignment_order` key rename
9328    /// described on `dbt_detconfig_tests::GOLDEN`. Preserve the historical DBT
9329    /// descriptor capabilities here as well as the historical bytes. Current
9330    /// DBT's independent descriptor facts require the typed envelope, whose
9331    /// exact round trip and all sixteen coupled-flag combinations are checked
9332    /// by `dbt_detconfig_tests`.
9333    #[test]
9334    fn historical_dbt_capabilities_preserve_legacy_detconfig_bytes() {
9335        let sequential = |mut config: DetConfig| {
9336            config.sequentialize_threads = true;
9337            config
9338        };
9339        let default_config = || env_free_detconfig("--epoch=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", "--seed=0");
9340        for (name, mut config, before) in [
9341            (
9342                "default",
9343                default_config(),
9344                include_str!("../tests/fixtures/dbt/detconfig-before-capabilities-default.json"),
9345            ),
9346            (
9347                "dbt",
9348                prepare_backend_config(sequential(default_config()), Backend::Dbt),
9349                include_str!("../tests/fixtures/dbt/detconfig-before-capabilities-dbt.json"),
9350            ),
9351            (
9352                "rich_dbt",
9353                prepare_backend_config(sequential(rich_detconfig()), Backend::Dbt),
9354                include_str!("../tests/fixtures/dbt/detconfig-before-capabilities-rich_dbt.json"),
9355            ),
9356        ] {
9357            config.backend.tool_shares_guest_descriptor_table = false;
9358            config.backend.rediscovers_descriptors_after_exec = false;
9359            // Read back as false, as the `Config` fields they replace were.
9360            config.backend.supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption = false;
9361            config.backend.delivers_preemption_timer_events = false;
9362            config.backend.runs_guest_code_between_injections = false;
9363            assert_eq!(
9364                detcore::to_legacy_backend_json(&config).unwrap(),
9365                before,
9366                "HERMIT_DBT_DETCONFIG for the {name} config changed"
9367            );
9368            // A reader of the earlier bytes recovers the capabilities.
9369            let decoded = detcore::from_legacy_backend_json(before).unwrap();
9370            assert_eq!(decoded.backend, config.backend, "{name}");
9371            assert_eq!(
9372                decoded.sequentialize_threads, config.sequentialize_threads,
9373                "{name}"
9374            );
9375            assert_eq!(
9376                detcore::to_legacy_backend_json(&decoded).unwrap(),
9377                before,
9378                "{name}"
9379            );
9380        }
9381    }
9382
9383    /// The fifteen per-backend keys, in the order the encoding has always
9384    /// carried them.
9385    const LEGACY_BACKEND_KEYS: [&str; 15] = [
9386        "cpuid_virtualized_by_backend",
9387        "backend_supports_madvise",
9388        "discover_live_file_metadata",
9389        "detect_host_clock_futex_timeouts",
9390        "syscall_clobbers_virtualized_by_backend",
9391        "cancel_killed_thread_rpcs",
9392        "backend_reports_physical_process_exits",
9393        "backend_tracks_process_children",
9394        "backend_runs_exit_robust_list",
9395        "backend_requires_thread_directed_process_signals",
9396        "backend_is_kvm",
9397        "kvm_shared_dequeue_timers",
9398        "backend_supports_parked_write_signal_interruption",
9399        "backend_virtualizes_capability_prctls",
9400        "backend_defers_vfork_child_registration",
9401    ];
9402
9403    /// Pin the current projection onto all fifteen legacy backend keys, once
9404    /// without and once with sequentialized threads. DBT's two descriptor
9405    /// facts project to `discover_live_file_metadata=true`; that legacy bit
9406    /// cannot retain their independence from the host-timed capabilities.
9407    /// Current DBT therefore uses the separately checked typed envelope, not
9408    /// this lossy projection. LiteInst's row is its in-guest runtime. KVM's
9409    /// first two digits are the capabilities `run_kvm` formerly set itself; the
9410    /// first, `cpuid_virtualized_by_backend`, is written false for every
9411    /// backend now that no backend installs a CPUID profile of its own, and so
9412    /// is the fourteenth, `backend_virtualizes_capability_prctls`, now that
9413    /// the capability prctls reach the kernel on every backend. KVM's fifth,
9414    /// `syscall_clobbers_virtualized_by_backend`, is set since Reverie's
9415    /// per-call slice 6 declared `virtualizes_syscall_clobbers`.
9416    #[test]
9417    fn every_backend_encodes_its_current_legacy_projection() {
9418        for (backend, unsequenced, sequential) in [
9419            (Backend::Ptrace, "010000011000100", "010000011000100"),
9420            (Backend::E9patch, "010000011000100", "010000011000100"),
9421            (Backend::Liteinst, "010001010000000", "010001010000000"),
9422            (Backend::InGuestTrap, "010001010000000", "010001010000000"),
9423            (Backend::Sabre, "011111110000000", "011111110000000"),
9424            (Backend::Dbt, "011001000100000", "011001000100000"),
9425            (Backend::Kvm, "000011010010101", "000011010011101"),
9426        ] {
9427            for (sequentialize_threads, expected) in [(false, unsequenced), (true, sequential)] {
9428                let config = prepare_backend_config(
9429                    DetConfig {
9430                        sequentialize_threads,
9431                        ..DetConfig::default()
9432                    },
9433                    backend,
9434                );
9435                let encoded: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> =
9436                    serde_json::from_str(&detcore::to_legacy_backend_json(&config).unwrap())
9437                        .unwrap();
9438                let digits: String = LEGACY_BACKEND_KEYS
9439                    .iter()
9440                    .map(|key| match encoded.get(*key) {
9441                        Some(serde_json::Value::Bool(true)) => '1',
9442                        Some(serde_json::Value::Bool(false)) => '0',
9443                        other => panic!("{key} encoded as {other:?}"),
9444                    })
9445                    .collect();
9446                assert_eq!(
9447                    digits, expected,
9448                    "{backend:?}, sequentialize_threads={sequentialize_threads}"
9449                );
9450            }
9451        }
9452    }

9545    /// A launch may pass the guest a terminal when a standard descriptor is
9546    /// one, when the launcher has a controlling terminal, or when that cannot
9547    /// be read; only a launch with neither is known not to. The device number
9548    /// is read past a command name that holds spaces and parentheses.
9549    #[test]
9550    fn a_launch_may_pass_a_terminal_unless_it_proves_it_has_none() {
9551        assert!(!super::may_pass_a_terminal(false, Some(0)));
9552        assert!(super::may_pass_a_terminal(true, Some(0)));
9553        assert!(super::may_pass_a_terminal(false, Some(34817)));
9554        assert!(super::may_pass_a_terminal(false, None));
9555
9556        let stat = "4242 (a) b (c)) S 1 4242 4242 34817 4242 4194560 0 0 0 0";
9557        assert_eq!(super::parse_controlling_terminal_device(stat), Some(34817));
9558        let stat = "4242 (hermit) S 1 4242 4242 0 -1 4194560 0 0 0 0";
9559        assert_eq!(super::parse_controlling_terminal_device(stat), Some(0));
9560        assert_eq!(
9561            super::parse_controlling_terminal_device("4242 (hermit"),
9562            None
9563        );
9564        assert_eq!(
9565            super::parse_controlling_terminal_device("4242 (hermit) S 1"),
9566            None
9567        );
9568        assert!(super::controlling_terminal_device().is_some());
9569    }

9597    fn liteinst_public_dispatch_runs_in_guest_detcore() {
9598        if Backend::Liteinst.ensure_available().is_err() {
9599            return;
9600        }
9601
9602        // In-guest LiteInst has no preemption timer and refuses a maximum
9603        // timeslice, so this run disables preemption; preemption is not what
9604        // this test checks.
9605        let config = super::DetConfig {
9606            max_timeslice: None,
9607            ..super::DetConfig::default()
9608        };
9609        let mut command = super::Command::new("/bin/echo");
9610        command.arg("hello");
9611        let output = super::run_with_output_backend(
9612            command,
9613            config.clone(),
9614            false,
9615            &None,
9616            Backend::Liteinst,
9617        )
9618        .expect("run /bin/echo through in-guest LiteInst");
9619        // Include captured output so a failed backend launch reports its diagnostics.
9620        assert_eq!(
9621            output.status,
9622            super::ExitStatus::Exited(0),
9623            "guest did not exit 0.\n--- guest stderr ---\n{}\n--- guest stdout ---\n{}",
9624            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr),
9625            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
9626        );
9627        assert_eq!(output.stdout, b"hello\n");
9628
9629        let status = super::run_with_backend(
9630            super::Command::new("/bin/true"),
9631            config,
9632            false,
9633            &None,
9634            Backend::Liteinst,
9635        )
9636        .expect("run /bin/true through in-guest LiteInst");
9637        assert_eq!(status, super::ExitStatus::Exited(0));
9638    }

9958    #[test]
9959    #[cfg(feature = "dbt")]
9960    fn dbt_public_dispatch_runs_echo_through_detcore() {
9961        use clap::Parser;
9962
9963        if Backend::Dbt.ensure_available().is_err() {
9964            return;
9965        }
9966
9967        // Isolate the controller's fd 2 in a subprocess, without redirecting a
9968        // descriptor shared by other tests in this process.
9969        const CHILD: &str = "HERMIT_TEST_DBT_LIBRARY_DIAGNOSTICS_CHILD";
9970        if std::env::var_os(CHILD).is_none() {
9971            let output = std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
9972                .args([
9973                    "--exact",
9974                    "tests::dbt_public_dispatch_runs_echo_through_detcore",
9975                    "--nocapture",
9976                ])
9977                .env(CHILD, "1")
9978                .output()
9979                .expect("run isolated DBT library output checks");
9980            let diagnostics = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
9981            assert!(output.status.success(), "{output:?}");
9982            assert!(
9983                diagnostics
9984                    .lines()
9985                    .filter(|line| line.starts_with("reverie-dbt: tool=Detcore "))
9986                    .count()
9987                    >= 2,
9988                "DBT native summaries did not prove both Detcore dispatches: {diagnostics}"
9989            );
9990            assert!(!diagnostics.contains("guest-stderr"), "{diagnostics}");
9991            return;
9992        }
9993
9994        let mut command = super::Command::new("/bin/echo");
9995        command.arg("hello");
9996        let mut config = super::DetConfig::parse_from(["hermit-dbt-test"]);
9997        config.sequentialize_threads = true;
9998        config.validate();
9999        let output = super::run_with_output_backend(command, config, true, &None, Backend::Dbt)
10000            .expect("run /bin/echo through DbtGuest<Detcore>");
10001
10002        // Include captured output so a failed backend launch reports its diagnostics.
10003        assert_eq!(
10004            output.status,
10005            super::ExitStatus::Exited(0),
10006            "guest did not exit 0.\n--- guest stderr ---\n{}\n--- guest stdout ---\n{}",
10007            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr),
10008            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
10009        );
10010        assert_eq!(output.stdout, b"hello\n");
10011        assert_eq!(output.stderr, b"");
10012
10013        let mut command = super::Command::new("/bin/sh");
10014        command.args(["-c", "printf 'guest-stderr\\n' >&2"]);
10015        let mut config = super::DetConfig::parse_from(["hermit-dbt-test"]);
10016        config.sequentialize_threads = true;
10017        config.validate();
10018        let output = super::run_with_output_backend(command, config, true, &None, Backend::Dbt)
10019            .expect("capture nonempty guest stderr through DbtGuest<Detcore>");
10020        assert_eq!(output.status, super::ExitStatus::Exited(0), "{output:?}");
10021        assert_eq!(output.stdout, b"");
10022        assert_eq!(output.stderr, b"guest-stderr\n");
10023    }

10071    // Keep the low-level vmcall transport covered independently from the ELF
10072    // process personality. Requires /dev/kvm; skips cleanly otherwise.
10073    #[test]
10074    fn detcore_drives_kvm_guest_for_synthetic_syscall() {
10075        use clap::Parser;
10076
10077        const MEMORY_SIZE: usize = 0x10_000;
10078        const ENTRY_POINT: u64 = 0x1000;
10079        const FRAME_ADDRESS: u64 = 0x2000;
10080
10081        let mut backend = match reverie_kvm::KvmBackend::new(MEMORY_SIZE) {
10082            Ok(backend) => backend,
10083            Err(error) => {
10084                eprintln!("skipping KVM Detcore experiment: cannot init VM: {error}");
10085                return;
10086            }
10087        };
10088
10089        // A guest that issues one `getpid` through the vmcall transport, then HLTs.
10090        backend
10091            .install_syscall(
10092                ENTRY_POINT,
10093                FRAME_ADDRESS,
10094                reverie_kvm::SyscallRequest::new(libc::SYS_getpid as u64, [0; 6]),
10095            )
10096            .expect("install synthetic getpid guest");
10097
10098        // Minimal deterministic Detcore config with RCB preemption disabled.
10099        let mut config =
10100            super::DetConfig::parse_from(["hermit-kvm-test", "--max-timeslice=disabled"]);
10101        config.validate();
10102
10103        let runtime = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
10104            .enable_all()
10105            .build()
10106            .expect("build tokio runtime");
10107
10108        let outcome = runtime.block_on(async {
10109            backend
10110                .run_with_tool::<super::Detcore, _>(
10111                    config,
10112                    // Executor: forward anything Detcore injects to the host.
10113                    |request: &reverie_kvm::SyscallRequest, _memory: &reverie_kvm::GuestMemory| {
10114                        // SAFETY: forwarding a register-only syscall (getpid) to the
10115                        // host; no guest pointers are dereferenced by the kernel.
10116                        unsafe {
10117                            libc::syscall(
10118                                request.number() as libc::c_long,
10119                                request.args()[0],
10120                                request.args()[1],
10121                                request.args()[2],
10122                                request.args()[3],
10123                                request.args()[4],
10124                                request.args()[5],
10125                            ) as i64
10126                        }
10127                    },
10128                )
10129                .await
10130        });
10131
10132        // The point of the experiment is to observe whether Detcore can be driven
10133        // to completion over KvmGuest at all; assert it did not error.
10134        outcome.expect("Detcore drove the synthetic KVM guest to completion");
10135    }

10137    // Minimal fake ELF payload: the loader only needs the image to NOT start
10138    // with `#!`, and a real ELF magic makes the intent obvious.
10139    const FAKE_ELF: &[u8] = b"\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01\x00 fake elf body";
10140
10141    fn shebang_tmpdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
10142        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
10143            "hermit-shebang-test-{}-{}",
10144            std::process::id(),
10145            tag
10146        ));
10147        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
10148        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
10149        dir
10150    }
10151
10152    #[test]
10153    fn resolve_shebang_plain_elf_is_unchanged() {
10154        let dir = shebang_tmpdir("plain");
10155        let prog = dir.join("prog");
10156        fs::write(&prog, FAKE_ELF).unwrap();
10157
10158        let argv = vec!["prog".to_owned(), "-a".to_owned()];
10159        let (path, out_argv, image) = resolve_kvm_shebang(&prog, argv).unwrap();
10160        assert_eq!(path, prog);
10161        assert_eq!(out_argv, vec!["prog".to_owned(), "-a".to_owned()]);
10162        assert_eq!(image, FAKE_ELF);
10163        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
10164    }
